item.title: The Lego Star Trek bridge diorama set should be your gateway to finally watching the Original Series
item.description: null It's not quite a five-year mission, but as Star Trek celebrated its 60th anniversary in September of this year (we may have mentioned it once or twice), I decided it was high time I finally watched the original Star Trek . Before this year, I hadn't seen a single episode of "Star Trek: The Original Series", as it's now known. I'm a millennial; I grew up on "The Next Generation", "Deep Space Nine" and "Voyager". By comparison, the old series (TOS) always looked so… old and naff whenever I saw clips of it. But now I have seen the original series. Over the course of 2026, I've ploughed through all 79 episodes, spread across three seasons. And you know what? It's pretty damn good. Even with the shiny 2006 remasters, you'll have to prepare yourself for some bad special effects work, but the scripts are interesting, the sci-fi concepts are out there, and the acting — especially from Shatner and Nimoy — is top-notch. And just as I finally discovered a love for this classic sci-fi series, what should drop into my lap? Why it's the new Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge diorama set from Lego. Now I have more on my wishlist to add to the Best lego space sets. Boldly building where no one has built before Building the Lego Star Trek: Bridge diorama. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Let's start with the Band-Aid rip: this set is $200. I know; it stings, especially when Star Trek promised us a future where money doesn't exist. But at 1701 pieces (nice, I see what you did there), it's much better value from a bricks-per-dollar perspective than the X-Files set we checked out recently. Still, that's no small investment for a toy, even if it will make a lovely display piece when it's built. As the name suggests, you get a full Lego-ified recreation of the bridge of the USS Enterprise (NCC-1701, no A, B, C, or D). This includes Captain Kirk's chair, the helm positions ahead of him (manned by Chekov and Sulu), and all of the surrounding computer displays where you usually find Spock, Uhura and Scotty. There's even a viewscreen that can sit in front of the crew, displaying an adorable Klingon commander facing off against Kirk. The minifigure bridge crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise (L-R): Nurse Chapel, Chekov, Scotty, Spock, Kirk, McCoy, Uhura and Sulu. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Star Trek: U.S.S. item.dc:creator: Ian Stokes
item.content:encoded: null It's not quite a five-year mission, but as Star Trek celebrated its 60th anniversary in September of this year (we may have mentioned it once or twice), I decided it was high time I finally watched the original Star Trek . Before this year, I hadn't seen a single episode of "Star Trek: The Original Series", as it's now known. I'm a millennial; I grew up on "The Next Generation", "Deep Space Nine" and "Voyager". By comparison, the old series (TOS) always looked so… old and naff whenever I saw clips of it. But now I have seen the original series. Over the course of 2026, I've ploughed through all 79 episodes, spread across three seasons. And you know what? It's pretty damn good. Even with the shiny 2006 remasters, you'll have to prepare yourself for some bad special effects work, but the scripts are interesting, the sci-fi concepts are out there, and the acting — especially from Shatner and Nimoy — is top-notch. And just as I finally discovered a love for this classic sci-fi series, what should drop into my lap? Why it's the new Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge diorama set from Lego. Now I have more on my wishlist to add to the Best lego space sets. Boldly building where no one has built before Building the Lego Star Trek: Bridge diorama. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Let's start with the Band-Aid rip: this set is $200. I know; it stings, especially when Star Trek promised us a future where money doesn't exist. But at 1701 pieces (nice, I see what you did there), it's much better value from a bricks-per-dollar perspective than the X-Files set we checked out recently. Still, that's no small investment for a toy, even if it will make a lovely display piece when it's built. As the name suggests, you get a full Lego-ified recreation of the bridge of the USS Enterprise (NCC-1701, no A, B, C, or D). This includes Captain Kirk's chair, the helm positions ahead of him (manned by Chekov and Sulu), and all of the surrounding computer displays where you usually find Spock, Uhura and Scotty. There's even a viewscreen that can sit in front of the crew, displaying an adorable Klingon commander facing off against Kirk. The minifigure bridge crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise (L-R): Nurse Chapel, Chekov, Scotty, Spock, Kirk, McCoy, Uhura and Sulu. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge: $199.99 Board the legendary starship and meet the crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 for an amazing building experience. Recreate the iconic bridge and transporter room that served as the backdrop for epic scenes from "Star Trek: The Original Series". View Deal Alongside the main bridge, there are a few fun extras bolted on, including a rotating transporter pad (which can make minifigures "disappear") and a working turbolift door connected to the back of the main bridge diorama. You'll have to make the swoosh sound effect yourself, though. It's a wonderfully faithful recreation of Kirk's command center, complete with computer panels and screens, swiveling chairs and that weird scope thing that Spock was always looking into. That said, it's a little lacking in proper Easter eggs. There are some tribbles hiding around the build, and the monitors have custom stickers showing cool Trekkie things. The weapon display racks on the back hold an array of pointy Klingon blades, Starfleet phasers, Sulu's fencing rapier and even Spock's harp, but compared to, say, the X-Files set we built recently, it feels a bit lacking in those deep-cut references. Helping Star Trek live long and prosper The complete Lego Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge diorama (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) All in all, it's a fantastic little diorama, but when it was announced, I'll admit I was a little puzzled as to who it was aimed at. "Star Trek fans, duh!" is the obvious response, but the Venn diagram crossover between "people who are nostalgic for the original series of Star Trek" and "people who want to buy $200 Lego sets" has to be pretty small, right? Star Trek first aired way back in 1966, which means the first generation of fans are now 70 years old and upwards. Lord knows I hope I'm still building Lego sets when I'm 70, but is that a large enough crowd to make this set a success? Then again the show was repeated and syndicated throughout the 70s and 80s, which means hopefully there'll be some younger buyers, too. The playset aspects of the set are even more puzzling. The working door, exploding monitor and spinning transporter pad are great additions to a kids' playset, but this isn't that — it's a display for nostalgic Star Trek fans. The design of the set just feels a bit confused. Scotty minifigure on the transporter pad. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) But then it hit me. Maybe this isn't just for fans of the original series; maybe it's meant to create some new fans. I started watching the original Star Trek 60 years after its debut because… well, I'm the sci-fi editor for a space website, and it felt wrong that I hadn't seen it. But most people don't have that sort of professional impetus. The average person won't jump back to watch a 60-year-old TV show without a polite nudge, and this set does a great job of highlighting the charm and optimism of Star Trek's debut outing. I don't know, maybe I'm just projecting here. Maybe Lego bought the rights to make Star Trek sets and needed something to do after they'd mined all the nostalgia they could from the excellent Enterprise D set they released in 2025. Maybe this is just a toy for big kids. Or maybe… just maybe, it's meant to inspire the next generation of Star Trek fans to check out where the magic started. Disclaimer: We were sent a copy of the Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge set by Lego.

item.title: Tesla will sell you a Cybercab for $30,000. Then charge $299 a month to use it
item.description: There is always a catch. Or in the case of Tesla ’s self-driving Cybercab , several. Last Friday night, Tesla said it had invited “select customers” to purchase their very own Cybercabs. The two-seat, gold vehicle is unlike any other on the market: It lacks a steering wheel and brake pedals, and is primarily driven by software. (Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Alphabet's Waymo and Amazon’s Zoox , offer self-driving rides on ride-hail networks , but don’t let people buy their cars.) Tesla’s " limited release ” will supposedly offer some people (unclear how many) the opportunity to pay $29,900 to take delivery in December. From there, though, the Cybercab will need constant cash infusions to stay on the road. Read full article Comments

item.title: Ridley Scott's Sci-Fi Masterpiece Could Return to Theaters in a Shocking Way, Producers Reveal
item.description: Blade Runner, Ridley Scott’s 1982 adaptation of Philip K. Dick’s 1968 novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? , is one of the best and most influential sci-fi films of all time, but it took 35 years for it to get a direct sequel. Producers Broderick Johnson and Andrew Kosove acquired the rights to the franchise in 2011 through their production company, Alcon, and used them to develop Denis Villeneuve’s Blade Runner 2049 , which is set 30 years after the events of Scott’s film. Now, the timeline is moving forward again in Blade Runner 2099 , which premieres on Prime Video on Nov. 25, and the producers are already thinking about what’s next for the cyberpunk series after that.

item.title: How The Verge is picking which Black Friday deals to share
item.description: For the past month, we’ve been inundated with Black Friday deals, signaling what’s to come on the biggest shopping day of the year in the US. We routinely get dozens of press releases a day, coming from brands big and small that hope that we’ll publicize these offers. Of course, the companies would prefer that we don’t do any research on these deals to see if they’re actually good, and most don’t provide any of the necessary context we’re looking for when vetting them. Most indicators of a good deal are confusing — not just for us, but for anyone who’s shopping. Groundwork Collaborative recently published its findings about the unclear manner in which Amazon displays deals. Its researchers tracked a selection of products ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday in 2024 and 2025, and they claim that nearly one in three products advertised as deals on Amazon didn’t offer savings during the actual shopping events. The investigation also found that nearly a tenth of the deals it examined were more expensive during the sales events than on some days in the month leading up to them. Something we commonly see on Amazon and attempt to correct for in our coverage are good deals with inflated discount claims. As in, the original retail amount (the “list” price) is sometimes higher than the usual day-to-day price to make the savings seem more substantial. Sometimes, the manufacturer’s suggested retail price (MSRP) is what’s shown, though that’s not always the case. In a recent statement to investigative journalist Ronan Farrow , an unattributed Amazon spokesperson shared that its “List Price” can also be aggregated from the past 90 to 180 days of prices, not the past 30 days as Groundwork Collaborative’s research states, and is based on prices from Amazon itself and other competing retailers. However, in our experience, the confusing way pricing and discounts are communicated isn’t limited to Amazon. View this post on Instagram The group’s findings show how easy it is to distrust the prices you see, especially online, where dynamic pricing sometimes comes into play. Regardless of retailer practices, we understand the importance of curating what you see on The Verge with care. Vetting deals for coverage consideration is a big, albeit invisible, part of our jobs, even outside of big shopping events. Most of what we’re pitched day to day, or what we see in our respective feeds, never hits the site because it doesn’t meet our standards. Even when the deal is for a product we’ve tested and really enjoy — our north star for what to cover on the deals front — that alone doesn’t guarantee coverage. We often skip covering deals that aren’t as good as a retailer or brand made them seem. Or maybe the deal is good, but it returns every week, lasts only a few hours, or it’s available only with a premium membership. item.dc:creator: Cameron Faulkner
item.content:encoded: For the past month, we’ve been inundated with Black Friday deals, signaling what’s to come on the biggest shopping day of the year in the US. We routinely get dozens of press releases a day, coming from brands big and small that hope that we’ll publicize these offers. Of course, the companies would prefer that we don’t do any research on these deals to see if they’re actually good, and most don’t provide any of the necessary context we’re looking for when vetting them. Most indicators of a good deal are confusing — not just for us, but for anyone who’s shopping. Groundwork Collaborative recently published its findings about the unclear manner in which Amazon displays deals. Its researchers tracked a selection of products ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday in 2024 and 2025, and they claim that nearly one in three products advertised as deals on Amazon didn’t offer savings during the actual shopping events. The investigation also found that nearly a tenth of the deals it examined were more expensive during the sales events than on some days in the month leading up to them. Something we commonly see on Amazon and attempt to correct for in our coverage are good deals with inflated discount claims. As in, the original retail amount (the “list” price) is sometimes higher than the usual day-to-day price to make the savings seem more substantial. Sometimes, the manufacturer’s suggested retail price (MSRP) is what’s shown, though that’s not always the case. In a recent statement to investigative journalist Ronan Farrow , an unattributed Amazon spokesperson shared that its “List Price” can also be aggregated from the past 90 to 180 days of prices, not the past 30 days as Groundwork Collaborative’s research states, and is based on prices from Amazon itself and other competing retailers. However, in our experience, the confusing way pricing and discounts are communicated isn’t limited to Amazon. View this post on Instagram The group’s findings show how easy it is to distrust the prices you see, especially online, where dynamic pricing sometimes comes into play. Regardless of retailer practices, we understand the importance of curating what you see on The Verge with care. Vetting deals for coverage consideration is a big, albeit invisible, part of our jobs, even outside of big shopping events. Most of what we’re pitched day to day, or what we see in our respective feeds, never hits the site because it doesn’t meet our standards. Even when the deal is for a product we’ve tested and really enjoy — our north star for what to cover on the deals front — that alone doesn’t guarantee coverage. We often skip covering deals that aren’t as good as a retailer or brand made them seem. Or maybe the deal is good, but it returns every week, lasts only a few hours, or it’s available only with a premium membership. Alternatively, the deal might only be available from a retailer none of us has heard of or shopped at. Needless to say, we consider a ton of factors. With Black Friday coming up, you deserve transparency from us so you know — whether it’s this month or a random day in February — that you’re looking at an actual deal when you visit our site. The most basic criteria we use to judge whether a deal is good is whether we like the product enough to write about it and whether its price has dropped. Then we assess whether the discount is actually worth your attention. That part of the conversation has become a little complicated in the past year. RAMageddon and the ripple effects of higher tariffs have, in some cases, substantially impacted pricing and, by extension, the deals we cover. We follow deals closely enough to know when to bite at an offer or let it pass For products hit by recent price hikes, the new deal prices sometimes amount to the original sticker price, or close to it. Several of us would nod our heads with you if you think, “Hey, that’s not a deal; that’s just the original price. I’m no fool!” But it’s also technically a deal for many of us who are just trying to save wherever possible. Along those lines, we’ll sometimes highlight ways to save on digital or physical goods by buying discounted gift cards, which can be used to buy in-demand products. These methods are the only way to get any kind of deal on Grand Theft Auto VI before launch, for example. To help us stay aware of price drops, we also use free tracking tools like CamelCamelCamel and Keepa, which provide an independent read on Amazon’s historical pricing. ( You can use them, too! ) They’ll alert us when a product we like — and that we know you’ll probably like — goes on sale. Amazon also has its own Alexa for Shopping tool , which can show up to a year of pricing data and perform several other AI chatbot-like actions, including automatically buying products on your behalf. In my experience, Amazon’s historical pricing data usually aligns with non-Amazon-affiliated companies. However, none of them are perfect. Even the third-party tools we use don’t always display the record-low prices we’ve covered, for whatever reason. All of this to say, there are a lot of ins and outs, but we follow deals closely enough to know when to bite at an offer or let it pass. We cast a fairly large net for products across a range of categories ahead of the holidays, including some that don’t often get much play on The Verge . However, of the thousands of deals that we’ve seen ahead of Black Friday, you’re seeing the mere dozens of standouts that we’ve tested or used in our personal lives within each category — headphones, TVs, gaming accessories, smart home tech, etc. — that meet our criteria for being good products at noteworthy prices.

item.title: Will Wright’s next game uses AI to map your memories
item.description: Will Wright, the creator of legendary franchises like SimCity and The Sims , is working on a new game - and it's built around AI. The new title, focused on your memories, is called MyMems . Like Wright's other titles, it sounds extremely ambitious, giving players a new way to explore worlds they create on their own. "We want to take your autobiography and turn it into a toy world," he tells The Verge . The MyMems website describes the mobile game as a "social simulation" with worlds "built from your memories and the people who shaped you." You can add "memories" to your game, like speaking a short story to your phone, and those memories are ge … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Tinubu’s tough reforms will ensure lasting prosperity for Nigeria – Wike
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, has urged market traders in Abuja to rally behind President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 for lasting prosperity. Wike, who made the call during a town hall with various market associations across the nation’s capital in Abuja on Wednesday, stressed that Tinubu administration’s economic reforms were laying the foundation for long-term national growth and stability. He acknowledged the economic difficulties triggered by the removal of the fuel subsidy but maintained that previous administrations lacked the courage to confront what he described as a systemic scam. “This country is nearly gone. For you to say that you must try to change what is happening means that you must lay a foundation first, and when you lay a foundation, you give it time to grow. “There is no government that has not identified that this oil subsidy is a scam, why university teachers cannot work, no payment of salaries, no payment of pensioners. “Everybody is afraid; they lack courage. If you don’t have good leaders who have courage to take decisions, that country will not grow,” he added. According to the minister, the temporary sacrifices necessitated by the subsidy removal have yielded tangible benefits nationwide. “This includes increased revenue allocations to states and local governments, clearance of pension backlogs, and an end to recurring strikes by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU).” Wike cautioned Nigerians against politicians promising to reverse the subsidy removal, arguing that such rhetoric was deceptive and would set the country backwards. “If we allow these policies that the government has put in place to mature, what is going to happen in the next four years will be good. Forget about people coming to tell you stories,” he said. Highlighting his administration’s achievements in Abuja since assuming office in August 2023, Wike pointed to ongoing and completed road infrastructure projects in satellite towns and districts, noting that good road networks were critical for reducing transportation costs and boosting commerce. He pledged to grant approval for the further development of markets in the territory and promised to hold regular interactive sessions with traders at least once every six months. Beyond physical infrastructure, the minister underscored institutional reforms approved by Tinubu for the FCT, noting that for the first time since the territory’s creation in 1976, an indigene was appointed to the Federal Executive Council. He also cited the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, which allows career civil servants to rise to the rank of Permanent Secretary and Head of Service, and the creation of Mandate Secretariats for Women and Youth. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, has urged market traders in Abuja to rally behind President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 for lasting prosperity. Wike, who made the call during a town hall with various market associations across the nation’s capital in Abuja on Wednesday, stressed that Tinubu administration’s economic reforms were laying the foundation for long-term national growth and stability. He acknowledged the economic difficulties triggered by the removal of the fuel subsidy but maintained that previous administrations lacked the courage to confront what he described as a systemic scam. “This country is nearly gone. For you to say that you must try to change what is happening means that you must lay a foundation first, and when you lay a foundation, you give it time to grow. “There is no government that has not identified that this oil subsidy is a scam, why university teachers cannot work, no payment of salaries, no payment of pensioners. “Everybody is afraid; they lack courage. If you don’t have good leaders who have courage to take decisions, that country will not grow,” he added. According to the minister, the temporary sacrifices necessitated by the subsidy removal have yielded tangible benefits nationwide. “This includes increased revenue allocations to states and local governments, clearance of pension backlogs, and an end to recurring strikes by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU).” Wike cautioned Nigerians against politicians promising to reverse the subsidy removal, arguing that such rhetoric was deceptive and would set the country backwards. “If we allow these policies that the government has put in place to mature, what is going to happen in the next four years will be good. Forget about people coming to tell you stories,” he said. Highlighting his administration’s achievements in Abuja since assuming office in August 2023, Wike pointed to ongoing and completed road infrastructure projects in satellite towns and districts, noting that good road networks were critical for reducing transportation costs and boosting commerce. He pledged to grant approval for the further development of markets in the territory and promised to hold regular interactive sessions with traders at least once every six months. Beyond physical infrastructure, the minister underscored institutional reforms approved by Tinubu for the FCT, noting that for the first time since the territory’s creation in 1976, an indigene was appointed to the Federal Executive Council. He also cited the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, which allows career civil servants to rise to the rank of Permanent Secretary and Head of Service, and the creation of Mandate Secretariats for Women and Youth. Dismissing ethnic and regional sentiments in governance, Wike urged the traders to judge leadership strictly by performance and tangible impact rather than tribal affiliation. “Governance has nothing to do with where I come from. It is not about Hausa, Yoruba, or Igbo; it is about, “If I do my business here, am I happy?” he stated. Wike also criticised opposition figures, faulting former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s handling of past privatisation exercises and questioning the track record of former Rivers Governor Rotimi Amaechi over uncompleted projects. Wike urged the market associations to participate in the upcoming campaign structure by nominating two representatives from each state chapter to join the campaign committee, assuring them of logistical support ahead of the 2027 general elections. Earlier, Amb. Maureen Tamuno, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Abuja Investments Company Ltd (AICL), described the interactive forum as a landmark engagement underscoring the minister’s commitment to people-orientated governance. Tamuno commended Wike for transforming both the city centre and satellite towns through road construction and rehabilitation, noting that projects such as the Saburi Road corridor had eased commercial movement. While urging traders to take full advantage of the dialogue to air their views constructively, the AICL boss reminded them that infrastructure development came with a shared responsibility to abide by market rules and regulations. Speaking on behalf of the traders, the Chairman of the Wuse Market Traders Association, Mr Okorie Ikechukwu-Raphael, lauded the transformation of internal market roads, shop redevelopments, and the opening up of area councils across the FCT. Ikechukwu-Raphael requested approval for AICL to develop new shops and malls in newly opened districts such as Katampe and Kaura to allow traders expand their businesses, as well as the green light to commence immediate cluster political mobilisation through trade unions, cooperatives, and community groups. Also, Chairman of the Arewa Traders Association, Alhaji Adamu Ibrahim, reaffirmed the readiness of northern traders to work for the electoral success of Tinubu and all allied candidates in the FCT in 2027. Highlighting the role of traders in job creation and revenue generation, Ibrahim urged the minister to grant market leaders a seat at the table when formulating market-related policies, while praising the AICL boss for proactive conflict resolution and regard for traders’ welfare. Adding her voice, the Chairperson of the National Assembly Quarters (Zone A) Market, Mrs Abiola Adekambi, who resided in Abuja for 26 years, described the pace of road construction, including the paving of roads around Sunnyvale, as unprecedented. Adekambi assured the minister of the loyalty of market women, vowing that they would vote in 2027 and remain at polling units to ensure their votes counted toward the re-election of President Tinubu. item.title: ‎CP Azare Charges Newly Promoted Officers On Discipline, Commitment To Duty
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Commissioner of Police, CP Baba Azare, has charged the newly promoted senior officers of the Command to live up to the demands of their new ranks and justify the confidence reposed in them. ‎CP Azare gave the charge when he decorated the officers with their new ranks at the Command headquarters, Ikot Akpanabia, Uyo, on Monday. ‎The newly promoted senior officers were decorated with new ranks following their recent promotion by the Police Service Commission. ‎The Police Commissioner, who congratulated the officers on what he acknowledged as their well-deserved promotions, described their elevation as recognition of their dedication, professionalism, hard work and commitment in the discharge of their duties. ‎“Promotion comes with higher responsibilities and more expectations. You are therefore charged to justify the confidence reposed in you through greater commitment to duty, professionalism, respect for human rights and strict adherence to the rule of law.” CP Azare advised. ‎The promoted senior officers comprise three Chief Superintendents of Police (CSPs) namely: CSP Richard Oguntola, CSP Magret Alapa, CSP Bokima Bassey, three Superintendents of Police (SPs) namely: SP John Mamodu, SP Glory George, SP Victor Lane and two Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSPs) namely: DSP Emmanuel Ayoka and DSP Godwin Awana. ‎CP Azare commended the Police Service Commission for the timely promotion of deserving officers, noting that such a gesture would further boost morale and inspire more commitment among officers. ‎The Commissioner also expressed gratitude to the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, for his visionary leadership, support and sustained commitment to the welfare of officers of the Nigeria Police Force. ‎CSP Richard Oguntola, responding on behalf of the newly promoted officers, expressed appreciation to the Almighty God for His mercy and grace to witness another memorable achievement. ‎He also expressed gratitude to the Police Service Commission and the Inspector-General of Police for finding them worthy for promotion. ‎CSP Oguntola particularly thanked CP Azare for his exemplary leadership, encouragement and support, which he stated had positively impacted their career progression. ‎He reiterated their commitment to the professional discharge of the constitutional duties of the Nigeria Police Force in their respective areas of responsibility in line with international best practices. ‎The decoration ceremony was attended by members of the management team, officers of the Command, families, friends and well-wishers who joined in celebrating the officers on their well-deserved promotions. ‎ ‎ The post ‎CP Azare Charges Newly Promoted Officers On Discipline, Commitment To Duty appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Business as usual, but Huang ain't coming back, says Nvidia
item.description: Nvidia's board says it has no plans to bring Jensen Huang back as the GPU giant reports quarterly revenue more than double that of a year ago. The AI infrastructure leviathan had some reassuring to do after its leather-jacketed rockstar leader left under a cloud last week. Huang had been central to its rise as the dominant supplier of AI compute. Newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones ruled out an imminent comeback, saying: "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Jones said the board was addressing the fallout and strengthening oversight, pointing to the creation of a committee to scrutinize the firm's security policies and export compliance. Nvidia has also retained the services of talent spotters Heidrick & Struggles to help find a new leader, according to Jones. Interim CEO and chief financial officer Colette Kress struck an upbeat tone on the company's Q3 earnings call. The results gave her plenty to work with : revenue rose 103 percent to $115.8 billion, while operating income climbed 115 percent to $77.5 billion. "We're addressing strong demand for compute across a diverse and expansive set of end customers, including hyperscalers, frontier labs, AI natives, enterprises, and governments," Kress said. She raised Nvidia's outlook for fiscal 2028, saying that the firm now expects revenue to grow approximately 75 percent year-on-year. Analysts immediately questioned this, asking what gave Kress the confidence to raise the outlook, given all the uncertainty surrounding the future direction of the company. Kress cited growing demand and additional supply as reasons for lifting the fiscal 2028 growth forecast from 70 to 75 percent. When asked about the financing deals that Nvidia provides for some of its customers, Kress appeared to hint that some things might change. "Our neoclouds have been so instrumental in terms of both supporting enterprises and supporting many of the different countries around the world, particularly on the sovereign perspective. And we continue to be working with them," she stated. But she added: "I think we would look at this and take a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing, as a lot of things have changed over this last quarter... but we do have some very, very strong existing customers that we will be continuing to work with." Kress also said that Nvidia's rack-scale Rubin platform had generated nearly $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments. She said the firm expects the major frontier AI labs to account for approximately 15 percent of its Data Center revenue this year. Kress said that Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed products based on its Hopper silicon to China, as scrutiny grows over Beijing's access to advanced AI technology, and so its future guidance does not count on any Hopper revenue from there. Nvidia sold $2.4 billion worth of Hopper kit to Chin

item.content:encoded: Nvidia's board says it has no plans to bring Jensen Huang back as the GPU giant reports quarterly revenue more than double that of a year ago. The AI infrastructure leviathan had some reassuring to do after its leather-jacketed rockstar leader left under a cloud last week. Huang had been central to its rise as the dominant supplier of AI compute. Newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones ruled out an imminent comeback, saying: "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Jones said the board was addressing the fallout and strengthening oversight, pointing to the creation of a committee to scrutinize the firm's security policies and export compliance. Nvidia has also retained the services of talent spotters Heidrick & Struggles to help find a new leader, according to Jones. Interim CEO and chief financial officer Colette Kress struck an upbeat tone on the company's Q3 earnings call. The results gave her plenty to work with : revenue rose 103 percent to $115.8 billion, while operating income climbed 115 percent to $77.5 billion. "We're addressing strong demand for compute across a diverse and expansive set of end customers, including hyperscalers, frontier labs, AI natives, enterprises, and governments," Kress said. She raised Nvidia's outlook for fiscal 2028, saying that the firm now expects revenue to grow approximately 75 percent year-on-year. Analysts immediately questioned this, asking what gave Kress the confidence to raise the outlook, given all the uncertainty surrounding the future direction of the company. Kress cited growing demand and additional supply as reasons for lifting the fiscal 2028 growth forecast from 70 to 75 percent. When asked about the financing deals that Nvidia provides for some of its customers, Kress appeared to hint that some things might change. "Our neoclouds have been so instrumental in terms of both supporting enterprises and supporting many of the different countries around the world, particularly on the sovereign perspective. And we continue to be working with them," she stated. But she added: "I think we would look at this and take a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing, as a lot of things have changed over this last quarter... but we do have some very, very strong existing customers that we will be continuing to work with." Kress also said that Nvidia's rack-scale Rubin platform had generated nearly $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments. She said the firm expects the major frontier AI labs to account for approximately 15 percent of its Data Center revenue this year. Kress said that Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed products based on its Hopper silicon to China, as scrutiny grows over Beijing's access to advanced AI technology, and so its future guidance does not count on any Hopper revenue from there. Nvidia sold $2.4 billion worth of Hopper kit to China during Q3 after being given the go-ahead from the Trump administration to sell products like its H200 accelerators in China. Analysts say they expect doubts to remain over Nvidia's future despite the strong Q3 results as the quarter was already in the bag by the time the Huang scandal broke. "Nvidia's next battle is not against competitors alone. It must navigate export controls, sovereign AI initiatives, supply chain expansion, and rising capital intensity – all while protecting industry-leading margins," commented Forrester principal analyst Naveen Chhabra. "The market sees the biggest risk not in the financials, but the leadership and employee motivation amidst turmoil, which began only after the Q3 ended. The bigger risk is not near-term demand but operations, maintaining employee confidence, retaining talent, and preserving Nvidia's innovation culture." February's results should offer a clearer view of Nvidia after Huang. For now, the mighty AI platform biz expects another record quarter, forecasting revenue of $130 billion, give or take 3 percent. ®

item.title: Windows Server 2028 won't be compatible by default
item.description: Microsoft has pushed Windows Server 2028 into public preview, with an eye on beefed-up security, new infrastructure support, and the inevitable nod to AI. Neil Hinnant, a director on the Windows Server team, talked up the security tweaks. There's a hardened Server Core configuration by default and a new security baseline. "Trusted Launch extends protection to virtual machines," he wrote . "Confidential VM support begins a journey to support integrity-protected runtimes on supported CVM hardware." Server Core will therefore arrive locked down by default – good news for security, potentially less so for administrators whose existing configurations depend on more permissive settings. "For years, Windows Server shipped compatible by default," wrote Senior Product Manager Christina Curlette. "Making the server secure was up to you, usually by applying the Security Baseline or your own hardening scripts after setup." With Windows Server 2028 (and starting from Windows Server Insider Preview build 29706), Server Core will be installed hardened. "Hundreds of security settings are on from first boot," Curlette wrote. "Because the defaults are now locked down, some things that worked on Windows Server 2025 may not work on Windows Server 2028 without changes. This includes older protocols, legacy authentication, and some management tools and scripts." For a company obsessed with backward compatibility, this is quite the step. Welcome though the hardening is, administrators will need to test carefully: working on Windows Server 2025 won't guarantee a smooth ride in the brave new world. AI gets a role on both sides of the security fence: helping uncover vulnerabilities and giving Microsoft another reason to sell servers. Windows Server 2028 is being pitched for running models locally, with support for accelerators such as AMD's Instinct MI350P. Not every server is destined to babysit a model, however, and the storage changes may be more immediately useful to enterprise administrators. Windows Server 2028 will enable native NVMe storage by default, along with NVMe over TCP and RDMA. Booting from ReFS is also planned, adding another item to the storage upgrade list. Intune management for Windows Server has also entered preview. Azure Arc, with its cloud-native management workflows, is obviously still around, while Intune brings a more familiar management interface for administrators already using it for endpoints. Hinnant acknowledged that this was a "major release," and it looks like the security hardening alone will require a good deal of thought from administrators before organizations adopt the eventual production release. Esben Dochy, Principal Technical Evangelist for SecOps at Lansweeper, told The Register that Microsoft had indicated that the hardened security only applied to new installations. item.dc:creator: Richard Speed
item.content:encoded: Microsoft has pushed Windows Server 2028 into public preview, with an eye on beefed-up security, new infrastructure support, and the inevitable nod to AI. Neil Hinnant, a director on the Windows Server team, talked up the security tweaks. There's a hardened Server Core configuration by default and a new security baseline. "Trusted Launch extends protection to virtual machines," he wrote . "Confidential VM support begins a journey to support integrity-protected runtimes on supported CVM hardware." Server Core will therefore arrive locked down by default – good news for security, potentially less so for administrators whose existing configurations depend on more permissive settings. "For years, Windows Server shipped compatible by default," wrote Senior Product Manager Christina Curlette. "Making the server secure was up to you, usually by applying the Security Baseline or your own hardening scripts after setup." With Windows Server 2028 (and starting from Windows Server Insider Preview build 29706), Server Core will be installed hardened. "Hundreds of security settings are on from first boot," Curlette wrote. "Because the defaults are now locked down, some things that worked on Windows Server 2025 may not work on Windows Server 2028 without changes. This includes older protocols, legacy authentication, and some management tools and scripts." For a company obsessed with backward compatibility, this is quite the step. Welcome though the hardening is, administrators will need to test carefully: working on Windows Server 2025 won't guarantee a smooth ride in the brave new world. AI gets a role on both sides of the security fence: helping uncover vulnerabilities and giving Microsoft another reason to sell servers. Windows Server 2028 is being pitched for running models locally, with support for accelerators such as AMD's Instinct MI350P. Not every server is destined to babysit a model, however, and the storage changes may be more immediately useful to enterprise administrators. Windows Server 2028 will enable native NVMe storage by default, along with NVMe over TCP and RDMA. Booting from ReFS is also planned, adding another item to the storage upgrade list. Intune management for Windows Server has also entered preview. Azure Arc, with its cloud-native management workflows, is obviously still around, while Intune brings a more familiar management interface for administrators already using it for endpoints. Hinnant acknowledged that this was a "major release," and it looks like the security hardening alone will require a good deal of thought from administrators before organizations adopt the eventual production release. Esben Dochy, Principal Technical Evangelist for SecOps at Lansweeper, told The Register that Microsoft had indicated that the hardened security only applied to new installations. "If that remains in the final release," he said, "in-place upgrades could be easier. The catch is that those servers may also miss out on the new security defaults." "Hardening is the right direction," he said, "but it will add work for teams moving to Server 2028." According to Lansweeper’s figures, as of October 2026, Windows Server 2019 ruled the roost with 33 percent. Windows Server 2025 had reached just 7 percent. "From behavior we've seen in the past," said Dochy, "adoption is primarily driven by lifecycle, so until the more used versions start going EOL, I don't expect much adoption, similar to what Server 2025 is experiencing." Windows Server 2025 remains under extended support until 2034, but Microsoft's direction of travel is clear: beefed-up security by default, a home for AI applications, and Intune management for fleets of servers. ®

item.title: Inside Nigeria's illegal gold mining industry
item.description: Nigerian authorities are attempting to clean up the mining sector in a country whose subsoil is rich in deposits of uranium, gold and lithium. The vast majority of these resources are mined illegally, meaning billions of euros are not included in the national GDP. Two years ago, the Nigerian government launched a paramilitary force, The Mining Marshals, to fight this illegal activity. Our Nigerian team visited an informal mine and then accompanied a patrol of Mining Marshals, here is their Report.

item.title: India's SatLeo Labs wants to build a 'thermometer for Earth' in space
item.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

AHMEDABAD, India — As climate disasters grow more frequent and severe, a young Indian space-tech startup is betting it can help the world act sooner by reading Earth's temperature from orbit in near-real time. SatLeo Labs, based here in western India, is building what it calls a " thermometer for Earth " in space. It plans to achieve its roadmap to deliver frequent, near-real-time thermal data through Pyro, a planned constellation of 15 microsatellites that will circle the planet in low Earth orbit by early 2030, if all goes to plan. Equipped with thermal sensors and onboard artificial intelligence , the satellites will measure the heat radiating from Earth's surface at a resolution finer than 10 meters (33 feet), which is sharp enough to map heat variations down to street level, the company says. "It's going to be that precise," SatLeo Labs co-founder Urmil Bakhai told Space.com in a recent interview. That level of detail, he said, helps distinguish temperatures across a single city and pinpoint urban hot spots, allowing governments and policymakers to plan targeted interventions and more heat-resilient city designs. The company is also targeting agriculture, and for good reason: Research suggests that thermal data can directly reveal water stress on crops days before leaves wilt, discolor or show other visible damage, unlike visible-light satellite imagery. Other uses the company is eyeing include spotting forest fires early, tracking industrial emissions and, on the defense side, detecting sudden temperature spikes from missile launches . Down the road, the team also envisions hyper-local uses. Near the top of its list are live heat maps built into navigation apps that could help gig-economy workers in India. These folks, who often ride motorcycles, could use the data to pick cooler routes during heat waves, said Bakhai. "We are in space, but we're solving problems on Earth ," said Shravan Bhati, SatLeo's co-founder and CEO. First, however, the company has to prove that its homegrown hardware works in space. On Oct. 1, SatLeo launched its first technology demonstrator, TAPAS-1, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare mission. Short for "Thermal Access Platform for Analytics & Solutions," TAPAS-1 is India's first commercial thermal payload in orbit and the first of SatLeo's three planned test payloads meant to validate its technology. Once complete, the 15-satellite Pyro fleet will scan all of the world's land surface at least twice a day, Bakhai said. Successful deployment of that fleet would make SatLeo one of just a few private thermal-imaging operators across the world, such as SatVu in the U.K. and OroraTech in Germany. The
item.dc:creator: Sharmila Kuthunur
item.content:encoded:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

AHMEDABAD, India — As climate disasters grow more frequent and severe, a young Indian space-tech startup is betting it can help the world act sooner by reading Earth's temperature from orbit in near-real time. SatLeo Labs, based here in western India, is building what it calls a " thermometer for Earth " in space. It plans to achieve its roadmap to deliver frequent, near-real-time thermal data through Pyro, a planned constellation of 15 microsatellites that will circle the planet in low Earth orbit by early 2030, if all goes to plan. Equipped with thermal sensors and onboard artificial intelligence , the satellites will measure the heat radiating from Earth's surface at a resolution finer than 10 meters (33 feet), which is sharp enough to map heat variations down to street level, the company says. "It's going to be that precise," SatLeo Labs co-founder Urmil Bakhai told Space.com in a recent interview. That level of detail, he said, helps distinguish temperatures across a single city and pinpoint urban hot spots, allowing governments and policymakers to plan targeted interventions and more heat-resilient city designs. The company is also targeting agriculture, and for good reason: Research suggests that thermal data can directly reveal water stress on crops days before leaves wilt, discolor or show other visible damage, unlike visible-light satellite imagery. Other uses the company is eyeing include spotting forest fires early, tracking industrial emissions and, on the defense side, detecting sudden temperature spikes from missile launches . Down the road, the team also envisions hyper-local uses. Near the top of its list are live heat maps built into navigation apps that could help gig-economy workers in India. These folks, who often ride motorcycles, could use the data to pick cooler routes during heat waves, said Bakhai. "We are in space, but we're solving problems on Earth ," said Shravan Bhati, SatLeo's co-founder and CEO. First, however, the company has to prove that its homegrown hardware works in space. On Oct. 1, SatLeo launched its first technology demonstrator, TAPAS-1, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare mission. Short for "Thermal Access Platform for Analytics & Solutions," TAPAS-1 is India's first commercial thermal payload in orbit and the first of SatLeo's three planned test payloads meant to validate its technology. Once complete, the 15-satellite Pyro fleet will scan all of the world's land surface at least twice a day, Bakhai said. Successful deployment of that fleet would make SatLeo one of just a few private thermal-imaging operators across the world, such as SatVu in the U.K. and OroraTech in Germany. The company has raised roughly $6 million since it was founded in 2023, and it holds letters of intent worth $54 million from prospective customers, Bakhai said. An illustration of SatLeo Labs' temperature-mapping payload. (Image credit: SatLeo Labs) 'Space is the only solution' SatLeo grew out of a government project that used satellite data for farming insights. Its founders found existing thermal data, such as from the U.S. government's Landsat satellites or Earth-observing craft operated by the San Francisco company Planet Labs , too coarse for India's fragmented farmlands, Bakhai said. When field teams and drones couldn't fill the gap at scale, "we realized space is the only solution," he said. SatLeo's orbital ambitions take shape on the ground, inside a light-blocked cleanroom at the company's headquarters here in Ahmedabad. When Space.com visited in late October, about three weeks after TAPAS-1 launched, a handful of engineers in cleanroom coats were already fine-tuning its successor, TAPAS-2. The payload itself sat perched on a solitary, nondescript table with a thick, hole-filled steel top meant to dampen vibrations from footsteps, traffic and the like. The room's only window was covered by a thick black blind to seal out stray light, a necessity for calibrating sensors meant to track the planet's thermal pulse from a few hundred kilometers up. Despite its small size, the payload is built to collect enormous amounts of data. How much detail a payload can capture "all depends upon the architecture of the detector," said SatLeo co-founder Ranendu Ghosh, a former scientist at the Indian Space Research Organisation ( ISRO ). The design captures two infrared bands, mid-wave and long-wave, on the same payload. The company says this lets a single design serve both civilian and defense uses: long-wave suits applications like agriculture, while the hotter signatures of fires or missile launches show up better in mid-wave. SatLeo Labs tests the payload for its TAPAS-1 satellite mission, which launched on Oct. 1, 2026. (Image credit: SatLeo Labs) 'Zeal to deliver in time' TAPAS-1 took just six months to build, and TAPAS-2 is on a similar timeline: It's expected to be ready by February 2027, according to the team. Access to government test facilities explains much of that speed, Bhati said. Rather than buy capital-intensive equipment, such as a thermal vacuum chamber that mimics conditions in space, the company calibrates its payloads at facilities run by IN-SPACe, the government agency that supports private space firms, and ISRO's Space Applications Centre, both in Ahmedabad. A small group of former ISRO scientists, about eight among a staff of around 40, also mentored the younger workforce and "really made this journey a little faster for us," Bakhai said. Ghosh, who spent more than two decades at ISRO, said the nature of a private company helps, too. "When I was in ISRO, I saw people delivering this kind of a payload," he said. "I never saw it delivered in less than a year." He credited the SatLeo team's "zeal to deliver in time," along with fewer administrative challenges than at ISRO, which he described as an organization where "you cannot bypass the hierarchy." The harder constraint, the founders said, is not building satellites but finding rockets to carry them to space. TAPAS-1's launch slipped from a planned February liftoff to October for lack of a ride, Bakhai said. SpaceX is reportedly not accepting new bookings until at least 2029. In addition, Skyroot Aerospace, which in July became the first Indian company to reach orbit , is still flying development missions meant to validate its Vikram-1 rocket before it begins full-scale commercial operations. SatLeo Labs' TAPAS-1 satellite (to left of arrow) deploys from the upper stage of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket on the Transporter-18 rideshare mission on Oct. 1, 2026. (Image credit: SatLeo Labs/SpaceX) "There is a challenge right now in terms of availability of launch vehicles," Bakhai said. Once additional Indian rockets, such as those built by Skyroot and Agnikul , are flying regularly, "things will be much easier." SatLeo is among more than 400 space startups that have emerged in India since the government opened the sector to private participation in 2020. Driven by this new wave of private enterprise, the country's space economy — currently valued at about $9 billion — is estimated to reach $40 billion over the next decade. Asked what advice they would give newcomers entering the growing industry, SatLeo's three co-founders offered a unified message for success: start with the problem, then decide what to build. "If you're solving a problem," Bhati said, "then people will bet on you."

item.title: Putin-Trump-Xi: Three men, three different agendas
item.description: An unprecedented trilateral summit of the leaders of China, Russia and the US will provide startling images and unsettle Europe this week, but all three presidents are approaching the meeting with starkly different agendas. Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will meet Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen for talks that have echoes of the US-UK-USSR February 1945 “big three” summit in Yalta. At that meeting, which took place months before the end of World War II, the leaders of Britain, the Soviet Union and the US agreed the postwar division of Europe. Europe, which will not have a representative at Thursday’s talks, will be eyeing them warily. The smiles and friendly handshakes may also cause chills in Ukraine, after almost half a decade of war with Russia, and Taiwan, the democratic island viewed by China as part of its territory. But analysts say it is unlikely that the meeting will result in a landmark breakthrough on key issues such as Ukraine, nuclear disarmament and AI, even if the fact it is taking place at all is remarkable. Here AFP looks at what the three men will want from the meeting. Putin: imagery and Ukraine On paper, Putin will be in the meeting as the junior partner, presiding over a country whose population, let alone economy, is dwarfed by both the United States and China. But the war sparked by Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine, which Trump famously vowed to resolve in 24 hours, will be at the centre of the talks as the conflict grinds towards its fifth anniversary. Putin will be buoyed by being able to set out his conditions for ending the war without Kyiv’s chief allies, the Europeans, or Ukraine being at the table. “He wants Russia, the US and China to decide everyone else’s geopolitical fate. But in the end it’s impossible to decide on the fundamentals of European security without Europeans,” said Fredrik Wesslau, senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR). The optics of the meeting, set to be relayed extensively by Russia’s state-controlled media, are also very important for Putin who has always pressed for Moscow to be seen as a great global power even after the collapse of the USSR. “A seat alongside the American and Chinese presidents would affirm Russia’s status as a global power, despite its much weaker economic position,” said Tsiporah Fried, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute. “Political rehabilitation would be a gain even without concessions on territory, sanctions, or Ukraine’s future alignment,” she added. Trump: nuclear and overcoming midterms Trump and the White House have framed the trilateral summit as a way of advancing nuclear arms control, although the president himself admitted before leaving Washington “it’s a tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes.” The imagery is also important for Trump as the 80-year-old contemplates his last two years in office as a lame-duck president followin

item.content:encoded: An unprecedented trilateral summit of the leaders of China, Russia and the US will provide startling images and unsettle Europe this week, but all three presidents are approaching the meeting with starkly different agendas. Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will meet Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen for talks that have echoes of the US-UK-USSR February 1945 “big three” summit in Yalta. At that meeting, which took place months before the end of World War II, the leaders of Britain, the Soviet Union and the US agreed the postwar division of Europe. Europe, which will not have a representative at Thursday’s talks, will be eyeing them warily. The smiles and friendly handshakes may also cause chills in Ukraine, after almost half a decade of war with Russia, and Taiwan, the democratic island viewed by China as part of its territory. But analysts say it is unlikely that the meeting will result in a landmark breakthrough on key issues such as Ukraine, nuclear disarmament and AI, even if the fact it is taking place at all is remarkable. Here AFP looks at what the three men will want from the meeting. Putin: imagery and Ukraine On paper, Putin will be in the meeting as the junior partner, presiding over a country whose population, let alone economy, is dwarfed by both the United States and China. But the war sparked by Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine, which Trump famously vowed to resolve in 24 hours, will be at the centre of the talks as the conflict grinds towards its fifth anniversary. Putin will be buoyed by being able to set out his conditions for ending the war without Kyiv’s chief allies, the Europeans, or Ukraine being at the table. “He wants Russia, the US and China to decide everyone else’s geopolitical fate. But in the end it’s impossible to decide on the fundamentals of European security without Europeans,” said Fredrik Wesslau, senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR). The optics of the meeting, set to be relayed extensively by Russia’s state-controlled media, are also very important for Putin who has always pressed for Moscow to be seen as a great global power even after the collapse of the USSR. “A seat alongside the American and Chinese presidents would affirm Russia’s status as a global power, despite its much weaker economic position,” said Tsiporah Fried, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute. “Political rehabilitation would be a gain even without concessions on territory, sanctions, or Ukraine’s future alignment,” she added. Trump: nuclear and overcoming midterms Trump and the White House have framed the trilateral summit as a way of advancing nuclear arms control, although the president himself admitted before leaving Washington “it’s a tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes.” The imagery is also important for Trump as the 80-year-old contemplates his last two years in office as a lame-duck president following his Republican Party’s brutal defeat in the US midterm elections earlier this month. Opponents also accuse Trump of having little to show for the hugely costly war against Iran, although the president insisted “we have Iran in very good shape.” In an early win for Trump, Xi took the unusual step of personally greeting him on arrival in Shenzhen. “Typically after bad midterms, this is how presidents reset and remind other leaders that they’re still in charge on foreign policy,” said Edgard Kagan, senior adviser at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). Trump will be wary of suggesting any easing of the restrictions on the export to China of the technology that powers AI, with the summit coming on the heels of the resignation of Jensen Huang, chief executive of AI chip giant Nvidia, over an affair with an alleged Chinese agent. “The room for manoeuvre for the Americans is constrained by the Nvidia scandal,” said Mathilde Velliet, a researcher at the French Institute of International Relations (IFRI), saying it had already led to a “hardening” of the US stance. China: glory for host, Taiwan and stability As host, Xi knows “the meeting could place China at the centre of global diplomacy and reinforce its standing alongside the United States,” said Fried, while cautioning “Beijing has reasons to avoid an ambitious agenda”. Beijing has maintained a careful stance throughout the Ukraine war, staying officially neutral while rejecting accusations of offering more than just tacit support to Russia including the alleged export of dual-use technology. “Xi does not want Russia to lose since this would be an overall win for the West,” said Wesslau. Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Mao Ning described the summit as being of “groundbreaking significance” with the three men due to have an “in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability in major-country relations.” On the nuclear issue, “China prefers bilateral nuclear talks with the United States over a trilateral format involving Russia,” said Tong Zhao, senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment, saying this allows Beijing to exercise leverage on matters it regards as “higher-priority” issues such as US arms sales to Taiwan. item.title: Supreme Court reserves judgment in Zamfara North APC senatorial dispute
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Supreme Court on Wednesday reserved judgment in the legal dispute concerning the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for the Zamfara North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. A five-member panel of the court, led by Justice Tijani Abubakar, reserved the matter for judgment after the contending parties adopted their respective briefs of argument. The appeal, marked SC/CV/840/2026, was lodged before the apex court by Senator Sahabi Ya’u, who is seeking to set aside a verdict the Sokoto Division of the Court of Appeal delivered in the matter. The APC had declared that Senator Ya’u won a primary election it conducted in the senatorial district on May 19. However, dissatisfied with the outcome of the primary, a governorship aspirant of the party, Dr. Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, took the matter to court. While challenging the process that led to the emergence of Senator Ya’u as the party’s flag bearer, Shinkafi told the court that no valid primary was conducted in the senatorial district. Processes before the court showed that the party had cleared three aspirants, Hanafi Musa Moriki, Shinkafi and Ya’u, to contest the primary poll. Shinkafi, in his suit, maintained that, contrary to the APC’s position, no valid consensus was reached among the aspirants to warrant the nomination of Senator Ya’u as the unopposed candidate. He told the court that he neither withdrew nor endorsed anyone as a consensus nominee, adding that he did not submit any written consent to withdraw from the race. Cited as respondents in the matter were the APC, INEC and Senator Ya’u. Meanwhile, in a judgment delivered on August 31, Justice Hassan Dikko of the Federal High Court in Gusau, Zamfara State, nullified the primary poll and ordered the APC to conduct a fresh one within 14 days. The high court held that the action of the APC was not in tandem with the principle of internal democracy entrenched in the party’s Constitution. Dissatisfied with the judgment, Senator Ya’u lodged an appeal before the Sokoto Division of the Court of Appeal. He, among other things, challenged the jurisdiction of the high court to meddle in a matter he said was within the realm of the domestic affairs of a political party and therefore non-justiciable. However, the appeal was dismissed, as the appellate court upheld the high court’s decision in the matter. Not happy with the verdict, Senator Ya’u approached the Supreme Court to set aside the concurrent decisions of the two lower courts. While the appellant argued his case on Wednesday through a team of lawyers led by Mr. Wale Balogun, SAN, the 1st respondent, Dr. Shinkafi, was represented by Mr. Bello Galadi, who filed a brief of argument on November 13 urging the court to dismiss the appeal for want of merit. item.title: NLC, TUC end rift, unite against anti-worker policies
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Nigeria’s two major labour centres, the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), have resolved their differences and agreed to strengthen their cooperation following the intervention of former leaders of both organisations. The reconciliation, announced at a joint world press conference on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, marks an end to the public disagreement that had threatened unity within the organised labour movement. The peace deal was brokered by former presidents of the two labour centres, who intervened to resolve the dispute and restore harmonious working relations between their leaderships. In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and TUC President General, Comrade Festus Osifo, the organisations reaffirmed their commitment to unity, solidarity and the protection of Nigerian workers’ rights and welfare. The statement acknowledged that a misunderstanding between the two labour centres had played out in the public domain but said the intervention of their former leaders had successfully resolved the disagreement. “It is no longer news that a family misunderstanding arose between the two Labour Centers, which unfortunately played out in the public domain. However, in the true spirit of labour solidarity, maturity and collective responsibility, distinguished former presidents of NLC and TUC intervened and worked tirelessly to resolve the disagreements. “We are pleased to announce that their intervention has yielded the desired results, and the misunderstanding has been amicably resolved,” the statement said. The two organisations declared that the unity of Nigerian workers was more important than disagreements among their leaders, pledging to work together in the interest of workers, pensioners and other vulnerable groups. They said the challenges confronting Nigerian workers required solidarity rather than division, adding that their common struggle must not be undermined by institutional differences or leadership disagreements. Both centres also reaffirmed that workers’ welfare, dignity and material well-being remained non-negotiable, stressing that their renewed partnership would focus on confronting exploitation, defending decent work, demanding economic justice and resisting policies they consider detrimental to workers and pensioners. “We are determined to ensure that our differences do not provide an opportunity for anti-worker forces to weaken the labour movement or undermine the gains achieved through decades of collective struggle,” they said. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Nigeria’s two major labour centres, the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), have resolved their differences and agreed to strengthen their cooperation following the intervention of former leaders of both organisations. The reconciliation, announced at a joint world press conference on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, marks an end to the public disagreement that had threatened unity within the organised labour movement. The peace deal was brokered by former presidents of the two labour centres, who intervened to resolve the dispute and restore harmonious working relations between their leaderships. In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and TUC President General, Comrade Festus Osifo, the organisations reaffirmed their commitment to unity, solidarity and the protection of Nigerian workers’ rights and welfare. The statement acknowledged that a misunderstanding between the two labour centres had played out in the public domain but said the intervention of their former leaders had successfully resolved the disagreement. “It is no longer news that a family misunderstanding arose between the two Labour Centers, which unfortunately played out in the public domain. However, in the true spirit of labour solidarity, maturity and collective responsibility, distinguished former presidents of NLC and TUC intervened and worked tirelessly to resolve the disagreements. “We are pleased to announce that their intervention has yielded the desired results, and the misunderstanding has been amicably resolved,” the statement said. The two organisations declared that the unity of Nigerian workers was more important than disagreements among their leaders, pledging to work together in the interest of workers, pensioners and other vulnerable groups. They said the challenges confronting Nigerian workers required solidarity rather than division, adding that their common struggle must not be undermined by institutional differences or leadership disagreements. Both centres also reaffirmed that workers’ welfare, dignity and material well-being remained non-negotiable, stressing that their renewed partnership would focus on confronting exploitation, defending decent work, demanding economic justice and resisting policies they consider detrimental to workers and pensioners. “We are determined to ensure that our differences do not provide an opportunity for anti-worker forces to weaken the labour movement or undermine the gains achieved through decades of collective struggle,” they said. To sustain the reconciliation, the labour centres said they had agreed to introduce measures to promote mutual respect, strengthen working relations, establish effective mechanisms for resolving future disagreements and prevent a recurrence of such disputes. They expressed appreciation to six former labour leaders whose intervention facilitated the peace agreement. They are Comrades Hassan Sunmonu, Peace Obiajulu, Peter Esele, Ayuba Wabba, Bobboi Bala Kaigama and Quadri Olaleye. The organisations described their intervention as a demonstration of the enduring values and shared sacrifices upon which the labour movement was built. They also called on their affiliates, state councils, industrial unions, workers and pensioners across the country to remain united and committed to the collective struggle. The statement urged workers not to allow the disagreement to erode their confidence in the two organisations, declaring that both centres remained united in their pursuit of social and economic justice. The joint statement was signed by Ajaero and Osifo, while Sunmonu signed on behalf of former presidents of the two labour centres. item.title: JAMB ends office visits for course changes
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has introduced a fully online process for candidates seeking to change their preferred institutions or courses, eliminating the need for physical visits to its offices to access the service. The new arrangement allows candidates to independently make the changes through the Board’s e-Facility portal from any location with internet access. The initiative is expected to reduce queues, transportation costs, waiting time and other inconveniences associated with physically accessing the service. In a statement issued by its Acting Director, Public Affairs and Protocol, Dr Fabian Benjamin, the Board said the development was part of efforts to improve service delivery and align its operations with the Federal Government’s Ease of Doing Business policy. Under the arrangement, candidates can complete the entire process, including payment, authentication and submission, online without visiting JAMB offices or accredited facilities. To access the service, candidates are required to log into the JAMB e-Facility portal at https://efacility.jamb.gov.ng using their registered email addresses and passwords. After logging in, they should select “Corrections and Uploads” from the sidebar menu, click on “Change of Programme/Institution”, select UTME and indicate the examination year for which the correction is required. Candidates are then expected to generate a payment invoice by clicking on “Make New Payment” and complete the transaction through the CREDO payment platform using a debit card or bank transfer. The Board advised candidates to return to the payment page on their profiles after making payment to confirm that the status has changed from “PENDING” to “PAID (Not Used)”. After confirming payment, candidates should return to the Change of Institution/Course page, enter their preferred institution and/or programme details and validate the transaction using a One-Time Password (OTP) sent to their registered email addresses. The process is completed by clicking the “SAVE” button, after which a confirmation message indicating that the change has been successfully made will be displayed. Candidates are also required to print their Change of Programme/Institution slips and log into the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) to confirm that their new choices have been updated. JAMB cautioned candidates to carefully review their selections before submitting requests to avoid errors. It also stressed that candidates must ensure their payment status reads “PAID (Not Used)” before proceeding and have access to their registered email accounts to receive and validate the OTP. The Board further advised candidates to carry out the process through their individual profiles rather than engage intermediaries or disclose their login details and OTPs to third parties.
