The new arrangement allows candidates to independently make the changes through the Board’s e-Facility portal from any location with internet access. The initiative is expected to reduce queues, transportation costs, waiting time and other inconveniences associated with physically accessing the service. In a statement issued by its Acting Director, Public Affairs and Protocol, Dr Fabian Benjamin, the Board said the development was part of efforts to improve service delivery and align its operations with the Federal Government’s Ease of Doing Business policy. Under the arrangement, candidates can complete the entire process, including payment, authentication and submission, online without visiting JAMB offices or accredited facilities. To access the service, candidates are required to log into the JAMB e-Facility portal at https://efacility.jamb.gov.ng using their registered email addresses and passwords. After logging in, they should select “Corrections and Uploads” from the sidebar menu, click on “Change of Programme/Institution”, select UTME and indicate the examination year for which the correction is required. Candidates are then expected to generate a payment invoice by clicking on “Make New Payment” and complete the transaction through the CREDO payment platform using a debit card or bank transfer. The Board advised candidates to return to the payment page on their profiles after making payment to confirm that the status has changed from “PENDING” to “PAID (Not Used)”. After confirming payment, candidates should return to the Change of Institution/Course page, enter their preferred institution and/or programme details and validate the transaction using a One-Time Password (OTP) sent to their registered email addresses. The process is completed by clicking the “SAVE” button, after which a confirmation message indicating that the change has been successfully made will be displayed. Candidates are also required to print their Change of Programme/Institution slips and log into the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) to confirm that their new choices have been updated. JAMB cautioned candidates to carefully review their selections before submitting requests to avoid errors. It also stressed that candidates must ensure their payment status reads “PAID (Not Used)” before proceeding and have access to their registered email accounts to receive and validate the OTP. The Board further advised candidates to carry out the process through their individual profiles rather than engage intermediaries or disclose their login details and OTPs to third parties. It said there was no need to pay individuals to perform a service candidates could complete independently online. According to the statement, the Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, reaffirmed the Board’s commitment to using technology to remove bureaucratic bottlenecks, improve service delivery and make essential services accessible to candidates irrespective of their locations. The Board said the objective was to enable candidates to spend less time dealing with administrative processes and more time pursuing their educational aspirations. The initiative is the latest in a series of measures aimed at reducing physical visits to JAMB offices, easing pressure on its facilities and improving service delivery to candidates and other stakeholders. item.title: US Congress neither met nor endorsed Obi – Atiku’s lobbyists
item.description: A Washington-based lobbying firm hired by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Von Batten-Montague-York, has dismissed reports that the United States Congress met with or endorsed the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi. The firm said the event attended by Obi during his visit to Washington, DC, was a private gathering and did not constitute an official meeting with the US Congress. The clarification followed reports suggesting that Obi had secured the endorsement of members of the US Congress for his 2027 presidential ambition. Obi had announced on his X platform that he arrived in Washington, DC, on Monday, November 16, for a series of meetings and engagements with congressional leaders from both the House of Representatives and the Senate, as well as other influential American figures. He said the discussions focused on Nigeria’s development, security, economic prosperity and the future of the country’s democracy. However, Von Batten-Montague-York, in a statement posted on its X platform on Tuesday, said neither the Congress nor its relevant foreign affairs committee met with or endorsed Obi. The firm’s principal, Dr Von Batten, said he was responding to media reports claiming that Obi had received congressional endorsement, particularly after his firm was mentioned in a public commentary. He said, “Congress did not meet with or endorse Mr. Obi. The event he attended was private, and no one in the video is a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee or its Subcommittee on Africa, which oversees U.S. foreign policy toward Africa. “I know everyone in the video, and no official from the State Department’s Bureau of African Affairs appears in it either.” Batten said he recognised Congressman Marlin Stutzman and Congresswoman Beth Van Duyne, who were among the American figures Obi identified as having met during his visit. He, however, noted that neither lawmaker served on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, adding that they served on committees responsible for budget and small business matters. He said his clarification was not intended to diminish the significance of Obi’s visit but to correct what he described as inaccurate reports. In his earlier account of the visit, Obi said he held a substantive interview with American television commentator Glenn Beck, during which they discussed Nigeria’s challenges, accountable leadership and the management of the country’s resources. He also listed Stutzman, Van Duyne, former Congressman Todd Tiahrt, Suzanne Bock Grisham and retired US Army Colonel Albert V. Short among the people he met. Obi further said he addressed an audience on Capitol Hill, where he highlighted the need for international cooperation and support for Nigeria, particularly in security, national unity, economic development and democratic governance. He maintained that Nigerians must determine the country’s future through credible elections and the protection of citizens’ rights. The

item.title: Police arrest 15 over £1.5M 'we'll recover your losses' scam targeting elderly
item.description: Fifteen people have been arrested over an alleged scam that squeezed more money from investment fraud victims by offering to help recover their losses. City of London Police searched 17 London addresses on November 11 and apprehended 14 men and one woman. All have since been released on bail. Investigators say the suspected fraudsters posed as regulators to persuade previous victims that compensation was available. Reports submitted through the UK's Report Fraud service helped investigators trace the compensation pitch to around 3,000 recipients since October 2025. Most victims were elderly, police said. The offers arrived by letter and email, promising redress for earlier investment losses. City of London Police said the victims were initially targeted by a range of investment scams related to art, carbon credits, land, whisky, wine, and pensions, and that some took place more than a decade prior to their re-victimization. Targets were directed to a company that demanded a holding fee before supposedly reclaiming their money. Police say those who paid were left further out of pocket. "Today's action sends a clear message to those who target vulnerable people for financial gain: you will be pursued and will face robust action," said Nik Adams, deputy commissioner at the City of London Police. "Behind every fraud report is a real person whose trust has been damaged, and in some cases, whose life savings have been stolen. We know the impact of these crimes can be devastating. "This case highlights the importance of reporting fraud through the Report Fraud service. Information provided by victims helped investigators link reports together, uncover the wider conspiracy, and identify those involved. It is a powerful reminder that every report counts and can play a vital role in bringing offenders to justice." The investigation also extends beyond London, with police identifying locations linked to the case in Kent and Hertfordshire. The searches resulted in officers seizing cash, drugs, and other high-value items, including a watch worth around £230,000, with the total haul valued at more than £2 million. Police put losses identified so far at £1.5 million and expect that figure to rise as the investigation continues. Knowing the details of an earlier scam doesn't make a caller trustworthy, police warned. That information can be used to sell victims a second fraud. Report Fraud has also highlighted substantial losses in other scams affecting older people. Fraudsters exploiting positions of trust stole a reported £93.8 million during 2025/26. People aged 70 and over lost more than £51 million, with relatives, friends, carers, and others entrusted with their finances among the perpetrators. Report Fraud received 3,812 reports in this category. "The impact of fraud extends far beyond financial loss, especially when it is carried out by those who are trusted by the victim," said Mark Evans, president at the Law Society of England and Wales. Report Fraud received 3,812 reports in this category. "The impact of fraud extends far beyond financial loss, especially when it is carried out by those who are trusted by the victim," said Mark Evans, president at the Law Society of England and Wales. Similarly, at the end of October, Report Fraud said £24.3 million was stolen between January and August 2026 through AI-augmented investment scams , with people aged 60 and over accounting for nearly 80 percent of reports. However, it's not always the elderly in scammers' crosshairs. Those in the 30-39 age bracket accounted for the most reports in one of the most lucrative frauds affecting Brits in recent times. Payment diversion fraud, which tricks victims into paying a criminal's bank account instead of the intended recipient's, resulted in £101 million in losses in the 2025/26 financial year, according to Report Fraud's figures. ®

item.title: Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details
item.description: In the one light-day that humanity's most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again. Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter's moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a "commemorative phonograph record," in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space. About those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson . While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs' overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago. Read full article Comments

item.title: Army intercepts 300 rounds of ammunition concealed in beans sack
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Troops of the Nigerian Army have arrested a 47-year-old man suspected of transporting ammunition to individuals in Kogi State, recovering 300 rounds of 7.62mm by 39mm ammunition concealed in a sack of beans. The interception followed an intelligence-led operation aimed at disrupting the supply of weapons and ammunition to criminal groups. The Army said the suspect, identified as Umaru Muhammad, a resident of Ashe Village, was intercepted at about 9:30pm on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, by troops of the Atsawa Blocking Force working with local vigilantes. In a statement on Wednesday, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said a search of the suspect’s belongings led to the discovery of the ammunition concealed in the sack of beans. According to the statement, preliminary interrogation indicated that the ammunition was allegedly intended for two individuals identified as Gimba and Dare, reportedly residents of Gori Village along the River Niger corridor in Lokoja Local Government Area of Kogi State. The Army said the identities and alleged roles of the individuals were being investigated, adding that the circumstances surrounding the attempted transfer of the ammunition remained subject to further inquiries. Other items recovered from the suspect included a Bajaj motorcycle, a mobile telephone and ₦30,500 in cash. Muhammad is currently in military custody as investigations continue to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged ammunition transaction and identify other persons who may be connected to it. The Army said the operation formed part of its ongoing efforts to disrupt the supply of arms, ammunition and other logistics to groups involved in terrorism, banditry and kidnapping. It added that troops would sustain intelligence-driven operations and strengthen cooperation with local security stakeholders to prevent criminal activities. The Army also urged members of the public to report suspicious movements, particularly the transportation of concealed arms, ammunition and other prohibited items, to security agencies. It reaffirmed its commitment to protecting communities and supporting efforts to restore peace and security across the country. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Troops of the Nigerian Army have arrested a 47-year-old man suspected of transporting ammunition to individuals in Kogi State, recovering 300 rounds of 7.62mm by 39mm ammunition concealed in a sack of beans. The interception followed an intelligence-led operation aimed at disrupting the supply of weapons and ammunition to criminal groups. The Army said the suspect, identified as Umaru Muhammad, a resident of Ashe Village, was intercepted at about 9:30pm on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, by troops of the Atsawa Blocking Force working with local vigilantes. In a statement on Wednesday, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said a search of the suspect’s belongings led to the discovery of the ammunition concealed in the sack of beans. According to the statement, preliminary interrogation indicated that the ammunition was allegedly intended for two individuals identified as Gimba and Dare, reportedly residents of Gori Village along the River Niger corridor in Lokoja Local Government Area of Kogi State. The Army said the identities and alleged roles of the individuals were being investigated, adding that the circumstances surrounding the attempted transfer of the ammunition remained subject to further inquiries. Other items recovered from the suspect included a Bajaj motorcycle, a mobile telephone and ₦30,500 in cash. Muhammad is currently in military custody as investigations continue to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged ammunition transaction and identify other persons who may be connected to it. The Army said the operation formed part of its ongoing efforts to disrupt the supply of arms, ammunition and other logistics to groups involved in terrorism, banditry and kidnapping. It added that troops would sustain intelligence-driven operations and strengthen cooperation with local security stakeholders to prevent criminal activities. The Army also urged members of the public to report suspicious movements, particularly the transportation of concealed arms, ammunition and other prohibited items, to security agencies. It reaffirmed its commitment to protecting communities and supporting efforts to restore peace and security across the country. item.title: Arewa group faults northern elders over Tinubu criticism
item.description: … Calls for broader consultation before claiming to speak for North By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — The Arewa Emerging Elites Round Table has disagreed with recent comments by Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, Dr Usman Bugaje, former Minister Adamu Maina Waziri and Prof Usman Yusuf on President Bola Tinubu’s administration, insisting that the views of a few individuals should not be presented as the collective position of Northern Nigeria. The group made its position known at a press conference in Kaduna, where it called for broader consultation among stakeholders before anyone claims to speak on behalf of the region. Reading a briefing titled, “Stop Hiding Naked Partisanship Behind the Sacred Robes of Arewa Eldership: You Do Not Speak for the North!”, the group’s chairman, Abubakar A. Kurawa, said Northern Nigeria comprised diverse interests and perspectives that should be adequately represented in public discussions. The organisation expressed concern over what it described as attempts to interpret comments made at a book presentation in Abuja as reflecting the position of the 19 Northern states. It questioned whether traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth organisations, professional groups and ordinary citizens across the region had been adequately consulted before such positions were presented as representing the North. The group maintained that individuals had the constitutional right to criticise government policies and express concerns about the administration but argued that such opinions should be clearly distinguished from the collective position of the region. It said public discussions about the performance of the Federal Government should accommodate different perspectives rather than suggest that a particular gathering or group of individuals represented the views of all Northern Nigerians. The Round Table also called on political leaders and former public office holders from the region to demonstrate accountability by highlighting their contributions to the development of Northern Nigeria. It stressed that discussions about leadership and governance should focus on measurable contributions to addressing the challenges confronting the region. The organisation further urged Northern stakeholders to give greater attention to insecurity, agriculture, infrastructure, education and economic development, describing them as critical issues requiring sustained engagement with governments at all levels. It said political and developmental interests of the North should take precedence over individual political interests and called for constructive engagement with the Federal Government on issues affecting the region. The group also emphasised that criticism of government policies remained an important feature of democratic governance, adding that public officials should be open to scrutiny and accountability. item.title: Plateau killings: Obi condemns attacks, questions intelligence failures
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has mourned victims of the latest attacks in Plateau State, condemned the recurring killings in the state and questioned intelligence failures that have left communities vulnerable. In a statement posted on his X handle on Wednesday, Obi called for stronger security measures, thorough investigations and justice for the victims, saying the continued loss of lives showed the need for urgent action to protect Nigerians. “I am deeply saddened and troubled by reports that at least nine people were killed in the Zuwagal community, Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State, in yet another assault on innocent Nigerians,” Obi said. He described the killings as part of a “deeply concerning pattern of recurring attacks, displacement and the destruction of communities throughout the country.” Citing OpenWatch security incident records, Obi said 261 deaths were reported across Nigeria between November 2 and 15, including 24 in Plateau during the first week and 15 in the second. He added that Plateau recorded further attacks on November 16. “These victims are not merely numbers. They were fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners whose lives were abruptly ended, leaving families and entire communities to mourn,” he said, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and the people of Plateau State. Obi questioned why communities continued to face threats without adequate protection and why intelligence reports were not leading to preventive action. He called on the government and security agencies to reinforce operations in vulnerable communities, investigate the attacks, establish reliable early-warning and rapid-response systems, support displaced families and ensure those responsible were brought to justice. “Every Nigerian life is valuable, regardless of ethnicity, religion or political affiliation. The right to life must never be subject to negotiation,” he said. “Nigeria must do more than mourn those who have died. We must protect those who are still living.” Vanguard reported that at least five people were killed in fresh attacks on communities in Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi local government areas. The latest incident occurred at about 9pm on Sunday, November 15, when suspected terrorists attacked Zwagal community in Jipal District, Mangu, killing three people, while others were reported missing. Two other people were killed in separate attacks in Riyom and Barkin Ladi. The Berom Youth Moulders Association said Da Ishaku Pam Vwos, 79, was killed in Sho village, Barkin Ladi, and Dauda John Davou, 42, was killed in Sambak community, Riyom. The association also said attackers entered Jol community but met resistance from local vigilantes. The association called on President Bola Tinubu, Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang and security agencies to strengthen deployments in vulnerable communities and investigate the killings. item.title: Subsidy benefits went to intermediaries, not Nigerians — Uzodimma
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, has said the benefits of Nigeria’s petroleum subsidy regime largely accrued to intermediaries in the oil sector rather than ordinary Nigerians it was designed to protect. Uzodimma stated this on Wednesday while delivering an address at the ongoing 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. The forum was organised by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and hosted by the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR). The governor said responsible governance required building public trust through community engagement, stakeholder relations and inclusive development. He described one of the greatest tests of leadership as taking difficult decisions that initially hurt the people but are expected to benefit them in the long run, while maintaining honest communication to secure public understanding and trust. He said: “I like to think about leadership, the experience I learned in leading Imo State as governor and keeping the trust. Especially when you want to accept a decision that will hurt people first before such decisions will help them. “It is even tougher when the administration is new and when the people are yet to see tangible results they can relate to.” Citing the removal of the petroleum subsidy as an example, Uzodimma said the policy was originally intended to ease the burden on ordinary Nigerians but that much of its benefits went to intermediaries in the petroleum sector. “The petroleum subsidy was meant to help ordinary Nigerians. But most of the benefits ended up with intermediaries in the sector,” he said. He defended President Bola Tinubu’s decision to remove the subsidy, describing it as necessary in the overall interest of the country. According to him, Nigerians across different sectors and segments of society had openly called for the removal of the subsidy before the policy was implemented. “Do not forget that before he did that, Nigerians across different sectors and segments had openly canvassed and demanded that it be removed,” he said. The governor further argued that the removal had increased the resources available to state governments and the Federal Capital Territory for infrastructure and socioeconomic development. He, however, acknowledged that the resulting price adjustments had created difficulties for many households, stressing that reforms were more likely to deliver their intended benefits when citizens understood the reasons behind them. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By John Alechenu ABUJA — Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, has said the benefits of Nigeria’s petroleum subsidy regime largely accrued to intermediaries in the oil sector rather than ordinary Nigerians it was designed to protect. Uzodimma stated this on Wednesday while delivering an address at the ongoing 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. The forum was organised by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and hosted by the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR). The governor said responsible governance required building public trust through community engagement, stakeholder relations and inclusive development. He described one of the greatest tests of leadership as taking difficult decisions that initially hurt the people but are expected to benefit them in the long run, while maintaining honest communication to secure public understanding and trust. He said: “I like to think about leadership, the experience I learned in leading Imo State as governor and keeping the trust. Especially when you want to accept a decision that will hurt people first before such decisions will help them. “It is even tougher when the administration is new and when the people are yet to see tangible results they can relate to.” Citing the removal of the petroleum subsidy as an example, Uzodimma said the policy was originally intended to ease the burden on ordinary Nigerians but that much of its benefits went to intermediaries in the petroleum sector. “The petroleum subsidy was meant to help ordinary Nigerians. But most of the benefits ended up with intermediaries in the sector,” he said. He defended President Bola Tinubu’s decision to remove the subsidy, describing it as necessary in the overall interest of the country. According to him, Nigerians across different sectors and segments of society had openly called for the removal of the subsidy before the policy was implemented. “Do not forget that before he did that, Nigerians across different sectors and segments had openly canvassed and demanded that it be removed,” he said. The governor further argued that the removal had increased the resources available to state governments and the Federal Capital Territory for infrastructure and socioeconomic development. He, however, acknowledged that the resulting price adjustments had created difficulties for many households, stressing that reforms were more likely to deliver their intended benefits when citizens understood the reasons behind them. Using an example from Imo State, Uzodimma explained how government interventions could benefit some groups while initially affecting the livelihoods of others. He said the introduction of modern buses operating at affordable fares along busy routes in Owerri would reduce transportation costs for workers, traders and students but could affect commercial drivers who might see the initiative as a threat to their businesses. He noted, however, that affected drivers could adapt by providing shuttle services, car hire operations and transportation services on routes not covered by the government buses. “The import here is that the same decision that hurts many can help a few, at least for a while,” he said. Uzodimma maintained that government’s responsibility was to ensure that the benefits of its policies reached as many people as possible while communicating the objectives and expected outcomes to those affected. “But as a government, our duty is to spread the good as widely as we can, and to communicate our intentions, our purposes and goals to those who must bear some pain along the way,” he said. He added that consistent, honest and effective communication was essential to helping citizens adjust to difficult policy decisions and maintain confidence in government. “Achieving these takes consistent communication. You will need to keep communicating honestly and effectively with the people until they trust you,” the governor said. item.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe is now one light-day away
item.description: Voyager 1 has traveled further than any other man-made object. | Photo by NASA/Hulton Archive/Getty Images After traveling through the void of space for 49 years, Voyager 1 has hit a momentous milestone: the spacecraft is now officially one light-day away from Earth, which is, as NASA put it, "very, very far." The probe crossed the milepost on Wednesday at 5:16AM ET, and is now 16.094 billion miles away from our planet - equal to the distance that light travels in 24 hours. It's the furthest that any human-made object has ever traveled, and Voyager 1's journey isn't over yet. It's been heading towards a star called Gliese 445 in the Ursa Minor constellation since completing its primary objectives to conduct flybys of Jupiter and Saturn in 1980. … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
item.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘When I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West’: the two lives of Bromley footballer Omar Sowunmi
item.description: Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career “I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds. Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons. Continue reading...

item.title: Super Eagles move up to 29th in latest FIFA world rankings
item.description: The Nigerian Super Eagles have moved up one place to 29th in the latest FIFA men’s world rankings released on Wednesday. The improvement also sees the team climb to fifth position among African countries, overtaking Algeria, which dropped out of the continent’s top five. The Super Eagles’ latest progress comes after their two November fixtures against Tanzania in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Eric Chelle’s men began the international window with a 3-1 victory over the Taifa Stars at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo last Friday. However, Nigeria failed to maintain their winning run, settling for a goalless draw against the same opponents in Tuesday’s return fixture at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar. Morocco retained their position as Africa’s highest-ranked team, followed by Senegal, Egypt and Côte d’Ivoire in second, third and fourth places, respectively. On the global ranking, Spain maintained their position as the world’s number one team, while Argentina, France and England retained their places among the top five. The post Super Eagles move up to 29th in latest FIFA world rankings appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins US Senate race in Alaska
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola ​won Alaska's US Senate race on Tuesday, projections from US media showed, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and giving her party its ninth Senate flip of the midterm elections and a commanding 56-44 majority in the upper house of Congress. France 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson has the latest.

item.title: ULA says Vulcan lacked the oomph to get Amazon satellites to orbit
item.description: United Launch Alliance (ULA) says poor booster performance appears to have doomed Sunday's Vulcan mission, which lost an Amazon Leo satellite payload on the rocket's return to flight. ULA's initial assessment points to trouble almost immediately. "Early indications are that just after liftoff the launch vehicle experienced low booster performance," it said. As a result, stage separation occurred at too low an altitude, and the rocket was not traveling fast enough for the payload to reach orbit. The second stage appeared to perform well, with its RL10 engines operating as planned, but that wasn't enough to make up for the shortfall, and the mission failed . ULA lost telemetry approximately ten minutes into flight. An investigation is underway, led by ULA and overseen by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), which had to activate two Debris Response Areas where debris was falling. The agency directs aircraft to leave these areas, and others are prevented from entering. Previous flights had been blighted by problems with the solid rocket boosters , designed to give the rocket a kick at launch. Those issues prompted a stand-down while investigators examined the cause. This time, ULA said: "All indications are that the solid rocket booster performance was nominal, following nozzle improvements implemented for this launch." Attention therefore turns to Vulcan's liquid-fueled core stage, powered by two Blue Origin BE-4 engines, though that does not establish an engine fault. Fuel delivery or another first-stage system could also be responsible, and the investigation is ongoing. The BE-4 also powers Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, which exploded on the launchpad during a ground test in May. In August, Blue Origin boss Dave Limp said that the issue originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines. Modifications were made to deal with the problem. The upper stage's apparently normal performance may offer some reassurance to NASA, although the investigation remains at an early stage. The agency dropped the delayed Exploration Upper Stage earlier this year and is pursuing a stretched Centaur V alongside its existing interim cryogenic propulsion stage as options for Artemis IV. NASA is targeting Artemis IV for early 2028 and Artemis V for later that year. ULA said: "We truly understand the impact this has on our customers and are committed to returning to flight as safely and quickly as we can." The failure also dents ULA's otherwise impressive launch record. A predecessor of Vulcan, the Atlas V, has a 100 percent success record for payloads reaching orbit. However, it uses Russian RD-180 engines, a dependency the US wishes to remove . ®

item.title: NLC, TUC Resolve Disagreement After N70,000 Transport Allowance Controversy
item.description: The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have resolved their recent disagreement, following the recent banter over the N70,000 one-off six-month allowance approved by President Tinubu. The two labour centres announced the resolution of the dispute on Wednesday at a joint press conference held in Abuja. In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and TUC President-General, Festus Osifo, the unions acknowledged that their disagreement had played out publicly but insisted that their shared history and responsibility to Nigerian workers must take precedence over leadership and institutional differences. Reaffirming their commitment to a united labour movement and the collective defence of workers’ rights, they described the disagreement as a family misunderstanding that had now been amicably settled through the intervention of former leaders of both organisations. A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The controversy followed its approval by the Federal Government for workers across all levels for six months. While speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief recently, Comrade Joe Ajero argued that the Union has the power to negotiate alone on labour matters based on the principle of most workers representatives of the International Labour Organization (ILO). “TUC can negotiate along with NLC, but NLC can negotiate alone based on the principle of most workers representatives of the ILO”, the NLC President noted. On his part, the TUC President, while also appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief , described the N70,000 agreement by the NLC President as an aberration, saying that the TUC was not carried along in the negotiations. Osifo challenged Ajaero to produce the ILO regulation document that said either of the labour unions could negotiate on behalf of the other. “He should show me in the ILO Regulations where it says one party is going to negotiate without the other one being there or consulted. He should show me! He should show Nigerians! NLC determines how TUC participates”, Ajaero adding that the TUC does not submit its proposal to TUC. “It is the other way round,” he stated that the Ministry of Labour and other labour authorities will not engage with the Trade Union, as it acts alone on workers’ welfare negotiations. The trade congress leader, in his reply, said, “As I listened to Ajaero today, I was wondering if it is the same NLC that produced the likes of Adams Oshiomole, Hassan Sumonu, Ayuba Wabba and so on. “There is nowhere in ILO regulations that says a trade centre cannot negotiate for its members. item.dc:creator: OpeOluwani Akintayo
item.content:encoded: The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have resolved their recent disagreement, following the recent banter over the N70,000 one-off six-month allowance approved by President Tinubu. The two labour centres announced the resolution of the dispute on Wednesday at a joint press conference held in Abuja. In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and TUC President-General, Festus Osifo, the unions acknowledged that their disagreement had played out publicly but insisted that their shared history and responsibility to Nigerian workers must take precedence over leadership and institutional differences. Reaffirming their commitment to a united labour movement and the collective defence of workers’ rights, they described the disagreement as a family misunderstanding that had now been amicably settled through the intervention of former leaders of both organisations. A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The controversy followed its approval by the Federal Government for workers across all levels for six months. While speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief recently, Comrade Joe Ajero argued that the Union has the power to negotiate alone on labour matters based on the principle of most workers representatives of the International Labour Organization (ILO). “TUC can negotiate along with NLC, but NLC can negotiate alone based on the principle of most workers representatives of the ILO”, the NLC President noted. On his part, the TUC President, while also appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief , described the N70,000 agreement by the NLC President as an aberration, saying that the TUC was not carried along in the negotiations. Osifo challenged Ajaero to produce the ILO regulation document that said either of the labour unions could negotiate on behalf of the other. “He should show me in the ILO Regulations where it says one party is going to negotiate without the other one being there or consulted. He should show me! He should show Nigerians! NLC determines how TUC participates”, Ajaero adding that the TUC does not submit its proposal to TUC. “It is the other way round,” he stated that the Ministry of Labour and other labour authorities will not engage with the Trade Union, as it acts alone on workers’ welfare negotiations. The trade congress leader, in his reply, said, “As I listened to Ajaero today, I was wondering if it is the same NLC that produced the likes of Adams Oshiomole, Hassan Sumonu, Ayuba Wabba and so on. “There is nowhere in ILO regulations that says a trade centre cannot negotiate for its members. It is not there! It is just that if you are going to the ILO, it is tripartite- the labour, government and the employers. Photo combo of TUC Osifo and NLC Ajaero Ajaero, responding to Festus’ position of having over 300,000 members in the federal civil service, said, “The 2005 Trade Union Amendment Act made membership of trade unions voluntary. “It is the worker that determines the union he belongs to. “Section 40 of the Nigerian 1999 Constitution as amended was clear that every Nigerian worker has the right to belong to any trade union, political or religious institution of his choice, which gives every worker the latitude to belong to any union of their choice”. He argued that Osifo saying he has a good number of workers in his union does not add up, given that only one member union of TUC belongs to the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, which consists of eight union bodies, and seven of them are in NLC. He further argued that one union from TUC, which is a member of the joint body, has subjected its power to the joint body. Speaking on the operation of the union, Osifo noted that “In that case, the two bodies must come together. We are not contesting the fact that NLC has more affiliates. “But what we are saying is that you have about 60 affiliates while we have about 40. You cannot! You cannot negotiate for a body that is represented, for a body that has a trade union. “You cannot negotiate on their behalf! It is not there anywhere! “Yes, if we go to negotiations- I sit down, you sit down, and we agree”. Osifo challenged Ajaero to produce the ILO regulation document that said either of the labour unions could negotiate on behalf of the other. “He should show me in the ILO Regulations where it says one party is going to negotiate without the other one being there or consulted. He should show me! He should show Nigerians! “ILO doctrine is that when you have more affiliates, and you are going for one of their events, it is not correct that the most represented will go and negotiate on behalf of the other one when the unions have their own umbrella. According to Osifo, the meeting where the N70,000 transport allowance was agreed upon was not attended by members of the Council and does not represent majority consensus. “But that meeting that took place was not the Council meeting. The Minister is not a member of the Council. Ajaero is not a member of the Council. The Council even has a quorum and the number of persons that must be seated to form a quorum. But at the end of the day, that meeting was not a JNC meeting. The members of JNC were not there! “Again, if you see the release that was sent out by those three bodies, you will discover that after the last minimum wage, we got about a 33 per cent increment, and how does that work? Because from N30,000, we got N70,000. “What you are supposed to do is that JNC will have to sit down and apply consequential adjustments.” Ajaero maintained that the NLC engaged with the federal government to secure the ₦70,000 transport intervention. “We gave the government an ultimatum; we were supposed to start an action. The government asked for four days to meet with us, and we met, and they resumed sitting after four days. After the meeting, the 70k allowance came up” He asserted that minimum wage demands could not be presented when the government has not set up a negotiation committee, stating that it required wider consultation among labour leaders, government officials, and employers before any wage increase can be agreed upon. NLC President, Joe Ajaero. FG Sets Up Committee To Review New Minimum Wage The Federal Government on Tuesday approved the constitution of a new committee to comprehensively examine and address the issues raised by the TUC regarding a new minimum wage for Nigerian workers. The development was revealed by the TUC’s Secretary-General, Comrade General N.A. Toro, in a statement on Tuesday, following a meeting with the Federal Government in response to a letter dated 8th October, 2026, titled “Request for an Urgent Meeting to Address Critical National Economic, Security and Labour Challenges,” submitted by the Union. While the meeting was chaired by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, the TUC delegation was led by the President, Comrade Engr. Festus Osifo, and comprised Comrade General N.A. Toro, Secretary-General; Comrade Shehu Mohammed, Deputy President; Comrade Akintola Benjamin, Trustee; and Comrade Kamal Ibrahim, Auditor II. The Federal Government meets with TUC on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Also in attendance were the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Ibrahim Kana. While providing further explanation, TUC noted that it had insisted on a salary increment rather than a mere one-off N70,000 six-month transportation package. “In the course of the deliberations, the TUC made its position unequivocally clear on the proposed ₦70,000 transport intervention for a period of six months, which it rejected, preferring instead a salary increase pending the commencement and conclusion of discussions on a new National Minimum Wage. “This po

item.title: ‘Fake Agency’ Case: Adeyemi in custody for his own safety, ICPC tells court
item.description: … as defendants plead not guilty, beg for bail By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) said on Wednesday that it kept the self-styled Director-General (DG) of the alleged “non-existent” Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Prince Adeniyi Adeyemi, in custody for his own safety. According to the Commission, many of those allegedly defrauded by the defendant, a number of whom have filed petitions against him, are capable of physically harming him on sight. It therefore prayed the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), sitting at Maitama in Abuja, to reject an application that Adeyemi filed to be released on bail pending the determination of the criminal charge against him. “My lord, the defendant is facing allegations of obtaining by false pretence. “There are many petitions against him, and the people who lodged those petitions are after him. “There is this particular man from Ibadan whom he defrauded, which formed part of the counts in the charge. He has been seriously searching for him. “We believe that it will be in his own best interest to remain in custody for safekeeping,” the prosecution counsel, Mr. Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, added. The ICPC urged the court to also deny bail to four civil servants who are facing trial alongside the alleged fake PFIPC DG. The anti-corruption agency took the position after the defendants pleaded not guilty to a 36-count amended charge it entered against them. All the defendants, through their respective lawyers, begged the court to release them on bail pending the determination of the charge. They anchored their bail applications on the provisions of sections 35(4) and 36(5) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, as well as sections 158 and 162 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015. The civil servants who were docked alongside Adeyemi on Wednesday are Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe. All the defendants, including Adeyemi, pleaded ill health, even as they pledged to make themselves available for trial. However, the prosecution counsel urged the court to refuse their bail requests and order an accelerated hearing of the case. item.content:encoded: … as defendants plead not guilty, beg for bail By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) said on Wednesday that it kept the self-styled Director-General (DG) of the alleged “non-existent” Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Prince Adeniyi Adeyemi, in custody for his own safety. According to the Commission, many of those allegedly defrauded by the defendant, a number of whom have filed petitions against him, are capable of physically harming him on sight. It therefore prayed the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), sitting at Maitama in Abuja, to reject an application that Adeyemi filed to be released on bail pending the determination of the criminal charge against him. “My lord, the defendant is facing allegations of obtaining by false pretence. “There are many petitions against him, and the people who lodged those petitions are after him. “There is this particular man from Ibadan whom he defrauded, which formed part of the counts in the charge. He has been seriously searching for him. “We believe that it will be in his own best interest to remain in custody for safekeeping,” the prosecution counsel, Mr. Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, added. The ICPC urged the court to also deny bail to four civil servants who are facing trial alongside the alleged fake PFIPC DG. The anti-corruption agency took the position after the defendants pleaded not guilty to a 36-count amended charge it entered against them. All the defendants, through their respective lawyers, begged the court to release them on bail pending the determination of the charge. They anchored their bail applications on the provisions of sections 35(4) and 36(5) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, as well as sections 158 and 162 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015. The civil servants who were docked alongside Adeyemi on Wednesday are Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe. All the defendants, including Adeyemi, pleaded ill health, even as they pledged to make themselves available for trial. However, the prosecution counsel urged the court to refuse their bail requests and order an accelerated hearing of the case. The ICPC specifically alleged that Adeyemi posed a flight risk, insisting he had enough funds at his disposal and the capacity to influence some of the proposed witnesses in the matter. Meanwhile, in urging the court to grant him bail on very liberal terms, Adeyemi, through his counsel, Mr. Ibrahim Angulu, SAN, told the court that, contrary to the prosecution’s claim, all his bank accounts had been frozen. “My lord, the accounts of the defendant were frozen, including those of his wives. They have all been frozen. So he does not have the means to escape or to influence the witnesses,” Adeyemi’s lawyer insisted. Trial Justice Halilu Yusuf adjourned the case until November 30 to rule on the defendant’s bail applications, as well as for the commencement of trial. While the court ordered the remand of all the male defendants in the Kuje correctional facility, it directed that the two female defendants be taken to the Suleja correctional facility. The ICPC alleged that Adeyemi, while passing himself off as a public servant, obtained over N27 billion to start the fake agency. He was also alleged to have dubiously obtained another N3.8 billion for personnel costs. The prosecution told the court that Adeyemi also obtained funds through a forged document addressed to the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy. It alleged that the defendant forged documents purportedly signed by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, which he claimed appointed him Director-General of PFIPC, and used them to occupy government office facilities at the Federal Secretariat Complex Phase III, Abuja. Besides, Adeyemi was accused of forging a document addressed to the Accountant-General of the Federation, captioned “RE: REQUEST FOR APPROVAL OF SELF-ACCOUNTING STATUS,” for the non-existent agency to operate within the government financial reporting structure. He was said to have forwarded forged documents to the DG of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) to get a domain name for the agency. The defendant was also accused of gifting N210,000, without official authorisation, to one of his co-defendants, Abdullahi, an Assistant Chief Technical Officer in the Office of the Secretary General of the Federation (OSGF), “to facilitate the allocation of office space.” He allegedly gifted another N300,000 to another co-defendant, Harry, an officer in the Office of the Chief Economic Adviser to the President, to facilitate the release and handover of two official vehicles, a Prado SUV and a Land Cruiser SUV, to him. Other counts in the charge included an allegation that on July 29, 2025, the defendant collected N20 million from one Oyekunle Gbenga, the Managing Director of Divine Dopacy Nigeria Limited, under the false pretence of a “project facilitation loan” for a purported N2.8 billion contract allegedly awarded by the fictitious agency for the procurement of furniture and renovation of the official residence of the DG of the said non-existent PFIPC. The ICPC insisted that he committed the offences between 2024 and 2026. He was said to have contravened Sections 364, 366 and 132 of the Penal Code Cap. 532, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (Abuja) 1990; Section 1(1)(a) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006, punishable under Section 1(3); and Section 9(a) of the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act, 2000, punishable under Section 9(b). Adeyemi, who has been in detention since July 14, was previously arraigned before the court on October 29. His re-arraignment on Wednesday followed the amendment of the charge to include the names of the four civil servants identified as his accomplices. The Federal High Court in Abuja had on October 12 struck out an initial eight-count charge that the Nigeria Police Force had filed against the first defendant, Adeyemi. The matter was terminated after it was withdrawn by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice. item.title: Nigeria still yearns for visionary leaders like Nnamdi Azikiwe – Abaribe
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – Senator Enyinnaya Abaribe representing Abia South Senator District, has praised the leadership philosophy of Nigeria’s first President, the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, lamenting that the country is still struggling to find leaders capable of providing the kind of purposeful leadership championed by the late nationalist He stated that Azikiwe demonstrated exemplary leadership through his emphasis on education, social reorientation, freedom, infrastructural development and visionary thinking, which he used as instruments for shaping society and advancing national development. Senator Abaribe who made the remarks during the 14th edition of the Zik Lecture Series held under the theme, “Zik’s Vision for Renaissance: Lessons from Emerging Economies in Africa”, identified himself as a student of Zik’s leadership philosophy, noting that the late statesman represented a generation of leaders whose political influence was guided by clear principles and a strong commitment to societal transformation. According to Abaribe, “leadership, as demonstrated by Azikiwe, went beyond the acquisition of political power to include the effective use of available resources and opportunities to influence the direction of a people”. He expressed concern that several African countries, particularly Nigeria, had continued to search for leaders committed to the principles of purposeful governance long after Azikiwe’s departure. Highlighting some of the challenges confronting Nigeria, the lawmaker identified weaknesses in the education sector, the growing divide between moral and immoral values, uncontrolled exposure to social media and the breakdown of family structures as issues requiring urgent attention. He, however, expressed optimism that recognising and acknowledging these problems would constitute an important step towards finding lasting solutions. Abaribe explained that his intention was not necessarily to provide immediate solutions but to draw attention to the deep-rooted challenges confronting the country and the African continent. He urged Nigerians to reflect deeply on the situation and take deliberate steps towards breaking the cycle of societal problems. Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Prof. Okechukwu Bond Anyiehie, described the theme of the lecture as timely and relevant to the country’s quest for development. Anyaehie noted that universities should not be seen merely as institutions for awarding academic degrees but as centres for generating ideas capable of driving societal transformation. Addressing the graduating students, whom he fondly referred to as Great Zikites, the Vice-Chancellor urged them to carry forward the ideals of courage, intellectual excellence, scholarship and Pan-Africanism associated with the late Azikiwe. item.content:encoded: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – Senator Enyinnaya Abaribe representing Abia South Senator District, has praised the leadership philosophy of Nigeria’s first President, the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, lamenting that the country is still struggling to find leaders capable of providing the kind of purposeful leadership championed by the late nationalist He stated that Azikiwe demonstrated exemplary leadership through his emphasis on education, social reorientation, freedom, infrastructural development and visionary thinking, which he used as instruments for shaping society and advancing national development. Senator Abaribe who made the remarks during the 14th edition of the Zik Lecture Series held under the theme, “Zik’s Vision for Renaissance: Lessons from Emerging Economies in Africa”, identified himself as a student of Zik’s leadership philosophy, noting that the late statesman represented a generation of leaders whose political influence was guided by clear principles and a strong commitment to societal transformation. According to Abaribe, “leadership, as demonstrated by Azikiwe, went beyond the acquisition of political power to include the effective use of available resources and opportunities to influence the direction of a people”. He expressed concern that several African countries, particularly Nigeria, had continued to search for leaders committed to the principles of purposeful governance long after Azikiwe’s departure. Highlighting some of the challenges confronting Nigeria, the lawmaker identified weaknesses in the education sector, the growing divide between moral and immoral values, uncontrolled exposure to social media and the breakdown of family structures as issues requiring urgent attention. He, however, expressed optimism that recognising and acknowledging these problems would constitute an important step towards finding lasting solutions. Abaribe explained that his intention was not necessarily to provide immediate solutions but to draw attention to the deep-rooted challenges confronting the country and the African continent. He urged Nigerians to reflect deeply on the situation and take deliberate steps towards breaking the cycle of societal problems. Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Prof. Okechukwu Bond Anyiehie, described the theme of the lecture as timely and relevant to the country’s quest for development. Anyaehie noted that universities should not be seen merely as institutions for awarding academic degrees but as centres for generating ideas capable of driving societal transformation. Addressing the graduating students, whom he fondly referred to as Great Zikites, the Vice-Chancellor urged them to carry forward the ideals of courage, intellectual excellence, scholarship and Pan-Africanism associated with the late Azikiwe. He challenged them to become worthy ambassadors of the university and uphold the vision of Zik’s renaissance in their various fields of endeavour. Speaking at the event, the wife of the late Nnamdi Azikiwe, Prof. Uche Azikiwe, expressed appreciation to the university management and Senator Ben Ndi Obi for establishing and sustaining the annual lecture series in honour of her late husband. She also expressed displeasure over what she described as persistent negative narratives about Azikiwe, stressing that no human being was perfect. According to her, rather than concentrating on perceived shortcomings in the life and leadership of the late nationalist, Nigerians should build on his achievements and continue the work of making the country better. She encouraged students to emulate her husband’s commitment to excellence by contributing positively to society and leaving behind legacies worthy of remembrance. Prof. Azikiwe further assured the university community of her continued support and willingness to participate in future celebrations organised in honour of the late statesman. Adviser Zik Lecture series, Prof. Au. Nonyelu and Chairman of the Local Organising Committee (LOC), Prof. Uju Ezenekwe in their separate remarks, thanked the benefactor of the lecture series, Chief Senator Ben Ndi Obi and all who strived to make the occasion a grand success. The annual lecture series remains an important platform for reflecting on the ideals, contributions and enduring legacy of one of Nigeria’s foremost nationalist leaders. The post Nigeria still yearns for visionary leaders like Nnamdi Azikiwe – Abaribe appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 1 light-day from Earth! NASA's Voyager 1 probe hits huge milestone in interstellar space
item.description: null NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is now one light-day from Earth — so far away that it takes signals a full 24 hours to reach the probe. Voyager 1 launched on Sept. 5, 1977, just a couple of weeks after Voyager 2 lifted off. But Voyager 1 launched on a faster trajectory than its twin and has just become the first spacecraft to ever reach one light-day away, which is equivalent to about 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), or the distance that one light particle travels in 24 hours. The milestone — which Voyager 1 hit today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) — shows the incredible ingenuity, technical ability and creativity from the teams at NASA that continue to innovate to keep this mission going nearly five decades later. "The Earth and Voyager are exactly 24 hours apart at the speed of light," Voyager Project Scientist Linda Spilker told Space.com. "It's a very special moment where Voyager 1 is about 16.1 billion miles away, and we're celebrating that moment because it's the first human-made object to actually reach one light-day distance." All things Voyager The two Voyager spacecraft have been on one serious ride since launching in 1977. And each of these twin probes has taken a unique and historic journey through our solar system and beyond. On Voyager 1's trip through our cosmic neighborhood, for example, it made countless groundbreaking observations of planets and moons that we had never before seen up close (or at all). The probe discovered a ring around Jupiter as well as the planet's moons Thebe and Metis. It also found five new moons and a new ring around Saturn. "Voyager 1 flew past the Jupiter system and took images of Jupiter's moon Io, and it actually discovered that Io is volcanically active. So, images that were taken showed these volcanoes that were actively erupting, and we learned that Io is actually the most volcanically active body in our solar system, which is just amazing," Cynthia Phillips, a project scientist for NASA's Europa Clipper mission, told Space.com about one of Voyager 1's many discoveries. item.content:encoded: null NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is now one light-day from Earth — so far away that it takes signals a full 24 hours to reach the probe. Voyager 1 launched on Sept. 5, 1977, just a couple of weeks after Voyager 2 lifted off. But Voyager 1 launched on a faster trajectory than its twin and has just become the first spacecraft to ever reach one light-day away, which is equivalent to about 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), or the distance that one light particle travels in 24 hours. The milestone — which Voyager 1 hit today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) — shows the incredible ingenuity, technical ability and creativity from the teams at NASA that continue to innovate to keep this mission going nearly five decades later. "The Earth and Voyager are exactly 24 hours apart at the speed of light," Voyager Project Scientist Linda Spilker told Space.com. "It's a very special moment where Voyager 1 is about 16.1 billion miles away, and we're celebrating that moment because it's the first human-made object to actually reach one light-day distance." All things Voyager The two Voyager spacecraft have been on one serious ride since launching in 1977. And each of these twin probes has taken a unique and historic journey through our solar system and beyond. On Voyager 1's trip through our cosmic neighborhood, for example, it made countless groundbreaking observations of planets and moons that we had never before seen up close (or at all). The probe discovered a ring around Jupiter as well as the planet's moons Thebe and Metis. It also found five new moons and a new ring around Saturn. "Voyager 1 flew past the Jupiter system and took images of Jupiter's moon Io, and it actually discovered that Io is volcanically active. So, images that were taken showed these volcanoes that were actively erupting, and we learned that Io is actually the most volcanically active body in our solar system, which is just amazing," Cynthia Phillips, a project scientist for NASA's Europa Clipper mission, told Space.com about one of Voyager 1's many discoveries. The Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 probes both flew past Jupiter in 1979, on their way out of the solar system. Represented here is Voyager 2's encounter with Jupiter. NASA/JPL A close-up of Jupiter's Great Red Spot as seen by one of NASA's Voyager spacecraft. NASA/JPL-Caltech Voyager 1 took photos of Jupiter and two of its satellites (Io, left, and Europa). The new study says that moons orbiting a gas giant planet greater than 8 Jupiter masses could help astronomers detect a rogue planet. NASA/JPL A mosaic of Jupiter by Voyager 1. JPL Jupiter and two of its moons — Io, to the left, and Europa — as seen by Voyager 1 on Feb. 13, 1979. JPL/NASA Voyager 1 image of Jupiter's volcanic moon Io, showing the active plume of a volcano called Loki. NASA/JPL/USGS "And then, as Voyager 1 continued out to the Saturn system, it actually discovered that Saturn's large moon Titan has a very thick atmosphere surrounding it," she added. "So it's one of the only moons that has a thick atmosphere." Decades later, Voyager 1's data is still incredibly important for scientists studying the planets and moons of our cosmic neighborhood. Phillips works on Clipper, which is on its way to study Jupiter's ocean moon Europa. And the basis of that work stems from early observations by Voyager. "Every time I get to use data from Voyager, I have to kind of think back to where that data came from," Phillips said. "I think about kind of the legacy, the missions that really set the precedent for a mission like Europa Clipper. Voyager is right there at the top of the list. And some of those images that we took with the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft of Europa — they're actually still, for some portions of Europa, they're the best pictures that we have. So, we're still using that data today, almost 50 years later." Today, Voyager 1 and 2 are both exploring interstellar space. On Aug. 25, 2012, Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to leave the heliosphere, or the protective bubble of solar particles that surrounds the planets and other objects in our solar system. After crossing that boundary, Voyager 1 entered interstellar space and has been exploring the interstellar medium ever since. Voyager 2 followed suit in November 2018. While the Voyager spacecraft have left the heliosphere, they have technically not left the solar system, as they are still within the gravitational influence of the sun. Today, Voyager 1 is traveling 38,000 mph (61,155 kph) through interstellar space, exploring farther than any human-made object in history. You need patience The Voyager mission team communicates with Voyager in radio waves via the Deep Space Network, a collective of giant radio antennas that NASA uses to "talk" to a wide range of far-off spacecraft. And since radio waves travel at the speed of light, it now takes 24 hours for communications to reach Voyager 1, and then another 24 hours for any response to return. The Canberra Complex of the Deep Space Network located in Australia. (Image credit: NASA) "You need to have patience because now, if you send a command to Voyager, Voyager receives that command 24 hours later," Spilker said. "So two days later, you receive confirmation that yes, Voyager one received your command and is sending back the information that you'd like it to send back." That patience is important, as the nearly-50-year-old Voyager mission is still actively making science observations and collecting new data. While some of the probes' science instruments have had to be shut off over the years to save battery life, both probes are still going strong. "It is always difficult when an instrument has to get turned off, knowing that it has returned good science data for so many years," Spilker said. "But a plan was laid down to make sure we had at least one instrument operating on each spacecraft, one type of instrument, for as long as we could." As long as the mission is active, the team will continue to investigate the unknown with Voyager. After all, ever since the probes entered interstellar space, they have been exploring areas of space that we've only ever studied remotely or in theory. An illustration showing how NASA's Hubble Space Telescope looks along the paths of NASA's Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft as they have traveled through the solar system and into interstellar space. (Image credit: NASA, ESA, and Z. Levay (STScI)) "Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause in 2012, and what we knew about interstellar space at that point really came just from remote observations and theories. And so, right away, Voyager started to find that what we expected was not exactly right," Spilker said. So far, the team has found that the sun's influence extends much farther from the heliopause than they expected. The Voyagers have observed and measured "ripples coming from the sun," as Spilker described them, deep in interstellar space. "Voyager is going to continue to measure the cosmic rays and particles, and also the radio waves coming from interstellar space and coming from the sun," Spilker said, adding that the team is always eagerly "waiting to see if there might be more surprises out there." An enduring legacy How has this mission from the 1970s continued to not just survive but actively push forward through all of that time, overcoming countless hurdles and unexpected challenges? "Voyager's longevity is really a tribute to all of the people who worked on Voyager, from those who designed the spacecraft, built it, programmed its computers, launched it, and then the teams of individuals that have flown it over that 50 years," Spilker said. Spilker is a longtimeVoyager veteran. Fresh out of school, she started her NASA career with Voyager, working on the mission for about a decade before moving on to NASA's Cassini Saturn mission. item.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations!
item.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. The post Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations! appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.description: More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time . Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans. But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players. “Our team has the opportunity to make history a second time this month.” GTA VI is great — and I’m not the only one who thinks so. Grand Theft Auto VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype ‘It’s a risk’: How Rockstar built the most detailed (and romantic) GTA yet If you want to play GTA VI on PS5 tonight, download yesterday’s firmware update first. item.title: UK.gov JV gets £178M Home Office hosting deal. Without competition
item.description: The Home Office has awarded a contract worth £178 million to a public-private hosting services joint venture - without competition - to support critical national infrastructure. According to a notice published last week , Crown Hosting Data Centres (CHDC) won the seven-year contract to support "essential national infrastructure underpinning the Home Office's most critical systems, including border security, the Police National Computer (PNC), and core intelligence environments." CHDC is a joint venture between the Cabinet Office, which owns 25 percent, and Ark Data Centres Ltd, which owns the rest. It was set up in 2015 for the express purpose of providing hosting services for the government. The award was made through an existing framework agreement, set up in February 2022, awarded to CHDC without competition via a Voluntary Ex-Ante Transparency Notice . The service is set to support Critical National Infrastructure, although the notice does not reveal specific services requested. Mention of continued support for the Police National Computer may raise eyebrows. The Home Office is managing the transition of the aging legacy system to the Law Enforcement Data Service (LEDS) under the National Law Enforcement Data Program (NLEDP). A notice in December 2024 said that the Home Office was "focused on the development and adoption of LEDS products to replace existing PNC capability across all police forces and other non-policing PNC consumers, enabling the retirement by March 2026 (the point at which PNC support will expire)." The government had previously set a target of decommissioning the PNC in 2022. The Register has asked the Home Office to clarify why Crown Hosting support is necessary beyond this date. The PNC – which is based on mainframe technology dating from the 1970s – was at the center of a scandal in 2021 when a technology failure led to the loss of 413,000 records of evidence . The incident, which left then Prime Minister Boris Johnson floundering in Parliament, was the result of a scripting error in code designed to weed out records to be deleted from the PNC, a system running on a Fujitsu BS2000/OSD SE700-30 mainframe-based at a datacenter in Hendon, London. In 2022, the Cabinet Office awarded a contract worth up to £250 million to CHDC, also without outside competition. ®
