item.title: 'We are not robots': Mauricio Pochettino's emotional USMNT goodbye was anything but business as usual
item.description: CINCINNATI — Mauricio Pochettino went through Tuesday's U.S. match like every other during his two-year spell. "It was a normal game," he said. "You are focused. You want to concentrate. You want to win. You want to help the players perform." And then the end came — the end of a 2-0 victory over Haiti , the end of a two-leg CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal that completed an 8-0 aggregate wipeout, and the end of a 37-match tenure that saw advances in the program at large but also disappointment in not advancing deeper at the World Cup. When it was over at TQL Stadium, the finality of it all hit Pochettino hard. He's passionate about people and soccer. While his decision to sign with Manchester United was purely business, his emotions about leaving behind a tight group were genuine. "When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things," he said. "Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything." There were hugs and tears, both on the field and in the locker room. "It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us," he said. "When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are not robots." Mauricio Pochettino and members of the team staff pose for a picture on the pitch after the victory over Haiti in a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal match at TQL Stadium. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS Captain Tyler Adams observed, "He fell in love with the country. That's first and foremost, the most important thing. He didn't know exactly what to expect when he took the job. He fell in love with the people. He fell in love with the football, and he fell in love with our team. That's special." item.dc:creator: Steven Goff
item.content:encoded: CINCINNATI — Mauricio Pochettino went through Tuesday's U.S. match like every other during his two-year spell. "It was a normal game," he said. "You are focused. You want to concentrate. You want to win. You want to help the players perform." And then the end came — the end of a 2-0 victory over Haiti , the end of a two-leg CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal that completed an 8-0 aggregate wipeout, and the end of a 37-match tenure that saw advances in the program at large but also disappointment in not advancing deeper at the World Cup. When it was over at TQL Stadium, the finality of it all hit Pochettino hard. He's passionate about people and soccer. While his decision to sign with Manchester United was purely business, his emotions about leaving behind a tight group were genuine. "When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things," he said. "Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything." There were hugs and tears, both on the field and in the locker room. "It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us," he said. "When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are not robots." Mauricio Pochettino and members of the team staff pose for a picture on the pitch after the victory over Haiti in a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal match at TQL Stadium. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS Captain Tyler Adams observed, "He fell in love with the country. That's first and foremost, the most important thing. He didn't know exactly what to expect when he took the job. He fell in love with the people. He fell in love with the football, and he fell in love with our team. That's special." Adams and the rest of the team sent Pochettino off in style with six consecutive victories, including four shutouts in a row. "We wanted to finish in a good way," Pochettino said. "The way we play, that is what we dream of when we arrive. The team really enjoyed playing football, playing soccer." In the first half, Christian Pulisic scored on an audacious bicycle kick and teenager Julian Hall continued the torrid start to his international career by scoring for the fifth time in six matches. Weston McKennie set up both goals. "It was a pretty bad cross, to be honest. I had to save him," Pulisic joked about his longtime friend's assist. "I saw it and I had to go for it. It was cool; it was special." Asked if he too had ever scored such a goal, McKennie said, "I've had side volleys, never bikes. I don't know if I'd survive the fall after that." The postgame mood was light, fun and emotional; it was human. Pochettino had fostered a positive, engaging environment that took hold last year and carried through the World Cup over the summer and into this fall. "It's a little bit sad Mauricio is departing, but as a team, we're going to continue to stick together," Hall said. "We're just waiting for what's ahead in the future." Reflecting on his tenure, Pochettino said he wished he had had more time in the buildup to the World Cup. The way the players performed at the tournament, he said, should have been how they performed six months before it. From there, he said, the team would have hit full capacity at the World Cup. He did, though, have them playing well through his finale. "It's a good way to end," Pulisic said, "and send him off in a good manner like that." Pochettino believes the U.S. is on the right path. "I am sure this group of players will achieve big things in the future, I have no doubt," he said. "Experienced players with the talent that is coming, it's the perfect combination." Who's got next? The U.S. Soccer Federation has begun the process of identifying candidates to replace Pochettino, who, after the game, was off to the airport to fly to England and begin work with a storied Premier League club that's off to its worst start in 40 years. The next official U.S. matches will come at the Nations League final four in late March. By then, the USSF would like to have a coach in place. "I don't think someone's going to come in and completely change everything we have going on here," Pulisic said. "There's a lot of positives, and hopefully he can help steer us in the right direction." What kind of coach is the star forward looking for? "Someone who can just continue to build off this culture we have. We have a really good starting place — having a good identity, finding ourselves and what we're going to look like moving forward in the next [few] years and going into the next World Cup." McKennie said he would like "someone that's ambitious, someone that's open-minded, someone that can gel with the group, has a good relationship with players, and believes in the youth as well." Pochettino said he would be happy to provide advice, should the federation need it. "For sure, they are not going to ask me because they have the capacity," he said. Then, with a devilish grin, he added, "More than two years ago they signed [women's coach] Emma Hayes and Mauricio Pochettino. I think they have good eyes!"

item.title: Victor Wembanyama’s ridiculous self-assisted dunk steals the show despite Spurs’ 105-93 loss to Pistons
item.description: Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images Victor Wembanyama produced another highlight-reel moment against the Detroit Pistons, throwing the ball off the backboard before catching it and finishing with a one-handed dunk. The San Antonio Spurs star used his incredible height and creativity to get past Ausar Thompson early in their meeting with Detroit. Wembanyama had already been blocked by one of the Thompson twins this season, but he found a different way to attack the basket this time. Victor Wembanyama’s self-assisted dunk steals the show against Detroit Pistons The 22-year-old drove towards the paint just over a minute into the game before sensing pressure from Thompson. Rather than force his way through the defence, Wembanyama threw the ball against the backboard, collected it in the air and threw down a one-handed finish. It was a reminder of the unusual skills that make the Frenchman such a difficult player to defend. At 7-foot-4, Wembanyama has the size to dominate near the rim, but his ability to improvise makes him even more dangerous. He entered the contest averaging 28.6 points and 11.6 rebounds through 14 appearances, ranking third and fifth in the NBA in those categories respectively. However, the highlight did not tell the full story of the night for San Antonio. Despite Wembanyama finishing with 25 points and 18 rebounds, the Spurs fell to a 105-93 defeat against Detroit at the Frost Bank Center. Dylan Harper added 20 points, while Julian Champagnie scored 14. Detroit also had the final say in the battle of the big moments, with Cade Cunningham producing a poster dunk over Wembanyama near the end of the first quarter. The defeat leaves San Antonio with a 12-3 record after starting the season strongly. item.title: Raptors Lose 15th Straight To Knicks: 4 Takeaways From Eastern Conference Thriller
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Just two nights removed from their overtime loss on Sunday , the Toronto Raptors had a chance to set things right with a rematch against the New York Knicks . This time, to their credit, the Raptors came out firing with a 29-point first quarter that took the champs by surprise. By the end, however, it was the Knicks that overwhelmed, riding the play of their stars to win their second straight game (111-102) and 15th straight against the Raptors in particular. As usual, Jalen Brunson led the way for New York. In 34 minutes, he finished with 31 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 45.5% shooting from the field (4-11 from three). At shooting guard, Mikal Bridges dropped 17 points, five rebounds, and one assist on 63.6% shooting from the field (2-5 from three), while center Karl-Anthony Towns dropped 16 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists, and one steal on 77.8% shooting from the field (1-2 from three). For the Raptors, Ja’Kobe Walter led the way with 25 points, one rebound, two assists, and two steals on 60.0% shooting from the field (7-12 from three). Veteran swingman RJ Barrett , meanwhile, contributed 22 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 52.9% shooting from the field (2-8 from three). Finally, there’s Scottie Barnes : 20 points, four rebounds, two assists, and two blocks on 50.0% shooting (1-2 from three). Whether it was the support of their home crowd or the desperation of not wanting to lose to the same team in back-to-back games, the Raptors came out with a lot of energy in this game, playing with an almost desperate urgency during the early minutes of the game. Eventually, though, that urgency turned to frustration as the Knicks got increasingly comfortable and expanded their lead down the stretch. In the grand scheme of things, this game likely won’t be remembered for long, but it told us a lot about where these teams are headed going into the Holiday season (NBA Christmas and Cup Finals). For the Knicks especially, it’s a step in the right direction that could signal an upcoming shift in the hierarchy. 1. item.content:encoded: Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Just two nights removed from their overtime loss on Sunday , the Toronto Raptors had a chance to set things right with a rematch against the New York Knicks . This time, to their credit, the Raptors came out firing with a 29-point first quarter that took the champs by surprise. By the end, however, it was the Knicks that overwhelmed, riding the play of their stars to win their second straight game (111-102) and 15th straight against the Raptors in particular. As usual, Jalen Brunson led the way for New York. In 34 minutes, he finished with 31 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 45.5% shooting from the field (4-11 from three). At shooting guard, Mikal Bridges dropped 17 points, five rebounds, and one assist on 63.6% shooting from the field (2-5 from three), while center Karl-Anthony Towns dropped 16 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists, and one steal on 77.8% shooting from the field (1-2 from three). For the Raptors, Ja’Kobe Walter led the way with 25 points, one rebound, two assists, and two steals on 60.0% shooting from the field (7-12 from three). Veteran swingman RJ Barrett , meanwhile, contributed 22 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 52.9% shooting from the field (2-8 from three). Finally, there’s Scottie Barnes : 20 points, four rebounds, two assists, and two blocks on 50.0% shooting (1-2 from three). Whether it was the support of their home crowd or the desperation of not wanting to lose to the same team in back-to-back games, the Raptors came out with a lot of energy in this game, playing with an almost desperate urgency during the early minutes of the game. Eventually, though, that urgency turned to frustration as the Knicks got increasingly comfortable and expanded their lead down the stretch. In the grand scheme of things, this game likely won’t be remembered for long, but it told us a lot about where these teams are headed going into the Holiday season (NBA Christmas and Cup Finals). For the Knicks especially, it’s a step in the right direction that could signal an upcoming shift in the hierarchy. 1. Mikal Bridges Is Back To say Mikal Bridges was struggling this season would be an understatement. He looked borderline unplayable at times, and head coach Mike Brown was facing growing calls to bench him . He started showing signs of life against the Pacers on Friday (18 points in 28 minutes), and he showed a familiar spark in today’s win, finishing with 17 points, five rebounds, and one assist on 63.6% shooting from the field and 40.0% shooting from three. Bridges held a steady rhythm all game, and that’s when the Knicks are at their best. Of course, even when Bridges was at his worst offensively, he still made a positive impact on defense. Tonight, that defensive touch was massive in containing the Raptors’ shooting and regularly contesting their attempts. Bridges was active on this end throughout the game, making that quiet impact even when he wasn’t scoring. It’s unclear what had Bridges in such a funk to begin with, but everything is easier for the Knicks when he’s making shots. By easing pressure off Brunson, spacing the floor, and punishing teams for leaving him open, it answers so many problems, and we saw how it worked out for them against the Raptors. 2. Knicks Own The Clutch If there’s one specific time when the Knicks are prone to elevate their game, it’s the fourth quarter. Tonight, after stumbling through most of the first half, they sealed the deal with a 31-point fourth quarter that ultimately decided the game. New York’s best moments came in the final three minutes, when Brunson single-handedly willed his team to victory after making a four-point play to put them up by four. Even Mikal got in on the action, delivering a dagger three with roughly 45 seconds left. The Knicks started the season 1-6 in clutch games, but we can assume that was an outlier now. As we were reminded today, this team is loaded with players who are not afraid of the moment. When the pressure was highest, they played with a sense of calm and poise, leading to smart decisions and crisp passes that always found their man. At this point, the Knicks have seen it all together, and they aren’t fazed by the pressure. What makes the Knicks so hard to beat is that they only get better in the clutch, and it’s not just Brunson who beats you. Tonight, practically everyone had their moment, highlighting the depth and versatility of the defending champions. 3. Kawhi Will Not Save The Raptors As Kawhi Leonard deals with swelling in his left knee, his status remains a mystery , leaving the Raptors without their best player. They clearly missed him tonight, but how much will his return actually change for this team? Other than Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett, the Raptors don’t have nearly enough depth or talent to keep up with the likes of the 76ers, Celtics, or Pistons in the East. They traded away their best perimeter scorer ( Brandon Ingram ) and gave up a promising young athlete in Gradey Dick. What the Raptors really lack is a center. Jakob Poeltl came off the bench tonight in favor of Collin Murray-Boyles , who finished with just eight points, one rebound, three assists, one steal, and three blocks on 66.7% shooting from the field. Sensing their advantage in the frontcourt, the Knicks were feasting inside, going in for easy layups and controlling the glass for a 44-23 rebounding advantage. While there’s no doubt the Raptors will be better off for Kawhi’s return, they cannot rely on him to come back and just resolve their issues. To salvage this season, more proactive measures are required, and the options are limitless. 4. Shamet Minutes Are Key The Knicks’ bench was a cause for concern going into the season, and it didn’t build confidence when their best bench scorer from last season ( Jordan Clarkson ) started seeing reduced minutes. Fortunately, veteran Landry Shamet has been filling the role just fine, and he gave the Knicks another fine showing tonight. In 24 minutes off the bench, he put up 12 points, one rebound, and one assist on 57.1% shooting from the field (2-4 from three). As the Raptors struggled to get anything from their second unit, Landry Shamet carried the Knicks’ bench to ensure his team never lost momentum. His versatility let him fit into various lineups, and he made few mistakes while providing a steady boost on the court. So while Shamet may not be the hero Knicks fans were expecting, he’s becoming a big storyline for their turnaround this season, and his importance is undeniable. Ultimately, the Knicks will always lean more on their star-studded starting lineup, but having that boost off the bench makes everything easier. Tonight, we saw the impact Shamet could have (+26) and why we can expect to see more of him over the course of the season.

item.title: Greenwich holds off Ridgefield for 4th straight Class LL girls swimming title, 33rd overall
item.description: Greenwich is ready to dive into the pool at the Cornerstone Aquatics Center in West Hartford after capturing the Class LL girls swimming championship on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) WEST HARTFORD - The Greenwich and Ridgefield girls swimming and diving programs have engaged in plenty of battles over the years, and the CIAC Class LL championship meet on Tuesday night at the Cornerstone Aquatics Center was no different. For the Cardinals, depth turned out to be key as they captured their fourth straight Class LL title and 33rd overall in program history. Greenwich scored 924 points to second-place Ridgefield's 878.5. Amity was third with 510.5 points. "I felt pretty confident going into this because I knew that everyone on the team has been working super hard, and I had a lot of faith in us," Greenwich junior Olivia DeVries said. With sophomore Alden Charette's first-place finish in Class LL diving, the Cardinals won three individual events and one relay. Seniors Kensie Worden (50 freestyle, 23.59) and Julia Kozma (100 butterfly, 57.70) won gold medals, as did the opening 200 medley relay team of Charette, junior Sara Jee, Kozma and Worden (1:47.96). Greenwich claimed 18 individual medals, including three golds, three silvers and three bronzes. DeVries claimed bronze medals in the 200 freestyle and 500 freestyle. "I'm super proud of the team because we all have worked so hard in practice. The captains have done such a good job to keep us motivated and I'm just very proud of how hard we worked," DeVries said. "Every single swimmer made a difference, every single spot. If you were in the C final, the A final, everyone makes a difference. We are all cheering for each other, and I think that's what makes Greenwich special." "We had some really great swims from all the girls, but especially our senior class," Greenwich coach Megan Kelly said. "I think it really means a lot to them, and to see them swim with such heart was really great." Senior Ellison Charette was second in the 200 IM and 500 freestyle, and she was part of the second-place 200 and 400 freestyle relay teams. "Ellison, she fought hard in both of her races. She had some really good swims. Overall, I was really, really pleased," Kelly said. "They didn't win the (200) free relay, but they went 1:35, which is All-American consideration time. That was pretty impressive." Greenwich's second-place 200 freestyle relay finished in 1:35.79. Ridgefield's first-place relay of sophomore Zsofia Milak, senior Dalia Katra, sophomore Mary Kelly and junior Ellie Griffin swam the race in 1:35.21, which broke Ridgefield's 2022 state record of 1:35.48. Milak had a terrific night for Ridgefield, winning individual gold medals in the 200 freestyle (1:50.20) and 100 freestyle (50.95). She was also part of the first-place 400 freestyle relay (3:32.60), along with Kelly, junior Chloe Archibald and sophomore Charlie Palmer. Kelly won the 500 freestyle in 4:59.44. Norwalk/McMahon

item.title: Waterford heading to boys soccer CIAC final for first time since 1987
item.description: The Waterford boys soccer team and its student section celebrate their 2-0 victory over Daniel Hand in the CIAC Class M semifinals at Valley Regional High School in Deep River on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. The Lancers advance to their first state final since 1987. (Bryant Carpenter/Hearst Connecticut Media) DEEP RIVER - Waterford boys soccer coach Jeff Emerich was grooving when he heard "Jump" by Kris Kross hip-hopping over the Valley Regional PA at halftime of Tuesday night's CIAC Class M semifinal between his No. 1-seeded Lancers and No. 5 Daniel Hand. Emerich knew, too, that if his boys executed a little more criss-cross on the pitch, they'd be jumping Waterford boys soccer into a state final for the first time since 1987, about five years before Chris "Mac Daddy" Kelly and Chris "Daddy Mac" Smith arrived on the scene. Yeah, it all goes back a ways, and it's funny what stands the test of time. This Waterford boys soccer team of 2026 is proving to be one for the ages. With a 2-0 victory over Hand on Tuesday night, in a game that showcased the breadth of their remarkable skill set, the Lancers are one step away from the first-ever boys soccer championship in Waterford history. Brady Wiseman scored off a left-side cross from Brayden Michonski two minutes into the second half and Jaydev Villa, set up by an inexorable upfield rush by Yaman Qarqour, added insurance with 20:35 to play as Waterford improved to 19-1-1 and advances to this weekend's state championship at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford to face No. 2 Weston, which dethroned reigning champ Tolland 1-0 in Tuesday's other Class M semi. "It's been since 1987 since the last time we made it in, so this is our first chance to go up and compete," Emerich said. "We've never won a state title, and it's been 39 years since we've seen a chance, so we are very humbled that we are able to do this, and we continue to work, and that's the thing that makes these boys special." The Lancers got an emotional boost on Monday when they learned goalie Luke Wilson was cleared from a concussion suffered in the ECC tournament semifinals against Bacon Academy. Wilson set the tone Tuesday night by charging out and sliding to break up a Hand scoring chance in the opening minute for the first of his 16 saves. "I didn't even know if I was going to be able to play this game, especially last week, watching when we played Lewis Mills (in the quarterfinals), I was still nervous," Wilson said. "All I wanted to do was get back on the field." Wilson wore a foam helmet for the first time Tuesday night. The Lancers advance to their first state final since 1987. (Bryant Carpenter/Hearst Connecticut Media) DEEP RIVER - Waterford boys soccer coach Jeff Emerich was grooving when he heard "Jump" by Kris Kross hip-hopping over the Valley Regional PA at halftime of Tuesday night's CIAC Class M semifinal between his No. 1-seeded Lancers and No. 5 Daniel Hand. Emerich knew, too, that if his boys executed a little more criss-cross on the pitch, they'd be jumping Waterford boys soccer into a state final for the first time since 1987, about five years before Chris "Mac Daddy" Kelly and Chris "Daddy Mac" Smith arrived on the scene. Yeah, it all goes back a ways, and it's funny what stands the test of time. This Waterford boys soccer team of 2026 is proving to be one for the ages. "It's been since 1987 since the last time we made it in, so this is our first chance to go up and compete," Emerich said. "We've never won a state title, and it's been 39 years since we've seen a chance, so we are very humbled that we are able to do this, and we continue to work, and that's the thing that makes these boys special." The Lancers got an emotional boost on Monday when they learned goalie Luke Wilson was cleared from a concussion suffered in the ECC tournament semifinals against Bacon Academy. Wilson set the tone Tuesday night by charging out and sliding to break up a Hand scoring chance in the opening minute for the first of his 16 saves. "I didn't even know if I was going to be able to play this game, especially last week, watching when we played Lewis Mills (in the quarterfinals), I was still nervous," Wilson said. "All I wanted to do was get back on the field." Wilson wore a foam helmet for the first time Tuesday night. The rest was very much the same look for a Waterford team that has now scored 94 goals and allowed just 13 on the season. The first half was fairly even, with both teams generating scoring chances. In the second half, the pitch decidedly tilted Waterford's way. Once Wiseman converted that cross from Michonski, a stiff challenge for Hand grew steeper. The Tigers, the last SCC team in the boys soccer state tourney, ended their season at 16-5-1. "I thought our team came out and executed our game plan in the first half really, really well," said Hand coach Mike Shirley. "It was always going to be a game decided by one-versus-one moments, and we knew we had to defend them on the edges, and it was just about, 'Can we find our opportunities and put them in the back of the net before they can?'" The Tigers could not, and with it passed their chance to return to the state finals for the first time since the grand slam championship run of 2016-2019. Dates and times for all state soccer finals will be announced later this week. Player of the Game Luke Wilson. Cleared from a concussion just one day before the game, Waterford's senior goalie opened the night with a sliding, charging stop to thwart a Hand scoring chance and punctuated the victory punching out a final shot in the final minute. Wilson had 16 saves in all. Quotable "Kudos to Waterford because they have some extremely talented players, and they also played a quality game " - Hand coach Mike Shirley. item.title: Gilbert Arenas claims ‘heartless’ Klay Thompson’s Megan Thee Stallion breakup led to resurgence
item.description: Photo by Raymond Hall/GC Images Klay Thompson is finding himself delivering at a level many fans got accustomed to during his prime with the Golden State Warriors. Earlier this year, Thompson ended his relationship with rapper Megan Thee Stallion, which became quite a pop culture controversy. And given how well Thompson is playing since joining the Miami Heat, Gilbert Arenas believes the breakup has helped him find his form again. Gilbert Arenas believes Klay Thompson is returning to form thanks to Megan Thee Stallion breakup Speaking on The Arena show, Gilbert Arenas spoke about Klay Thompson’s recent return to form from a shooting standpoint. Arenas suggests that the nature and fallout of his recent breakup with rapper Megan Thee Stallion has somehow given him the confidence he needs to once again become the elite shooter he once was. “One of the greatest shooters of all time not having his shot, when that’s what you do for a living… Sometimes, certain type of minds need certain things,” Arenas said. “I think the Megan Thee Stallion (situation), just watching someone like, ‘this is the worst break-up I’ve ever had,’ made him sleep good at night. The old Klay is back!” “Sometimes, in the movie, that killer has a soft spot, and he’s more vulnerable… He just lost his touch. When he’d seen that, and she was all distraught, he probably sat back like, ‘Yeah. This is me. When they’re crying at the doorstep, my shot is back!’ “I just really believe that’s all it took. Looking at the phone, talking about, ‘I hate your guts,’ and he’s thinking, ‘Yeah, I’m about to have 30 tonight!’ Everything is back. “Klay is back! The killer is back! Keep shooting the ball, baby, and keep breaking hearts! You’ve got to add that part to it. He shoots like he’s heartless! Gotta keep breaking hearts!” This season, Thompson is averaging 15.5 points, 2.1 assists, and 1.4 rebounds, while shooting 45.1% from the field and 43.4% from beyond the arc. Thompson has hit 50+ three-pointers in just 13 games this season, the fastest he has reached this mark at any point in his NBA career. item.title: Cade Cunningham makes a bold claim after leading the Pistons in snapping the Spurs' streak
item.description: Cade Cunningham makes a bold claim after leading the Pistons in snapping the Spurs' streak originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Heading into Tuesday's game between the Detroit Pistons and the San Antonio Spurs , the latter were the overwhelming favorites. The Pistons faced a tough game, especially without Duncan Robinson. However, the Pistons shocked the world by taking control and winning. They snapped the Spurs ' 12-game winning streak, and Cade Cunningham was at the center of it all. Cade Cunningham cements the Pistons as a top team once again As one of the best point guards in the NBA, Cunningham has proven to be a fantastic player for the Pistons. He has been their leader for a while now, and he is delivering on his potential from being drafted first overall in 2021. Since then, the Pistons have gone through all kinds of struggles, but also some solid successes. They were the first seed in the Eastern Conference in the 2025-26 season, but their early exit from the Playoffs has led to doubts. With this performance against the Spurs, the doubters were silenced. MORE: Cade Cunningham is calling out the people who doubted him and the Pistons Cunningham has affirmed that the Pistons are ready for the team to hit another level. They are ready to prove that they are still one of the best teams in the league, and they are ready to go toe-to-toe with the top teams like the Spurs. "It was a group effort; everybody had to bring it. I like my guys; we do this together every day. We love basketball; we all come from grit, to get to this point... Nobody in that locker room has fear in their heart for anybody," Cunningham said on the NBC broadcast after the big win . Winning against a team like the Spurs is a big achievement, and Cunningham was key to that. However, he is the first one to credit his team for helping him beat the Spurs, one of the toughest tasks any team has ths season. item.title: Bonkers Cutter Gauthier stats prove he is untouchable right now
item.description: Bonkers Cutter Gauthier stats prove he is untouchable right now appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images The Anaheim Ducks had a messy offseason that threatened to end their contention window before it began. So far this season, though, they have remained a competitive team. One major reason for this is star forward Cutter Gauthier . 🎩 HAT TRICK CUTTER GAUTHIER 🎩 It's a one-goal game! pic.twitter.com/Oag7IdmLHP — Anaheim Ducks (@AnaheimDucks) November 18, 2026 CUTTER GAUTHIER SCORES AGAIN. - 2nd of the night - 20th goal of the season (20 GP) - 18TH GOAL IN THE LAST 10 GAMES Simply INSANE 🤯😵‍💫 pic.twitter.com/QcR0EWSujo — Gino Hard (@GinoHard_) November 18, 2026 ANOTHER GAME, ANOTHER CUTTER GAUTHIER GOAL 🚨 pic.twitter.com/QPurBQfStp — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) November 18, 2026 Gauthier may be the hottest player in the league right now. On Tuesday, he scored his fourth hat trick in nine games in a chaotic loss to the St. Louis Blues. He made history as a result, becoming the first player in league history with four hat tricks in a calendar month, via Sportsnet Stats. But the extent of his run has gone even further than that. " Cutter Gauthier has scored 17 goals in November. That's more than the Boston Bruins, Detroit Red Wings, Columbus Blue Jackets, Buffalo Sabres, Calgary Flames, Pittsburgh Penguins, Toronto Maple Leafs or Seattle Kraken have scored in November," Associated Press reporter Greg Beacham noted on Tuesday night. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Gauthier has scored in each of his last 10 games. The last time he went without a goal was October 27 against the Vancouver Canucks. He now has 21 goals and 29 points on the season following the loss to the Blues. WHAT IS HAPPENING!?!? 🤯 Cutter Gauthier has himself ANOTHER hat trick! pic.twitter.com/l8LnIKR2q2 — NHL (@NHL) November 18, 2026 The Ducks star began his incredible run on November 1st. He scored back-to-back hat tricks to begin the month. His third hat trick of the month came on November 8 against the Pittsburgh Penguins. Click Above to Subscribe The Ducks still have six games remaining in the month of November. There is a chance the 22-year-old Gauthier can improve on his already incredible performance. We'll see if he can make it five hat tricks on the month when Anaheim takes on the Colorado Avalanche on Thursday.

item.title: Aljamain Sterling Reveals Umar Nurmagomedov’s Alleged Role in Yas Hilton Hotel Brawl With Merab Dvalishvili
item.description: The controversy surrounding the altercation at the Yas Hilton Hotel during RAF Abu Dhabi has taken another unexpected turn. The incident involved Merab Dvalishvili and Saba Lazishvili, who were confronted by Usman Nurmagomedov and members of his Dagestani entourage. Videos circulating online captured the moment the PFL champion approached Dvalishvili and slapped the Georgian fighter, setting off a mass brawl involving multiple individuals. Authorities subsequently detained all 10 people involved, with the group spending nearly 48 hours in custody. Dvalishvili and Lazishvili eventually walked free after reportedly receiving a $14,000 fine without any jail time. The outcome was harsher for the Dagestani contingent. Eight individuals, including Nurmagomedov, were reportedly handed six-month prison sentences , alongside an $82,000 fine and deportation orders to be enforced after their prison terms. Following a revision of the original ruling, all eight convicted Dagestanis have now been released , according to an update shared by the Abu Dhabi Criminal Court on X. While this development could appear to bring the legal proceedings to a close, the fallout from the hotel brawl may not be over just yet. Dvalishvili’s teammate and former UFC bantamweight champion, Aljamain Sterling, has revealed more harrowing details of the attack that were not captured on tape. First, Aljo slammed the Dagestani contingent for a cowardly attack. item.content:encoded: The controversy surrounding the altercation at the Yas Hilton Hotel during RAF Abu Dhabi has taken another unexpected turn. The incident involved Merab Dvalishvili and Saba Lazishvili, who were confronted by Usman Nurmagomedov and members of his Dagestani entourage. Videos circulating online captured the moment the PFL champion approached Dvalishvili and slapped the Georgian fighter, setting off a mass brawl involving multiple individuals. Authorities subsequently detained all 10 people involved, with the group spending nearly 48 hours in custody. Dvalishvili and Lazishvili eventually walked free after reportedly receiving a $14,000 fine without any jail time. The outcome was harsher for the Dagestani contingent. Eight individuals, including Nurmagomedov, were reportedly handed six-month prison sentences , alongside an $82,000 fine and deportation orders to be enforced after their prison terms. Following a revision of the original ruling, all eight convicted Dagestanis have now been released , according to an update shared by the Abu Dhabi Criminal Court on X. While this development could appear to bring the legal proceedings to a close, the fallout from the hotel brawl may not be over just yet. Dvalishvili’s teammate and former UFC bantamweight champion, Aljamain Sterling, has revealed more harrowing details of the attack that were not captured on tape. First, Aljo slammed the Dagestani contingent for a cowardly attack. In an interview with ESPN , Sterling did not hold back when discussing the incident, saying, “I wish I was there—me and the other boys—to see if they would have kept that same energy because they have this M.O. for doing this type of thing.” He further questioned the manner in which the Dagestani group confronted Dvalishvili, adding, “They don’t approach guys one-on-one, and I would have respected Usman if he would have done that, or established he has a problem, or him slapping Merab and establishing he had a problem. But to do that with a group of guys, it’s just soft. It’s just animalistic behavior.” However, Sterling’s biggest allegation concerned what happened after the cameras stopped recording. He claimed that Umar Nurmagomedov, who was absent from the viral footage circulating online, joined the altercation later and attacked Dvalishvili. Sterling said, “Umar was nowhere to be found, but after the camera turns off, Umar then comes up and punches Merab in the face.” ALSO READ: Conor McGregor Names Josh Hokit UFC’s Second-Biggest Draw After Star-Making War With Ciryl Gane The former champion also questioned Umar Nurmagomedov’s conduct during the aftermath of the initial confrontation, stating, “It looked like he was going to de-escalate the situation because this was after everything kind of settled down. What about this is respectable?” Sterling went on to describe the alleged off-camera events as particularly disturbing. He concluded, “I could have let the first clip that was shown on video go, but after I heard about everything that happened afterward — nah. To Umar walking up and doing what he did. Then them holding down Saba — pinning his arms so they could stomp his head. I think that’s attempted murder.” These allegations also align with Dvalishvili’s previous account of the incident on The Ariel Helwani Show. The Georgian fighter claimed that the 30-year-old bantamweight attacked him after the initial confrontation and attributed his injuries, including multiple cuts and lacerations, to the events that unfolded once the cameras were off. Interestingly, despite the alleged severity of the incident, Dvalishvili requested the release of the men who were imprisoned over the brawl. However, Sterling’s latest allegations raise further questions about what transpired inside the hotel and whether the initial footage captured the full extent of the violence.

item.title: Knicks coach Mike Brown compliments Raptors coach despite him mocking Jalen Brunson during clash
item.description: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images Toronto Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic made it clear that he was not a fan of New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson flopping during their game. The Knicks picked up a 111-102 win over the Kawhi Leonard-less Toronto Raptors on November 17 to improve their record to 8-6 for the season. Brunson is overcoming his slow start to the season and put up 31 points, five rebounds and five assists in the win. However, his on-court antics seem to run Raptors coach Rajakovic the wrong way. Mike Brown impressed by Darko Rajakovic even after he mocked Jalen Brunson’s flopping during Knicks vs. Raptors Rajakovic was caught on camera imitating Brunson for flopping after a shot, with cameras catching how openly Rajakovic mocked Brunson after that play. Nonetheless, Brown was positive about Rajakovic after the game . “Darko does a heckuva job…those guys play hard, really good defensively, give us fits. I thought our execution, especially down stretch at a pretty high level both ends of the floor, in particular, offensively… Our pace, spacing, screening, take care of basketball down stretch. Brunson had the last laugh, leading the Knicks to a much-needed win over the Raptors and establishing themselves as an East contender after a slow start to the season. Brunson is averaging 27.0 points, 5.9 assists and 2.9 rebounds this season, and shooting 7.2 free throws per game. He ranks 11th in free-throw attempts this season, so his flopping hasn’t helped him get to the line much. Brunson’s scoring is the key offensive weapon the Knicks are built around, evidenced by his performances in their run to the 2026 NBA Championship. While Rajakovic did not do anything excessive in terms of complaining about Brunson’s actions, he did display his feelings in a hilarious fashion. This was Toronto’s fifth straight loss of this season, falling to 5-9 on the season. Rajakovic has the support of the organisation and likely felt comfortable calling out Brunson with his gesture instead of biting his tongue. However, complaining about calls will not change the Raptors’ fortunes this season, as evidenced by the loss to the Knicks. item.title: AUS vs ENG 3rd ODI 2026 live scorecard, toss winner, winning probability, result and highlights from Hobart
item.description: AUS vs ENG 3rd ODI 2026 live scorecard, toss winner, winning probability, result and highlights from Hobart originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY MATCH DETAILS: (Australia vs England 3rd ODI) Venue: Bellerive Oval, Hobart Captains: Mitchell Marsh ( Australia ), Harry Brook ( England ) Toss result: England have won the toss and will bat first Live Telecast: Fox Cricket, Kayo Sports (Australia); TNT Sports (UK); Eurosport, Fancode (India) Umpires and match officials: Sharfuddoula, Shaun Haig (on-field umpires), Chris Gaffaney (TV umpire), Sam Nogajski (reserve umpire), and Javagal Srinath (match referee) Match result: TBD Player of the Match: TBD Player of the Series: TBD FOLLOW LIVE: Ball-by-ball updates of the match Australia vs England 3rd ODI live match scorecard Follow along with the latest live scorecard here as the match unfolds, or click here for key text commentary updates from the action. Australia vs England 3rd ODI Live Score & Updates Welcome to CricketNews.com's live coverage of the third ODI between Australia and England at the Bellerive Oval in Hobart. After 20 overs, England are 137/2 England added 58 runs across overs 11 to 20 while losing just one wicket, stabilizing the innings at 6.85 runs per over after Australia pulled back the scoring rate through spin. Matt Renshaw delivered the breakthrough in the 15th over (14.4), bowling Joe Root for 12 off 15 balls (1 four) to end a 38-run second-wicket partnership at 112/2. Ben Duckett anchored the middle overs effortlessly, bringing up a composed half-century to reach 62* off 55 balls (10 fours) alongside captain Harry Brook (14* off 15 balls, 2 fours), who helped take 11 runs off Spencer Johnson in the 20th over. After 10 overs, England are 79/1 England raced out of the blocks in the first 10 overs against Australia, scoring at 7.90 runs per over on the back of 15 boundaries. Openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett put on a brisk 74-run stand before Jack Edwards broke through in the 9th over (8.4), having Banton caught by Mitchell Marsh for 44 off 35 balls (9 fours). Duckett anchored the rest of the Powerplay unbeaten on 30 (22 balls, 6 fours) alongside Joe Root (0 off 3 balls), while Mahli Beardman closed out the 10th over conceding just 5 runs (2-0-15-0). Toss result: England won the toss and opted to bat first Pre-match: Australia and England head into the third and deciding ODI in Hobart with the series level at 1-1 after two one-sided contests. It is the first time since 1979 that the teams have entered the final match of an ODI series in Australia with the score tied. Bellerive Oval will also host a men's ODI for the first time since 2018 in a game that could offer both sides a valuable confidence boost ahead of next year's World Cup. Despite missing several frontline players, Australia will look to make home advantage count, but England have an opportunity to secure a rare ODI series victory on Australian soil. Australia

item.description: Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images AFC Playoff Picture: How standings, playoff odds look after Bengals blowout, Drake Maye injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the NFL season passes the halfway point, the AFC playoff teams are starting to take hold of their positions. There are seven spots in the AFC playoffs, and it would not be a shocker if the teams that currently own those positions would finish the season as postseason teams. The Buffalo Bills have the best record in the AFC , and they are rolling with an 8-1 record. The Bills have been motivated all season under first-year head coach Joe Brady. The Bills were angry a year ago when they lost their grip on the division and the New England Patriots took advantage of a fourth-place schedule and stole it from them. They appear to be quite secure in their position as they have a 3.5-game lead over the Pats (5-5), who have lost two in a row and saw QB Drake Maye go down with an ankle injury. The Bills are plus-110 to emerge with the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs, according to DraftKings. The Bills are the only team likely to make the playoffs from the AFC East. The Patriots still have a chance, but they will be sending Tommy DeVito out to lead the attack, and he struggled badly after taking over for Maye in the Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions. The Bills, Bengals and Jaguars appear to have the best route to the playoffs and the top seed in the AFC. However, the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos can’t be counted out in the AFC West. Both teams are well on their way to making the playoffs and it’s just a question of which of these 7-2 teams is going to emerge with the AFC West crown. The Chiefs are demonstrating that last year’s 6-11 finish was basically just a fluke The Chiefs have returned to excellent form and there is always confidence when Patrick Mahomes has the ball in his hands in a close game. The Chiefs are listed as minus-12500 to make the playoffs and plus-550 to earn the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Broncos have easier closing schedule than Chiefs The Broncos appear to have a better shot at winning the AFC West crown over the Chiefs because their closing schedule is much easier. They play the Raiders twice, the Dolphins, the Jets and the Chargers, while the Chiefs have challenging games against the Bills, Rams and Bengals in consecutive weeks and another tough game against the 49ers. The Broncos are minus-8000 to make the AFC playoffs and plus-380 to take the No. 1 seed. The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) and the surprising Cleveland Browns (6-4) are both in positions to take the final two seeds in the AFC playoffs. The Steelers suffered a 38-18 loss to the Bengals in Week 10, but head coach Mike McCarthy and QB Aaron Rodgers have no reason to panic. The Steelers are listed at minus-290 to make the playoffs. Their closing schedule features tough games against Denver and Jacksonville and winnable games against Philadelphia, Baltimore (2), Carolina and Tennessee. Browns holding on to No. 7 seed in AFC The Browns currently have the No. 7 and final seed in the AFC playoffs. They have a 1.0-game lead over the Patriots, and while history says that it will be difficult for Cleveland to hold on to that playoff spot, first-year head coach Todd Monken has this team believing in itself even though this team is devoid of stars. The Browns are minus-130 to make the playoffs. The Browns have been depending on Deshaun Watson at quarterback, and he has thrown for 2,118 yards and 7 TDs. He has also demonstrated that he can run away from pass rushers. He has 266 rushing yards and 2 TDs. The Browns are getting a lift from tight end Harold Fanin Jr. He has caught 44 passes for 544 yards and 4 TDs. The struggling Patriots are the closest team that is out of the AFC playoff structure to gaining a position, but the absence of Maye means it is a major long shot Mike Vrabel’s team to make the playoffs. If the Browns are going to fall apart, it would seem that the Las Vegas Raiders or the Texans have the best shot at making a run at the postseason. The Raiders (4-6) have some winnable games against the Browns, Chargers, Titans and Cardinals, but their trade of QB Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings may have hurt their chances for success. The Texans were expected to battle the Jaguars for the division title because they have a potentially dominant defense. They would suddenly have to hit their stride in order to make a run, but that seems unlikely because of the way DeMeco Ryans’ team has played to this point. item.title: Awkward Jim Harbaugh-Justin Herbert Moment Adds Weird Vibe To Chargers Win
item.description: Justin Herbert trade rumros Getty It took nine games, but the Los Angeles Chargers got their first win of the 2026 regular season on Monday night against the Baltimore Ravens. A 1-8 record is not much to celebrate, and an awkward moment in the locker room after the game between head coach Jim Harbaugh and quarterback Justin Herbert just gave the whole thing a very weird vibe. In a video shared on social media which can be viewed here, Harbaugh congratulated the team for the win and then implored everyone to give each other a high five. The camera catches Harbaugh and Herbert exchanging a high five where the signal caller did not look all that enthused as he lightly exchanged a high five with his head coach. Some on social media saw the moment as evidence that Herbert doesn’t like Harbaugh or that he doesn’t have a good attitude. Others defended Herbert, asking whether he should have been doing back flips for their first win of the season. It’s probably just a moment that got blown way out of proportion but when a team has had as terrible a season as the Chargers, every single little moment is going to be scrutinized whether it is fair or not. To give Herbert the benefit of the doubt, it has been a brutal season. He probably doesn’t want to be celebrating too hard when his team is just having a completely embarrassing year. Plus, Herbert has always been fairly mild-mannered and reserved. Mina Kimes wrote a whole profile about Herbert years ago for ESPN which delved into how he is an introvert and just simply isn’t the big personality that many people expect an NFL quarterback to be. Herbert and Harbaugh really do not mix on paper That is what makes the Herbert-Harbaugh pairing so interesting on paper. Harbaugh is loud, bombastic, and prone to outbursts. Herbert is serene, cool, and supremely understated. It wouldn’t seem like the two would work together well but sometimes opposites attract in relationships. The last two seasons the two seemed to work together quite well as the team went 11-6 and made the playoffs each season. Maybe the addition of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is what threw things off a bit but Herbert has remained steadfast in his support of his offensive playcaller . Maybe the moment in the locker room is evidence of Herbert showing his displeasure with his head coach, or maybe it’s just how Herbert is. He and Harbaugh are completely different personality-wise so most likely it is just a case of two very different people sharing a bit of an awkward moment which wouldn’t even be blinked at if the team was 8-1 rather than 1-8. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Awkward Jim Harbaugh-Justin Herbert Moment Adds Weird Vibe To Chargers Win appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 18 – An M-class Solar Flare
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 18 – An… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Medium-Sized Solar Flare Explanation: What a flare for the chromatic ! Today’s image captures a piece of the Sun ’s chromosphere , the layer of the Sun ’s atmosphere above its surface where the temperature rises . Why would the Sun become hotter farther away from its core ? This is potentially due to energy from the swirling magnetic fields extending up through the Sun’s atmosphere. Those same magnetic fields can twist and snap , releasing light and energetic particles as a solar flare . The H-alpha filter used for today’s image captures light from energized hydrogen atoms as they travel off the Sun’s surface during a flare on May 14, 2025. This flare was classified as an M1 based on GOES observations , meaning it was moderately bright in X-rays . M-class flares can cause radio blackouts at Earth’s poles and minor radiation storms that can harm astronauts. They aren’t even the most powerful flares ! NASA, NOAA , and other agencies monitor the Sun to predict and identify such storms so we can protect humans on Earth and in space. item.title: Spurs' Dylan Harper suffers apparent injury late in Monday night's loss to Detroit
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper (2) is injured during the fourth quarter during the NBA game against the Detroit Pistons at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) Guard Dylan Harper suffered an apparent injury late in the Spurs' 105-93 loss to Detroit on Monday night at the Frost Bank Center. Harper headed to the locker room with some help from teammate Keldon Johnson after he slipped and landed awkwardly while attempting to catch a pass from Stephon Castle with 53.6 seconds left. "It just looked like he slipped, obviously, so hoping for the best, but don't know anything yet," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. Harper finished the game with 20 points on 8-of-14 shooting (0 of 4 from 3-point range), four rebounds and two assists. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.title: Florida’s Todd Golden showers Houston with ultimate praise before Players Era showdown
item.description: Candice Ward-Imagn Images Florida’s Todd Golden showers Houston with ultimate praise before Players Era showdown appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Florida and Houston took care of business in the Players Era 8 Tournament on Tuesday, beating Notre Dame and Rutgers, respectively, at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas. The No. 1 Gators defeated the Fighting Irish , 86-78, to improve to 5-0, while the No. 8 Cougars upended the Scarlet Knights , 85-73, to climb to 4-0. Something’s gotta give between Florida and Houston, as they will battle on Wednesday. Not to mention, their all-time series is tied at 2-2. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Ahead of the big-time showdown, Gators coach Todd Golden was effusive in his praise of the Cougars, as reported by PaperCity Magazine’s Chris Baldwin. “That’s why I wanted to come to this event. To play some of the best teams in America, and we believe Houston to be one of the best programs in America, with what Coach (Kelvin) Sampson and his staff have done. They’re not the same as they’ve been in the past, but they have very similar qualities,” said Golden. “I think it’s going to be a great test. Obviously, it’s going to be a physical game, and we have to step up to the challenge in that way.” Florida coach Todd Golden on Houston vs. Florida Chapter II: "That's why I wanted to come to this event – is to play some of the best teams in America. And we believe Houston to be one of the best programs in America. What Coach Sampson and his staff have done. They're not the… pic.twitter.com/MNZPpRpsuI — Chris Baldwin (@ChrisYBaldwin) November 18, 2026 It will be a rematch of the national title game in 2025, when Florida came back from a 12-point deficit to beat Houston, 65-63. Golden, then 38 years old, became the second-youngest coach to rule the NCAA Tournament. He is aware that the Cougars will be hungry for revenge. “They know us, and we know them. It’s going to be kind of mano a mano that way to see who the tougher team’s going to be, both mentally and physically,” added Golden. Florida will lean on Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon, Rueben Chinyelu, while Houston will parade Dedan Thomas Jr., Delrecco Gillespie, and Mercy Miller. item.title: Chiefs Sign Eagles OL After Successful Workout, But Not to Active Roster
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 20: Fred Johnson #74 of the Philadelphia Eagles defends against the New York Giants during the first half at MetLife Stadium on October 20, 2024 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Getty EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 20: Fred Johnson #74 of the Philadelphia Eagles defends against the New York Giants during the first half at MetLife Stadium on October 20, 2024 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs reportedly bought in former Philadelphia Eagles offensive lineman Fred Johnson for a workout on Tuesday after he was released by the Eagles back on Nov. 13. After Johnson cleared waivers on Monday he was free to sign with any team. And it appears that a decision has been made rather quickly, as he has now signed with Kansas City. Chiefs Sign Former Eagles Offensive Lineman Fred Johnson The #Chiefs are signing OL Fred Johnson to their practice squad, per source. pic.twitter.com/8Fj9S3ZQ6s — Arrowhead Corner (@ArrowheadCorner) November 18, 2026 The news was also released onto the Chiefs’ official website. “John FitzPatrick (TE), E.J. Smith (RB), Fred Johnson (T) signed to the Practice Squad. Jacob De Jesus (WR), Bub Means (WR), Cole Christiansen (LB) Practice Squad contracts terminated.” The team’s official site posted on Nov. 17. Will Fred Johnson Suit Up For the Chiefs This Weekend? Getty EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY – OCTOBER 20: Fred Johnson #74 of the Philadelphia Eagles defends against the New York Giants during the first half at MetLife Stadium on October 20, 2024 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) The move to add Johnson to the practice squad rather than the active roster likely signals the team’s uncertainty about the playing statuses of right tackle Jaylon Moore and guard Trey Smith, who are dealing with an ankle injury and a concussion respectively. If both are good to for Week 11, it’s less likely that the Chiefs will see Johnson either activated for game-day or possibly full-on elevated to the 53-man roster. If the pair are both ruled out, there is a far better likelihood that Kansas City will require his services in some form come this weekend’s game hosting the Arizona Cardinals. Johnson joins a thin practice squad offensive line setup that currently sports 2024 undrafted free agent tackle Ethan Driskell and rookie UDFA center Pete Nygra as the only representatives of the unit. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Chiefs Sign Eagles OL After Successful Workout, But Not to Active Roster appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Duke hits new low in 37 years with blowout loss to Illinois
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Rob Kinnan-Imagn Images Duke hits new low in 37 years with blowout loss to Illinois appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . History has the receipts proving Duke is a basketball powerhouse . However, nobody is completely invincible. On Tuesday, No. 5 Duke reluctantly welcomed No. 10 Illinois to the famed Cameron Indoor Stadium in Durham, North Carolina. The Illini defeated the Blue Devils 99-78. It was not only a blowout loss, but also the first of its kind in a long time for Duke, per Joe Tipton of On3Sports.com. The last time the Blue Devils lost by more than 20 points at home was in 1989, 37 years ago, to be exact. Additionally, the Blue Devils ‘ 35-game winning streak at home came to an end. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Duke had not lost at home by 20 points since 1989, a span of 37 years. The Blue Devils’ 35-game home winning streak, the longest in the nation, is also over. Historic win for Illinois. This group is connected, tough, and fearless. Brad Underwood has a dangerous group. https://t.co/WkERFMjFN1 — Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton) November 18, 2026 Illinois came ready to play. A major factor was Andrej Stojakovic scoring a record 46 points , the most points scored by an opponent at Cameron Indoor Stadium since Grady Wallace scored 43 points for South Carolina in 1957. Despite their size and height, Duke was outrebounded by Illinois in a 54-34 win. The Illini also grabbed 18 offensive rebounds and scored 19 second-chance points. Plus, Illinois won the battle in the paint, 48-30. They also put up 22 points off 14 Blue Devils turnovers. The Blue Devils shot 24-for-64 from the field (37.5%) and 9-for-40 from 3 (22.5%). They were also only 21-for-33 from the field and missed 12 free throws. For Duke, freshman center Joaquim Boumtje-Boumtje led the way with 17 points and five rebounds. Senior guard Caleb Foster added 15 points and six rebounds. Second-year guard/forward Sebastian Wilkins added 10 points. The Blue Devils are now 3-2. They enter the season trying to shake off an Elite Eight exit to UConn after being the No. 1 seed. On Saturday, the Blue Devils will play against Utah in Pittsburgh. item.title: Sierra Snow Season Spins Up
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Sierra Snow Season Spins Up Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search November 12 November 14 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison November 12 November 14 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison November 12 November 14 Curtain Toggle 2-Up California’s Sierra Nevada got an early taste of wintry weather when one of the first major snowfalls of the water year arrived on November 13, 2026. A moisture-laden storm delivered heavy rains to lower elevations in the Sacramento area and snow accumulations of around a foot to some mountainous areas. The recent bout of wet weather was the first in a quick succession of Pacific storms bringing rain, snow, and wind to the U.S. West in mid-November. The MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Terra satellite captured this image (right) of fresh snow in the Sierra Nevada on the morning of November 14, during a lull between weather systems. Two days earlier (left), the mountains were mostly bare, with snow appearing only at the highest elevations. Nearly 12 inches (30 centimeters) of snow fell at Donner Pass, northwest of Lake Tahoe, on November 13, according to the Central Sierra Snow Laboratory . The accumulation snarled traffic on Interstate 80 in the area, prompting officials to close the highway in both directions that evening. To the south, the ski resort at Mammoth Mountain reported 9 to 13 inches (23 to 33 centimeters) of new snow, and officials at Yosemite National Park closed several roads ahead of the storm. More wet weather and mountain snow are forecast to follow . The National Weather Service (NWS) issued a winter storm warning for portions of the Sierras above 5,000 feet (1,500 meters) in elevation from November 18 to 20. NWS warned of difficult-to-impossible travel conditions, gusty winds, and snow accumulations of around 4 feet (120 centimeters) possible above 8,000 feet (2,400 meters). NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using MODIS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE and GIBS/Worldview . Story by Lindsey Doermann. item.title: ‘Human’ wins Cambridge dictionary’s word of the year
item.description: Meaning and use of word has become more important in age of AI chatbot, says dictionary In a world where the line between people and machines is more blurred than ever, Cambridge dictionary has sided with natural intelligence for its word of the year: human. Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence – led by the arrival of ChatGPT three years ago – have made the question of what it means to be human as vexed as ever, but the dictionary has drawn a firm line with its choice of the word of 2026, defining “human” as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines”. Continue reading...

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty The Indiana Fever are moving closer to finding their next basketball executive, and their search has drawn three candidates with extensive NBA experience. Boston Celtics vice president Allison Feaster, Sacramento Kings vice president Phil Jabour and former Dallas Mavericks executive Matt Riccardi have emerged as strong candidates for the position, according to Annie Costabile and Sam Amick of The Athletic , who first reported the development Tuesday, Nov. 17. ESPN’s Alexa Philippou and Shams Charania subsequently reported that Indiana is working through a group of finalists, with a hire expected within the next month. Philippou also clarified that the Fever intend to hire one basketball operations executive rather than separate replacements for former team president Kelly Krauskopf and former general manager Amber Cox. The search comes at a critical point for Indiana, which must address major roster decisions surrounding Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell. The development comes nearly four weeks after the Fever parted ways with two of their highest-ranking executives. Fever Identify Three Leading Front Office Candidates Getty 13 Jun 2000: Allison Feaster of the Los Angeles Sparks dribbles the ball during a game against the Seattle Storm at Key Arena in Seattle, Washington. The Storm defeated the Sparks 59-69. Feaster brings a combination of playing experience and NBA front office leadership. A former WNBA player, she currently serves as Boston’s vice president of team operations and organizational growth. She joined the Celtics in 2019 after an accomplished professional playing career. Her work has focused on player development, organizational culture and relationships throughout the basketball operation. Jabour offers a different background. The Kings executive has worked extensively in scouting, player evaluation and roster construction. Before joining Sacramento, he held a scouting leadership position with the Philadelphia 76ers. Riccardi, meanwhile, previously served as an assistant general manager with the Mavericks. He also spent more than a decade with the Brooklyn Nets organization, including a stint running their G League affiliate. Following Nico Harrison’s dismissal in Dallas in November 2025, Riccardi and Michael Finley briefly shared interim general manager responsibilities. All three candidates bring NBA experience, although Indiana has not announced a finalist or identified a preferred choice. Fever Planning One Hire After Major Leadership Shake-Up The Fever’s search began after team president Kelly Krauskopf stepped down Oct. 23. General manager and chief operating officer Amber Cox departed later that day, leaving Indiana with significant vacancies in basketball leadership. However, Philippou clarified that the Fever intend to hire one basketball executive rather than separate replacements for Krauskopf and Cox. That distinction is significant. The incoming executive will inherit a franchise with championship expectations and several consequential personnel decisions approaching. Krauskopf helped build the Fever from their inception and guided the franchise through its first WNBA championship in 2012. Cox, meanwhile, oversaw basketball operations during a period of heightened attention surrounding the team’s young core. Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell Await Fever’s Next Move Getty Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever confer against the Chicago Sky during the first half at Wintrust Arena on August 23, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. The timing of Indiana’s search adds urgency to the decision. Caitlin Clark remains the centerpiece of the franchise, while Kelsey Mitchell enters another important offseason following a career-best 2026 campaign. Mitchell’s upcoming free agency presents an immediate challenge for whoever takes charge. The four-time All-Star has established herself as one of the WNBA’s premier scorers, making her future a central question in Indiana’s plans. The next executive must also evaluate the roster around Clark and Mitchell while working with coach Stephanie White to establish a sustainable championship contender. Indiana’s leadership changes have created uncertainty. Tuesday’s report, however, suggests the search is entering its final stages. With several NBA-connected candidates under consideration and a decision expected within weeks, the Fever could soon have the person responsible for guiding their next chapter. item.title: Maple Leafs Have Bigger Problems Than the Standings
item.description: TORONTO, CANADA - SEPTEMBER 29: Auston Matthews #34 of the Toronto Maple Leafs skates against the Montréal Canadiens at Scotiabank Arena on September 29, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Chris Tanouye/Getty Images) Getty The last thing the Toronto Maple Leafs want to do right now is look at the standings. Seeing themselves in last place in the Atlantic Division could do far more harm than good. Unless the team can find some sort of motivation in seeing themselves at the bottom of the division, the only thing the Leafs need to look at is themselves. The club just needs to work hard and focus on controlling the things they can control. Otherwise, the prospect of salvaging this season may be too much to pull off. For now, the talk shouldn’t be about making the playoffs. Yes, that’s a major goal for the organization. But it shouldn’t be the only thing guiding the team’s performance at this point. The guiding factor should be trying to get back to the fundamentals and win hockey games. It might sound like a cliché, but the Maple Leafs have entered a territory in which only the next game matters. While injuries have played a major role in derailing their season, the fact is that the only thing the Leafs can actually do about it is go out there and execute. One can find all the sports adages used to help teams focus on winning. But the bottom line is that the only game that matters is the next one. Thinking about games in the spring won’t do anyone any good. Maple Leafs Have to Dump Thoughts of Magic Fixes From time to time, everyone wishes there was a magic button they could just push to solve everything. That would be fantastic if it really existed. Such a magic button would make Morgan Rielly, Oliver Ekman-Larsson and Chris Tanev 10 years younger. That button would also morph Sergei Bobrovsky into the Vezina Trophy-caliber goalie he once was. Heck, that magic button would wipe 10 years off John Tavares and restore Auston Matthews to his 60-goal form. Alas, that button doesn’t exist. And so, Maple Leafs GM John Chayka cannot afford to think that there’s a single solution out there. A coaching change or a major trade won’t save the season. Even if it doesn’t end in a playoff appearance, turning things around this year won’t happen with some incantation or ritual. The turnaround will happen with the team avoiding the costly mistakes that doomed its six-game homestand. Toronto Still Has Time to Turn It Around Even at the risk of sounding like hopium, the Maple Leafs still have time to turn things around. The team has the talent and the firepower to make a run at a playoff spot. Once in, Toronto could become a very tough out. The clock is ticking, nonetheless. That’s why the focus can’t go beyond the next game or even the next shift. Teams that focus on winning each shift end up winning hockey games. Like losses, wins quickly pile up. And if rivals even stumble just a little, a hot team can make up ground in the standings. Ultimately, the Maple

It’s either give up on the season and play out the string, even in November, or take it one game at a time and try to make a serious run at it. item.title: Bayern Munich News: Arsenal wants Michael Olise; FC Barcelona eyeing Man City’s Josko Gvardiol?; and MORE!
item.description: (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) | Getty Images Gunners keeping close tabs on Olise? (Football Transfers) Bayern Munich star Michael Olise will continue to be one of the most sought-after and speculated-upon players in the world until he signs a contract extension or announces his intention to transfer. One club that is keeping a close eye on the Frenchman is Arsenal, which is looking to bring in a blockbuster-type player: One Bundesliga superstar Arsenal are keeping tabs on is Michael Olise – despite not being a left-winger. More precisely, the Gunners are attentive to his contract situation and his impending negotiations with Bayern. The Bavarians are desperate to hand the France international improved terms in order to guarantee that he will stay at the club beyond 2027. Olise has fielded interest from the likes of Real Madrid, PSG and Liverpool in recent months, hence the urgency. We can confirm that a release clause will be one of the key points under discussion. Olise does not currently have one, but Bayern may have to compromise in order to get him to extend. The Munich outfit previously had a no-release-clause policy, but they have been forced to soften this stance in recent seasons, with both Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala – their best-paid players – having exit mechanisms in their contracts. Given Arsenal’s financial strength and willingness to pay whatever it takes for players of the calibre of Vini Jr and Olise, a release clause could make a transfer to North London possible even if he were to sign a new deal. However, it must be emphasised that this is all hypothetical right now. Arsenal are not actively pursuing the 24-year-old at this stage; they are just keeping themselves informed on his situation. Arsenal can join Real Madrid, Liverpool, Paris Saint-Germain, and the rest in line to take a run at Olise. Bayern Munich will not flinch until the summer, when extensive talks are expected to take place. In this case, it at least appears that everyone understa nds Olise will not be leaving midseason. If he decides that he wants to leave Bayern Munich, that is where it will all get interesting. With a contract that runs through 2029, the Bavarians would have some decisions to make at that point. However, there is also the possibility that he signs a contract extension—a proposition that most Bayern Munic h fans would prefer . Gvardiol, 24, has become one of the best young defenders in Europe in recent years and Barca are keen to strengthen their defensive options. Bayern Munich will not flinch until the summer, when extensive talks are expected to take place. In this case, it at least appears that everyone understa nds Olise will not be leaving midseason. If he decides that he wants to leave Bayern Munich, that is where it will all get interesting. With a contract that runs through 2029, the Bavarians would have some decisions to make at that point. However, there is also the possibility that he signs a contract extension—a proposition that most Bayern Munic h fans would prefer . Barca could be contemplating move for Gvardiol (ESPN) FC Barcelona is reportedly hungry to bolster its backline. With Manchester City’s future uncertain, the Catalans could be looking to convince Joško Gvardiol to make the jump to LaLiga: Manchester City defender Josko Gvardiol is on the radar of Barcelona, according to AS. Gvardiol, 24, has become one of the best young defenders in Europe in recent years and Barca are keen to strengthen their defensive options. However, while the club are interested in signing the Croatia international, they do not think a deal will be possible unless he pushes to leave amid the fallout from City’s financial charges. Gabriel headed to Real (Transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano) After a few months of back-and-forth, it looks like Manchester United phenom JJ Gabriel is headed to Real Madrid: 🚨💣 BREAKING: JJ Gabriel confirms he has decided to leave Manchester United, saying officially goodbye to the club. 16 year old talent has decided to join Real Madrid, deal set to be signed — here we go will follow very soon. 🤍🔜 Gabriel put out a video — which is completely ludicrous considering he never made a senior team appearance for the Red Devils: 🚨⤵️ JJ Gabriel announces his departure from Manchester United. Move to Real Madrid imminent. #MUFC https://t.co/GVTjttee58 pic.twitter.com/ppv6K2dk73 — Florian Plettenberg (@Plettigoal) November 17, 2026 Rice to ink new deal with Arsenal (The Athletic’s David Ornstein) Declan Rice appears to be set to sign a contract extension with Arsenal: 🚨 EXCL: Arsenal reach agreement with Declan Rice to sign new 5yr contract. 27yo midfielder’s existing deal ran until June 2028 (+1) – fresh terms extend to summer 2031 & reward status for club/country. England int’l to put pen to paper soon @TheAthleticFC Remember when Rice was contemplating his final decision between Arsenal and Bayern Munich? That feels like forever ago, but he was never really headed to Germany, was he? Ngomuha still an option for Bayern (Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg via @iMiaSanMia) It appears that Bayern Munich is not giving up on its pursuit of Liverpool attacker Rio Ngumoha: Rio Ngumoha remains a very interesting option for Bayern for the left wing position. Bayern made a very concrete attempt to sign Ngumoha last summer, but the move fell through. As things stand, Liverpool are doing everything to extend the player’s contract – but nothing is done yet. The outcome is open. United to pursue Thiaw? (ESPN) Manchester United could be looking to take a run at Germany international Malick Thiaw, who was impressive in last Friday’s 3-1 win over Serbia: Manchester United are among the clubs interested in Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw, according to Sky Germany. Despite establishing himself as a key figure in the Magpies’ backline, the 25-year-old Germany international could be available next summer, although Newcastle would demand at least an €80 million fee for his signature. However, Newcastle will reject any January offers for left back Lewis Hall amid longstanding interest from United, according to The Telegraph. The 22-year-old was the subject of an enquiry from the Red Devils last summer before signing a new long-term contract in September.
