item.title: Midnight Mania! No Belt, But Still UFC’s New King
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 14: Josh Hokit prepares to face Ciryl Gane of France in their heavyweight championship fight during the UFC 334 event at Madison Square Garden on November 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Zuffa LLC) Welcome to Midnight Mania! Let’s start the night off by taking a look back over the three biggest stories of Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua start time, full Netflix fight card details : Anyone particularly excited about the most overdue matchup in boxing? Daniel Cormier under review as petition to boot ‘DC’ from UFC commentary nears 6,000 signatures : I’m not a fan of Cormier’s commentary generally — too much podcasting — but his commentary was far more accurate than Rogan’s in regards to the UFC 334 main event. UFC Saudi Arabia’s Shara Magomedov chasing second wife so he ‘doesn’t have a desire to cheat’ : Let’s get Khabib’s opinion on this pressing topic. Insomnia Based on the UFC 334 traffic, Josh Hokit really is one of the biggest modern draws. Hard to believe! After the weekend’s performance, and outside of myself, Josh Hokit is the biggest draw in the ufc today! Bravo champ! Onward to greener and more exciting pastures, you are in the right place with Paradigm Sports! CONTRACTMAXXING 101 #Welcome https://t.co/Kvvv4rJ3Dk — Conor McGregor (@TheNotoriousMMA) November 17, 2026 It will be a long while before we see Cody Gibson back in action. Life Update: Tore my ACL and meniscus competing in a jiu jitsu tournament about a month ago. Surgery set for Dec 1st. Got hired to teach at the state prison. Starting that job soon. Gym is going good but in order for it to grow I need to stack my profits and not rely on them… — Cody Gibson (@TheRenegade559) November 17, 2026 Lanky guys and pushups rarely mix that well. Kamaru Usman made pushups look like a warm up while Israel Adesanya was fighting for his life ☠️ pic.twitter.com/TiLadmth0o — FIGHTFLIX (@Fightflix_) November 17, 2026 It just so happens that Shara Magomedov is looking for a wife! Just kidding, that would be crazy … unless? Kayla Harrison is ready to find her husband. #HelwaniShow pic.twitter.com/ipK4rnA3vM — Jed I. Goodman © (@jedigoodman) November 17, 2026 Sedriques Dumas promises a brighter future after his various crimes and punishments. Mickey Gall next? I’m finally done. With all my legal stuff I’m off house arrest now I’m done with courts and I’m done with the street life. If im treat my career right I’m do it the right way for the first time in my life. — Sd Thereaperufc (@SdUnbroken) November 17, 2026 There are multiple ways to make it big in combat sports, but being a dominant champion in another organization is an underrated one. For all rising fighters, you need to learn from Salahdine Parnasse. – Find a good promotion. – Build within, your record, marketing, & fanbase. – Get PAID while doing so. – Become wanted. No DWCS for him. Congrats @SalahdineP on the Nike deal & being a GQ man of the year. 👏 pic.twitter.com/YEH

item.title: ‘Ridiculous’: Dale Earnhardt Jr. Shuts Down Chase Elliott Crew Chief Criticism
item.description: Dale Earnhardt Jr. fires back at Chase Elliott crew chief criticism. Getty Dale Earnhardt Jr. defended the driver/crew chief pairing of Chase Elliott and Alan Gustafson in the wake of Hendrick Motorsports’ 2027 lineup change. While HMS drivers William Byron and Alex Bowman are getting different crew chiefs, Elliott and Gustafson remain together for 2027. On Monday, it was announced that Rudy Fugle will be atop the pit box for Bowman in 2027 after six seasons as Byron’s crew chief. Adam Wall, who was the crew chief for Corey Day in the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series, will move up to the Cup level as Byron’s crew chief in 2027. Meanwhile, the pairing of Elliott and Gustafson, as well as Kyle Larson and Cliff Daniels, will stay together next year. Earnhardt Jr. Fires Back at Elliott, Gustafson Criticism: ‘None of Y’all’s Business’ Earnhardt Jr. discussed the shake-up at Hendrick Motorsports on the recent episode of “The Dale Jr. Download.” The former HMS driver said that some fans might look at the news of the crew chief changes and be angered by the fact Gustafson will continue to be Elliott’s crew chief next year. In the wake of the news, some fans have voiced their frustrations on social media under an X post by motorsports reporter Jeff Gluck regarding the matter . The NASCAR Hall of Famer dismissed those voices, noting that the two enjoy working with each other. Earnhardt Jr. was blunt in saying the partnership is nobody else’s business besides the people involved. “There’s this small little group of people that are seeing this news and going, ‘They’re going to leave Chase and Alan together still?’ It’s ridiculous. Chase and Alan want to work together. It’s their [expletive] choice. None of y’all’s business,” Earnhardt Jr. said. Earnhardt Jr. noted that Elliott has been on record saying he enjoys working with Gustafson and questioned why there is so much criticism around the crew chief. “Chase likes it. He’s said it multiple times. He likes Alan. What are we missing?” Earnhardt Jr. acknowledges that fans are allowed to have an opinion and do not know the full behind-the-scenes story with things like this. However, because Elliott has expressed his desire to work with Gustafson, Therefore, Earnhardt Jr. believes fans should give the pairing a break. “This is something that Chase, multiple times, has said, ‘I want to work with him. He’s great.’ Let’s just leave it alone,” Earnhardt Jr. said. Things started out promising for Elliott and company. The 2020 Cup champion won the seventh race of the campaign at Martinsville Speedway, the earliest in a season he had ever won before. He’s great.’ Let’s just leave it alone,” Earnhardt Jr. said. Chase Elliott Hit Career Lows During 2026 Season Perhaps some of the criticism regarding the Elliott/Gustafson combination stems from the performance of the No. 9 team in 2026. Things started out promising for Elliott and company. The 2020 Cup champion won the seventh race of the campaign at Martinsville Speedway, the earliest in a season he had ever won before. Four races later, Elliott captured another victory at Texas Motor Speedway. However, things went downhill from there as Elliott scored only one top-5 finish in the next 15 races. Elliott dropped from as high as third in the standings to eighth by the time the Chase began. In the Chase, Elliott only led one lap throughout the 10-race period and fell back to 12th in the standings by season’s end. Elliott scored 13 top-10 finishes, a career-low, and tied his career-low for average finish at 15.1. Elliott only scored eight top-5 finishes during the 2026 season, the second-lowest in his career. His lowest was seven top fives in 2023, a year where he missed six races. What started out as a strong year for Elliott turned into a difficult one as the season carried on. item.title: You’ve Been Serb’d: Illinois 99, Duke 78
item.description: Nov 17, 2026; Durham, North Carolina, USA; Duke Blue Devils guard Caleb Foster (1) reacts on the bench during the second half against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Cameron Indoor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rob Kinnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect First of all, there’s no doubt that Illinos deserved the win at Cameron on Tuesday night. The Illini just thumped the Blue Devils in almost every way. They outrebounded Duke, 54-34, and Duke had 14 turnovers. Illinois also outscored Duke 31-21 from the line, and ruthlessly controlled the paint. Duke took 40 threes in this game, hitting just 9. Illinois shot just 6-32, but their control of the paint made that irrelevant. And so did the performance of Andrej Stojakovic. When Duke played Cal in 2024, Stojakovic finished with 10 points on 4-14. Tuesday night, he lit Duke up for 46 points on 14-21/2-3 from the floor, along with 16-20 from the free throw line. It was a record-breaking performance: the most points ever scored by an opponent in Cameron was 43 by South Carolina’s Grady Wallace in 1957, when the ACC was 3 years, 9 months, and 15 days old. It came perilously close to breaking Dick Groats’ record of 48 points, set in 1952. He was superb and nearly unguardable, but he’s not the only reason that Illinois won. Quentin Coleman racked up 27, but it was more than that. Here’s something you may not have caught: Zavier Zens, cousin of Kon and Kager Knueppel, who is 6-7, got 8 rebounds. He out-rebounded every Duke player who got on the floor. So did Coleman, who is 6-4, and so did reserve Stevan Vaaks, who, like Zens, is 6-7. JoJo Boumtje Boumtje got 5 rebounds. He’s 7-2. Patrick Ngongba got 4 rebounds. He’s 6-11. Cameron Williams, 7-0, got 3. Drew Scharnowski, 6-10, got 2. Three players, all 6-7 or under, and two of them freshmen, outrebounded Duke’s stable of big men. The leading rebounder for Duke? Caleb Foster, who had 6. That’s who. Basically, the same thing happened with Illinois that happened at Michigan State: both teams were significantly tougher and more focused than was Duke, and the Blue Devils paid the price. At the half, Scheyer pulled two starters: Boumtje Boumtje and Cayden Boozer, opting for Foster and Sebastian Wilkins instead. Wilkins has played very well all season, and deserved his shot, and Foster is highly reliable, but it didn’t make any difference, because Stojakovic stayed red hot, and to a lesser extent, so did Coleman. Those two finished with 73 of the 99 Illinois hung up in Cameron. It was a dismal night, but nonetheless, there were some bright moments. You could argue that Duke’s second five outplayed the starters. Cameron Williams came in and almost immediately blocked two shots. That’s at least the second time he’s done that, and possibly the third. He has great instincts for blocks. Scharnowski hit a three, which, we believe, was the first he’s ever hit in college. item.content:encoded: Nov 17, 2026; Durham, North Carolina, USA; Duke Blue Devils guard Caleb Foster (1) reacts on the bench during the second half against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Cameron Indoor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rob Kinnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect First of all, there’s no doubt that Illinos deserved the win at Cameron on Tuesday night. The Illini just thumped the Blue Devils in almost every way. They outrebounded Duke, 54-34, and Duke had 14 turnovers. Illinois also outscored Duke 31-21 from the line, and ruthlessly controlled the paint. Duke took 40 threes in this game, hitting just 9. Illinois shot just 6-32, but their control of the paint made that irrelevant. And so did the performance of Andrej Stojakovic. When Duke played Cal in 2024, Stojakovic finished with 10 points on 4-14. Tuesday night, he lit Duke up for 46 points on 14-21/2-3 from the floor, along with 16-20 from the free throw line. It was a record-breaking performance: the most points ever scored by an opponent in Cameron was 43 by South Carolina’s Grady Wallace in 1957, when the ACC was 3 years, 9 months, and 15 days old. It came perilously close to breaking Dick Groats’ record of 48 points, set in 1952. He was superb and nearly unguardable, but he’s not the only reason that Illinois won. Quentin Coleman racked up 27, but it was more than that. Here’s something you may not have caught: Zavier Zens, cousin of Kon and Kager Knueppel, who is 6-7, got 8 rebounds. He out-rebounded every Duke player who got on the floor. So did Coleman, who is 6-4, and so did reserve Stevan Vaaks, who, like Zens, is 6-7. JoJo Boumtje Boumtje got 5 rebounds. He’s 7-2. Patrick Ngongba got 4 rebounds. He’s 6-11. Cameron Williams, 7-0, got 3. Drew Scharnowski, 6-10, got 2. Three players, all 6-7 or under, and two of them freshmen, outrebounded Duke’s stable of big men. The leading rebounder for Duke? Caleb Foster, who had 6. That’s who. Basically, the same thing happened with Illinois that happened at Michigan State: both teams were significantly tougher and more focused than was Duke, and the Blue Devils paid the price. At the half, Scheyer pulled two starters: Boumtje Boumtje and Cayden Boozer, opting for Foster and Sebastian Wilkins instead. Wilkins has played very well all season, and deserved his shot, and Foster is highly reliable, but it didn’t make any difference, because Stojakovic stayed red hot, and to a lesser extent, so did Coleman. Those two finished with 73 of the 99 Illinois hung up in Cameron. It was a dismal night, but nonetheless, there were some bright moments. You could argue that Duke’s second five outplayed the starters. Cameron Williams came in and almost immediately blocked two shots. That’s at least the second time he’s done that, and possibly the third. He has great instincts for blocks. Scharnowski hit a three, which, we believe, was the first he’s ever hit in college. He played hard and certainly didn’t back down. Deron Rippey didn’t score, but he had 7 assists to two turnovers. And when Bryson Howard was in, he may have defended Stojakovic more effectively than anyone else on the team. He really gave him trouble in a way no one else did. We’ve already talked about Wilkins and Foster, but we should say this about Wilkins: he’s looking better and better. He moves incredibly well on the court, he defends, and he’s the furthest thing from selfish. We’re not sure what lessons Jon Scheyer will draw from this game, but from our vantage point, we saw that Duke was soft inside. And until that gets fixed, there are going to be games like this. We’ve seen enough of Ngongba to know that a bad game doesn’t mean the next one will be bad, too, but we can’t say that about Boumtje Boumtje. Clearly, he’s got a perimeter game, but 7-2 is a gift from God that one shouldn’t squander. In the second half, he was far more willing to take it to Illinois, and got to the line as a result. At whatever point he gets mad enough to rip someone’s head off on a dunk, you’ll know that part of the problem with this team has been solved. Side note: remember when Dahntay Jones did pushups after that insane dunk against Virginia? The reason he did it was because he was angry at his coach, Mike Krzyzewski, who had challenged him in some pretty elemental ways, as we understand it, and Jones wanted to make a point. We’re not sure how Scheyer will do that, but it might need to be done. And in fairness to Boumtje Boumtje, and we’re not picking on him, but the kid is 17. He’s adapting to a very new situation. Let’s give them both time and space to figure that out. The reality though is that in sports, there’s a goal, and that goal is to win. As we saw in the second half, sometimes changes need to be made. It’s going to be hard not to give minutes to Williams, Scharnowski, Howard, and most of all, Wilkins, if the starters let themselves get pushed around. Notes – Scheyer got a technical in the first half, which we think is his third as head coach…so did Dame Sarr…people are upset about the loss, but remember that Coach K took some beatings during his long and storied career…we wouldn’t judge this team in November…not only was that Scharnowski’s first made three, but it looks like it’s the only one he’s taken in three years…we’d love to see Blackwell go off soon… Behind Stojaković’s career night, No. 10 Illinois hands No. 5 Duke 99-78 loss in Cameron Indoor Stadium Andrej Stojakovic sets record with 46 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium as Illinois routs Duke Peja Stojakovic’s son makes history with 46-point explosion at Duke’s Cameron Indoor Stadium Illinois Routs Duke, Andrej Stojakovic Shows He’s the Best Scorer in College Basketball Illinois’ Quentin Coleman threw up, still scored 27 points vs. Duke Andrej Stojaković’s Breakout vs. Duke Could Make Illinois More Dangerous Than We Thought The Duke Blue Devils need to start paying rent, as Illinois basketball owns Cameron Indoor Stadium Illinois’ Andrej Stojakovic scores 46 points, most ever by an opponent at Duke Duke’s Scheyer after losing to Illinois; their worst loss at home since 1989 (Video) Duke basketball news: Blue Devils hit new low in 37 years with blowout loss to Illinois Changes are necessary at Duke after Illinois routs home Blue Devils behind Andrej Stojakovic’s historic game Duke gave Illinois basketball the perfect stage for the freshmen to thrive 5 Illinois basketball observations from the revenge beatdown of Duke Go to the DBR Boards to find Blue Healer Auctions || Drop us a line

item.title: Ohio State Drops Concerning Injury Update on RB Ja’Kobi Jackson
item.description: IOWA CITY, IA - OCTOBER 3: Running back Ja'Kobi Jackson #24 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs up the field in the second half against the Iowa Hawkeyes at Kinnick Stadium on October 3, 2026 in Iowa City, Iowa. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 26: Julian Sayin #10 of the Ohio State Buckeyes hands the ball off to Ja'kobi Jackson #24 during the first quarter of the game against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Ohio Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Kirk Irwin/Getty Images) AUSTIN, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 12: Ja'kobi Jackson #24 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs the ball for a touchdown against Justin Cryer #28 of the Texas Longhorns during the first quarter at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on September 12, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) The Ohio State Buckeyes thought they’d have a two Jackson backfield to carry them this season. Bo Jackson remains healthy, but Ja’Kobi Jackson remains out with an injury. It’s not as important an absence as that of QB Julian Sayin, but it isn’t an ideal situation for OSU heading into the last two games of the regular season. Ohio State plays at Nebraska on Saturday before returning home to host Michigan on Saturday, Nov. 28. The odds are slim of the Buckeyes making the College Football Playoff, but to do it, they’ll at the very least need to win both of their remaining regular season games. It doesn’t sound like Ja’Kobi Jackson will be part of the picture to do that, though. Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO – SEPTEMBER 26: Julian Sayin #10 of the Ohio State Buckeyes hands the ball off to Ja’kobi Jackson #24 during the first quarter of the game against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Ohio Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Kirk Irwin/Getty Images) Jackson remains out after having foot surgery in October. Ohio State head coach Ryan Day held his weekly press conference on Tuesday and provided an update, although it wasn’t a good one. He said that once Jackson begins running again, the Buckeyes will then consider him “week-to-week” — but added that Jackson hasn’t even started running yet. With time running out on the season, it’s seeming less and less likely that Ja’Kobi Jackson will play again for Ohio State this season. item.title: Is Cricket Australia re-opening investigation into Sandpapergate? CA announces new 'forum' as Usman Khawaja expresses concern
item.description: Is Cricket Australia re-opening investigation into Sandpapergate? CA announces new 'forum' as Usman Khawaja expresses concern originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Cricket Australia has set up a new forum linked to the 2018 Cape Town incident. Usman Khawaja’s book triggered the move, and several former colleagues have rejected his claims. The board insists this is not a fresh inquiry, yet Khawaja still has doubts. What is Cricket Australia's new Sandpapergate forum? Everything explained Cricket Australia has stepped back into one of the most uncomfortable chapters in its recent history, and the way it has done so has left many people asking what the board is really trying to achieve. The governing body announced on Wednesday that it will create a forum for those connected with the 2018 sandpaper incident in South Africa. Interim chair David Boon and chief executive Todd Greenberg made the announcement at Bellerive Oval, a little more than an hour before the third ODI between Australia and England was due to begin. The board had met the night before and agreed on the plan, which allows players and staff who were involved in the events of that tour to share their experiences. The decision comes only days after Usman Khawaja made a series of allegations about the Cape Town incident in his autobiography, Sabr, which was published last week. His claims drew responses from captain Pat Cummins and others, and they have kept a subject that many in Australian cricket hoped was behind them in the headlines. MORE: Former Aussie star reconfirms everyone knew about Sandpapergate According to the board, the forum will be confidential, and it will be open to anyone who was present at the time, although nobody will be forced to take part. An independent person will be appointed in the coming days, along with the terms of reference, and CA will decide later how much of the process is made public. Boon stressed that the aim is not to go back over the incident but to let those involved share their recollections as part of a push to move forward. "Last night, the Cricket Australia Board met, and we reached a decision that we believe is in the best interests of the game,” Boon said. “After careful discussion, we agreed to establish a forum that will allow players and staff involved in the events of South Africa in 2018 to share their experiences and their perspectives.” The interim chair then described how the long-running debate has affected the sport, which he said has become a distraction over time. He added: “For almost a decade, the fallout from these events, or from those events, has remained part of the conversation around Australian cricket. It has been a difficult chapter for many people, and increasingly, the ongoing debate has become a distraction for our game. We believe it is time for a circuit breaker.” Boon repeated that the forum is not intended to revisit the past in a legal sen

He added: “For almost a decade, the fallout from these events, or from those events, has remained part of the conversation around Australian cricket. It has been a difficult chapter for many people, and increasingly, the ongoing debate has become a distraction for our game. We believe it is time for a circuit breaker.” Boon repeated that the forum is not intended to revisit the past in a legal sense, and he closed with a call for unity. “This forum is not about re-litigating the past at all. It’s about creating an opportunity for those who wish to be heard to tell their stories in a respectful, safe environment, and for our sport to listen.” “Australian cricket is at its strongest when we’re united, and we owe it to everyone who loves the game to make every reasonable effort to move forward together with understanding, respect, and perspective.” Cricket Australia Interim Chair David Boon announced the establishment of a forum for players to discuss their sandpapergate experience. PRESSER ➡️ https://t.co/3LYlghFwsz https://t.co/aHaKPGuoKL — Telegraph Sport (@telegraph_sport) November 18, 2026 Is Cricket Australia re-opening the Sandpapergate investigation? Greenberg’s answer The short answer from the board is no. Greenberg confirmed that the original 2018 investigation will neither be reopened nor made public, with confidentiality given as the reason. Greenberg said the game is hurting right now, and then spoke about the need to recover. “It’s not good for anyone. We need to find a path through, and we need some time to heal.” He also made clear what the new process is and is not meant to do, and he repeated that taking part is a personal choice. He said: “As part of this process, and so that all parties who wish to can tell their version of events, we have set up now an independent forum. It’s a chance to give everyone a voice in an independent and a safe setting. It’s not a re-investigation. It’s not designed to re-prosecute or to sanction.” “No one is compelled to participate. It is entirely up to each individual. It’s important to remember we’re talking about events that happened eight and a half years ago, and I hope everyone will respect this process.” MORE: Warner accused CA of never interviewing bowlers in Sandpapergate probe, clarifies statement (Getty Images) Usman Khawaja and David Warner react to Cricket Australia’s Sandpapergate forum Khawaja welcomed the idea of a safe space but told Kayo Sports that he still has questions about the forum. He wants the public to hear the full story, and he believes that is impossible unless every person involved speaks. He said: “I have always wanted a safe space to chat… I also have some questions about Cricket Australia because the public wants to know what happened there. It’s hard to get the whole truth unless everyone is speaking.” MORE: Akram questions Australian bowlers' 'didn't know' defence in Sandpapergate He then said he does not want to see anyone punished, and he raised a concern about what the board will do with the material. He further asked: “I don’t think there should be any sanctions… the board makes the decisions but what comes out at the end? I have a really good relationship with Todd Greenberg, and I respect what he’s trying to do there. "But at the end of the day if you’re going to cherry-pick what is said in this report, the board can choose whatever they want to come in, or come out. Are we just going in a circle here? That’s the thing I’m not sure about.” Warner, who was speaking alongside Khawaja, also ruled out any desire for further penalties. He pointed to what the players accepted at the time and to what he sees as the real purpose of the forum. He said: “We put our hands up, we accepted what Cricket Australia handed out to us. It’s not about penalties. It’s about transparency and accountability - which Todd’s acknowledged, on CA’s behalf, about the culture at the time with the players and CA.” MORE: 'Tried eradicating it': Cummins admits Australia of 2018 had a 'win at all costs' mentality A forum without a published outcome may not settle the Sandpapergate debate The board’s intention is easy to understand, because nearly a decade of argument has simply worn people down. A confidential, voluntary forum offers a way for everyone to speak without the threat of sanctions, and that is a reasonable starting point. However, the same features that make the forum safe may also limit its value. Khawaja has already pointed out the central weakness: CA will decide what is released at the end. If the public sees only a short summary, those who want answers are likely to treat it as a polished version of events, and the debate will carry on. The voluntary nature of the process is a second problem. Cummins and Starc have strongly rejected Khawaja’s version, and if they choose not to take part, the forum will hear one side of the dispute far more than the other. A discussion with missing voices is unlikely to produce the shared understanding Boon hopes for. CA can improve its chances by publishing the terms of reference early, by naming a respected independent figure, and by being clear about what will be shared. The board has said it wants a circuit breaker, but a breaker only works if people trust it. That trust will depend on how openly the process is run. For all the latest cricket news, opinion,

item.title: Cincinnati schedules home-and-home with Missouri for 2027 and 2032
item.description: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 07: Cincinnati Bearcats football helmet rests on the visitors' sideline during the college football game between the Cincinnati Bearcats and Houston Cougars on November 7, 2026 at TDECU Stadium in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Leslie Plaza Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images While the 2026 regular season is in its twilight stages, some teams are already looking ahead to 2027. On Tuesday, Cincinnati and Missouri announced a home-and-home non-conference series. Missouri will host the Bearcats at Faurot Field on Sept. 18, 2027, while Cincinnati welcomes the Tigers to Nippert Stadium on Sept. 11, 2032. Although the campuses are separated by fewer than 500 miles, the 2027 matchup will mark the first-ever meeting between the Big 12 and SEC opponents. Cincinnati has now finalized its non-conference schedule for the 2027 season. The Bearcats will host Central Connecticut of the FCS on Aug. 28, remain at home against Missouri State on Sept. 4, and complete their non-conference slate at Missouri on Sept. 18. Cincinnati does not have a game scheduled for the weekend of Sept. 11, when it will either play its Big 12 opener or take a bye. Both Missouri and Cincinnati experienced recent cancelations in their 2027 non-conference slates, making them a perfect match for each other. The Tigers saw their 2027 home contest against Illinois get axed, while Cincinnati’s looming road trip to Boston College was also removed from the schedule. The Bearcats have won five consecutive regular season non-conference matchups, sweeping all three opponents during the 2026 season. The 2027 trip to Missouri will mark the program’s first true road non-conference game since Sept. 14, 2024 when it traveled to crosstown rival Miami (OH). Also, it will be the Bearcats’ first out-of-state non-conference road game since Sept. 9, 2023 at Pittsburgh and first SEC matchup since Sept. 3, 2022 at Arkansas. Cincinnati traditionally had one non-conference vacancy reserved for Miami, as the two competed in one of the longest running series in college football. The rivals played their 129th and final scheduled meeting this past September, making it the fourth-most played FBS matchup behind Minnesota-Wisconsin, Auburn-Georgia, and North Carolina-Virginia. Although an iconic rivalry has been shelved, the Bearcats can look forward to securing their first victory over SEC competition on Sept. 18, 2027 in Columbia.

(Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 30: Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors stands on the court during their game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on October 30, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The Golden State Warriors are struggling amid the absence of superstar guard Stephen Curry, who is recovering from a right oblique abdominal tear. Curry missed his second straight game on Monday as the Warriors suffered another blowout loss, this time against the New Orleans Pelicans. The Warriors will be without Curry until Thanksgiving, though it’s possible he could be sidelined for an even longer period, as per BasketNews. Stephen Curry Opens Up About Knee Injury Getty Steph Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors reacts after making a basket against the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on October 30, 2026 in San Francisco, California. Last season, Stephen Curry missed 39 games last season due to rest, minor issues and a major knee injury. Curry was out for 27 consecutive games after being diagnosed with patellofemoral pain syndrome in his right knee, more commonly known as runner’s knee. Speaking to ESPN’s Anthony Slater , Curry shared how painful the injury was and the setbacks he suffered during his adjustment and recovery from what was described as a chronic issue the two-time MVP will have to play with for the rest of his career. “Against Detroit, it took everything in me down there on the training table just to be like, ‘Oh, I can go out here tonight and play,'” Curry said. “And I was just faking it for the first whatever (25 minutes).” Getty Steph Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors warms up wearing a Golden State Valkyries before their preseason game at Chase Center on October 16, 2026 in San Francisco, California. The Warriors superstar tried to return after the All-Star break and even worked out with Sabrina Ionescu . However, “there were certain directions of movement and stuff that just didn’t work,” so his return was pushed back. Curry was supposed to scrimmage with the team in late March, but his right knee “felt worse than it had before.” He called it a “true setback,” though he managed to come back before the end of the regular season. The Warriors labored to make the NBA play-in tournament. They shocked the LA Clippers to have a shot at the No. 8 spot, but they were blown out by the Phoenix Suns . Steph Curry Hints About Future Getty Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors stands on the court during their game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on October 30, 2026 in San Francisco, California. In the same interview with ESPN’s Anthony Slater, Stephen Curry admitted that the two-year, $115 million extension he signed in the offseason could be his last. “I assumed that it would probably be one of, if not the last, contract I signed,” Curry said. “I’m not afraid to say it. But maybe I’ll surprise myself and want to keep going.” At the age of 38, Curry was playing at an MVP level before his oblique injury. And with the way the Warriors lost their first two games since the injury, they still need their superstar more than ever. item.title: Pochettino's USMNT swan song signals change
item.description: Nov 17, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino walks off the pitch after the victory over Haiti in a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal match at TQL Stadium. From the moment Mauricio Pochettino was announced as United States men’s national team head coach in September 2024, things felt different. It wasn’t his experience or his personality - although, both were certainly noteworthy. Instead, it was his name. His stature. His reputation. Suddenly, somehow, the United States - the perpetually overlooked, stigmatized name in the halls of global soccer - was dating the prom king. It was unexpected. It was surreal. And it was bound to be fleeting. Now, following a 2-0 victory against Haiti at TQL Stadium, in Cincinnati, the Mauricio Pochettino fairytale is officially over. After just two years in charge of the USMNT (and a whirlwind two years at that), Pochettino departs to take up the coveted / cursed position of Manchester United manager. It’s a change that’s as disappointing as it is unsurprising. Despite the misty-eyed soundbites over the last week in which he described the decision as “one of the toughest” of his career, Pochettino’s return to club football has felt inevitable. He made no bones about his wandering eye, always quick to profess his love for the Premier League while maintaining his London residence throughout his time with the USMNT. Even when his contract extension was announced this summer, the conditions of that deal made it abundantly clear that should an attractive suitor come calling, he would answer. Now, after years apart, he'll get to rekindle that romance. As Pochettino celebrated Christian Pulisic putting the U.S. ahead in the 25th minute with one of the most acrobatic goals of the attacker's career (a high-flying bicycle kick that cut the ball inside the far post), some of his personnel were already across the Atlantic, laying the groundwork for his upcoming rendezvous. Even if his couching staff was divided, Pochettino insisted that his focus was not. And with Julian Hall doubling the USMNT's lead in the 43rd minute, perhaps he wasn't lying. It’s rare that football managers exit on their own terms. Even rarer still when they finish out their tenure having already secured their next job. Likely rarest of all, is to go straight from a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final to the biggest derby in English football. Then again, little about Pochettino's tenure has been normal. To even appoint the Argentine, U.S. Soccer aimed higher, spent more, and was bolder than ever before. The mechanisms employed to secure his signature (including donations-as-salary from hedge-fund billionaire Ken Griffin) were as opportunistic as they were canny. Ultimately, they succeeded. But has Pochettino? If this window is anything to go by then the answer is emphatically yes . Eight goals, zero conceded, across two competitive performances is beyond reproach. Exciting attacks, the promise of youth, undeniable
item.content:encoded: Nov 17, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino walks off the pitch after the victory over Haiti in a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal match at TQL Stadium. From the moment Mauricio Pochettino was announced as United States men’s national team head coach in September 2024, things felt different. It wasn’t his experience or his personality - although, both were certainly noteworthy. Instead, it was his name. His stature. His reputation. Suddenly, somehow, the United States - the perpetually overlooked, stigmatized name in the halls of global soccer - was dating the prom king. It was unexpected. It was surreal. And it was bound to be fleeting. Now, following a 2-0 victory against Haiti at TQL Stadium, in Cincinnati, the Mauricio Pochettino fairytale is officially over. After just two years in charge of the USMNT (and a whirlwind two years at that), Pochettino departs to take up the coveted / cursed position of Manchester United manager. It’s a change that’s as disappointing as it is unsurprising. Despite the misty-eyed soundbites over the last week in which he described the decision as “one of the toughest” of his career, Pochettino’s return to club football has felt inevitable. He made no bones about his wandering eye, always quick to profess his love for the Premier League while maintaining his London residence throughout his time with the USMNT. Even when his contract extension was announced this summer, the conditions of that deal made it abundantly clear that should an attractive suitor come calling, he would answer. Now, after years apart, he'll get to rekindle that romance. As Pochettino celebrated Christian Pulisic putting the U.S. ahead in the 25th minute with one of the most acrobatic goals of the attacker's career (a high-flying bicycle kick that cut the ball inside the far post), some of his personnel were already across the Atlantic, laying the groundwork for his upcoming rendezvous. Even if his couching staff was divided, Pochettino insisted that his focus was not. And with Julian Hall doubling the USMNT's lead in the 43rd minute, perhaps he wasn't lying. It’s rare that football managers exit on their own terms. Even rarer still when they finish out their tenure having already secured their next job. Likely rarest of all, is to go straight from a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final to the biggest derby in English football. Then again, little about Pochettino's tenure has been normal. To even appoint the Argentine, U.S. Soccer aimed higher, spent more, and was bolder than ever before. The mechanisms employed to secure his signature (including donations-as-salary from hedge-fund billionaire Ken Griffin) were as opportunistic as they were canny. Ultimately, they succeeded. But has Pochettino? If this window is anything to go by then the answer is emphatically yes . Eight goals, zero conceded, across two competitive performances is beyond reproach. Exciting attacks, the promise of youth, undeniable tenacity - much of what fans hoped they would get from Pochettino's appointment was on display against Haiti. But stepping out of the moment, things become a little more complicated. Pochettino’s time as U.S. head coach saw no records broken and no trophies won. The USMNT's ranking is identical to when he took over while his win percentage is less than that of predecessor Gregg Berhalter. Meanwhile, his relationship with the players (Christian Pulisic, in particular) was at times tense, and his rapport with media and fans could even be patronizing. It was, however, also under his watch that 78 different players earned a cap, nine teenagers made debuts, and the USMNT put in one of their all-time great performances (Paraguay), World Cup or otherwise. Altogether, it's a portfolio that plays like a Rorschach test. Love him or hate him, you'll find stats to back you up. But stats aren't really where Pochettino's legacy lies. Indeed, what Pochettino left the U.S. with - and perhaps even the wider soccer world - was a shift in perception. The US can should think bigger. Our talent is plentiful. World Cups are winnable. How true these notions actually are remains to be seen, but what isn’t up for debate is who promoted them: Mauricio Pochettino. USMNT head coach Muaricio Pochettino. The sheer reality of that fact makes any future fantasies just a little more plausible. It's something that even Pochettino seemed to recognize. “Being head coach in USA now is prestigious,” he said. Self-aggrandizing, sure, but also true - even if only symbolically. And this, more than anything, is Pochettino’s great success. Two years ago, the thought of a top-tier, globally in-demand manager taking over the United States men's national team was unthinkable. International football simply wasn't a jewel in the managerial crown - let alone a program as disparaged as the U.S. But one Pochettino later, and the narrative has changed. Now, some of the biggest names in soccer (Tuchel, Carlo, Klopp) find themselves helming national teams (England, Brazil, Germany, respectively) while arguably the biggest name is rumored to be intrigued by the prospect of taking over the USMNT. The likelihood of Pep Guardiola becoming the next United States head coach is slim, at best. But what's remarkable is that it's no longer laughable. This is a massive country, with tremendous resources, and enormous potential. The scale and scope of a USMNT "project”, combined with the prospect of unleashing a sleeping giant, might actually entice a name as big as Pep (see Man City). Still, in the immediate context of Haiti and a Nation's League quarter final, it's a prospect that's hard to reconcile, and, ultimately, a reflection of the unique place that the U.S. now finds itself. A place where B.J. Callaghan is mentioned alongside Julian Nagelsmann. Where the self-deprecating backwaters of USMNT fandom have turned a little less dark. Where the once overlooked now get second glances. A place that was good enough for Mauricio Pochettino.

item.title: Oracle reveals fix-this-ASAP-grade Java4Shell bug that allows attacks on many third-party apps
item.description: The United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has urged Java users to immediately patch a high-severity flaw in the software, which attackers can use to crash the Java virtual machine or achieve unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). Oracle revealed the flaw in its monthly patch dump for November , which offers 655 patches, 62 of them rated critical, affecting 62 products. Several of the flaws are rated more dangerous than the Java problem, CVE-2026-114938 , which Big Red didn’t single out as worthy of special attention despite CISA’s warning . The cyber-agency’s decision seems apt because vulnerability research and red teaming outfit Calif.io, which discovered the flaw, used its X account to claim news of the problem had leaked before public disclosure and the release of Oracle's fixes. By then, Calif had already tested the flaw, which it named “Java4Shell,” and found applications including Keycloak, Atlassian’s Jira and Confluence, Jenkins, Apache Kafka Broker, and Elasticsearch are susceptible to RCE. Calif, which also helped to find the PHP2Shell flaw , says the flaw is a memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. “Base64 is a very common way of representing binary data as text. It is used in authentication protocols, to encode file uploads, and to deliver network messages,” the company explained. “To decode Base64 faster, OpenJDK uses specialized x86-64 CPU instructions to process many bytes at once.” “We discovered a bug in that optimized machine-level code that lets malformed input overwrite neighboring memory. With careful exploitation, the corruption can reveal sensitive memory, as Heartbleed did, or lead to remote code execution. The corruption itself can be triggered by just 64 A characters followed by a single =:” Calif applied the CVSS 4.0 bug-rating scheme and gave the flaw a critical-rated score of 9.2/10. Infosec outfit SentinelOne’s analysis suggests the flaw “sits in the Java standard library, so exploit traffic is specific to each application.” “Any Base64 value an application passes to java.util.Base64.Decoder can carry the payload, including HTTP Basic credentials, SAML artifacts, CSRF tokens, and MIME encoded words. In default configurations of the affected applications listed above, attackers can reach this code path prior to authentication.” Cisco’s Talos security team pointed out that the flaw is present in OpenJDK Java versions 17.0.6 and later running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions) support enabled. “These vulnerabilities have already been tested against a suite of Java applications with success, but the attack surface is likely much larger as additional targets are tested and confirmed,” Talos advised. Cisco’s infosec experts urged adoption of the fixed versions of Java Oracle posted on Tuesday but noted it is possible to mitigate the flaw on x86-64 machines by starting the JVM with support for AVX-512 disabled. In default configurations of the affected applications listed above, attackers can reach this code path prior to authentication.” Cisco’s Talos security team pointed out that the flaw is present in OpenJDK Java versions 17.0.6 and later running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions) support enabled. “These vulnerabilities have already been tested against a suite of Java applications with success, but the attack surface is likely much larger as additional targets are tested and confirmed,” Talos advised. Akamai’s Chief Information Security Architect Jan Schaumann, writing on the Openwall project’s mailing list , expressed a little discomfort with Calif’s work. “Calif.io set their priorities on publicity-maxxing, it seems,” he wrote, pointing out that the flaw-finding firm’s announcement of Java4Shell opens by stating “After we disclosed PHP2Shell, we realized many people didn't know what PHP was. So we decided to go after something a little more familiar: Java.” Talos’s analysis of Java4Shell includes the interesting observation that it “has not observed in-the-wild exploitation of this vulnerability yet. However, we anticipate probing attempts may pick up soon after public disclosure.” That second sentence perhaps supports Calif’s assertion that news of the flaw leaked before disclosure. The rest of Big Red’s flaws Java4Shell deserves a place high up on patch priority lists. So do the six 10.10 flaws Oracle reported, three in its Access Manager product, one in the Oracle Platform Security for Java, another in the WebLogic Server, and one in Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition. Big Red also repaired five 9.9-rated bugs, in Oracle Text, Hyperion, RDBMS, and Autovue. The November patch dump also includes 28 flaws rated 9.8/10. By Tenable Security’s count , 249 of the patches are for high severity bugs. Oracle’s Hyperion enterprise performance management accounts for 267 of the bugs. Such is life in the age of AI-powered flaw finders – which Calif says burned through just $200 worth of tokens to find Java4Shell. ®

item.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
item.description: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new "frontier ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. Read full article Comments

item.title: Daily disruptive outages that ground planes and halt work – welcome to the new normal
item.description: Another day, another disruptive network outage (or two) as government officials and company execs scramble to assure an anxious populace that these are not coordinated cyberattacks – and security experts call this the new normal. A classified network that the US National Security Agency uses for internal communications, called NSANet, went offline on Tuesday in what the agency described as a “temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance.” “While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues,” the NSA said in a statement following media reports about the outage. “NSA's infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.” Around the same time, Apple users began reporting issues across multiple services – including Apple Support, iCloud, the App Store, Apple Pay, and more – with Apple retail stores worldwide also reportedly experiencing disruptions that halted sales and in-person support. A day earlier, customers at major US banks including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and US Bank reported service outages that Chase attributed to “a software bug in on-premise hardware systems - there is no evidence this is cyber-related.” All of these high-profile outages followed last week’s US Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) order g rounding all planes on Friday due to problems with copper wiring during an L3Harris network upgrade, and a Microsoft 365 outage on Thursday. Redmond later blamed the massive service disruption on a faulty software update it pushed back in July. Despite the weekend respite from network outages, your humble vulture still had to field is-this-the-beginning-of-the-end questions from friends and family all day Saturday and Sunday, most of whom suspected Russia or China – maybe even Iran – caused the spate of downed systems and services. A highly sophisticated, coordinated nation-state hack would be a much more exciting cause for the disruptions. The real culprit, however, appears to be aging, under-funded infrastructure , riddled with decades-old bugs and held together by digital sticks and glue . “As someone who started out as a hacker , I know how tempting it is to connect the dots when major systems fail one after another,” Remedio CEO Tal Kollender told The Register, adding that there’s “no credible public evidence that these outages were part of a coordinated cyberattack,” and most have been attributed to technical failures. “What concerns me more is what these incidents reveal about the fragility of our digital infrastructure. item.dc:creator: Jessica Lyons
item.content:encoded: Another day, another disruptive network outage (or two) as government officials and company execs scramble to assure an anxious populace that these are not coordinated cyberattacks – and security experts call this the new normal. A classified network that the US National Security Agency uses for internal communications, called NSANet, went offline on Tuesday in what the agency described as a “temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance.” “While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues,” the NSA said in a statement following media reports about the outage. “NSA's infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.” Around the same time, Apple users began reporting issues across multiple services – including Apple Support, iCloud, the App Store, Apple Pay, and more – with Apple retail stores worldwide also reportedly experiencing disruptions that halted sales and in-person support. A day earlier, customers at major US banks including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and US Bank reported service outages that Chase attributed to “a software bug in on-premise hardware systems - there is no evidence this is cyber-related.” All of these high-profile outages followed last week’s US Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) order g rounding all planes on Friday due to problems with copper wiring during an L3Harris network upgrade, and a Microsoft 365 outage on Thursday. Redmond later blamed the massive service disruption on a faulty software update it pushed back in July. Despite the weekend respite from network outages, your humble vulture still had to field is-this-the-beginning-of-the-end questions from friends and family all day Saturday and Sunday, most of whom suspected Russia or China – maybe even Iran – caused the spate of downed systems and services. A highly sophisticated, coordinated nation-state hack would be a much more exciting cause for the disruptions. The real culprit, however, appears to be aging, under-funded infrastructure , riddled with decades-old bugs and held together by digital sticks and glue . “As someone who started out as a hacker , I know how tempting it is to connect the dots when major systems fail one after another,” Remedio CEO Tal Kollender told The Register, adding that there’s “no credible public evidence that these outages were part of a coordinated cyberattack,” and most have been attributed to technical failures. “What concerns me more is what these incidents reveal about the fragility of our digital infrastructure. We've built an interconnected world on layers of aging systems, complex configurations, and dependencies that organizations don't always fully understand. A single misconfiguration, failed update, or broken dependency can create disruption on a massive scale, even without an attacker,” Kollender said. “The uncomfortable reality I think we're grappling with is that attackers don't always have to break our systems. Sometimes, our systems are already capable of breaking on their own.” For people who couldn’t withdraw money from their bank, board a flight, or use email at work on Friday, “the disruption was real regardless of the cause,” she said. “Cybersecurity has spent decades investing in detecting threats, identifying vulnerabilities, and generating reports,” according to Kollender. “Yet we still allow for these preventable weaknesses and configurations that can bring entire systems down.” Cynthia Kaiser, senior VP of Halcyon’s Ransomware Research Center and former deputy director of the FBI’s Cyber Division, told The Reg that the recent disruptions show “how deeply interconnected our digital infrastructure has become, and how a single technical failure or software update can cascade with outsized effects across critical systems.” AI has entered the chat Then we go and add AI to this already delicate balance, and everything essentially blows up. AI-assisted bug hunting and exploit development has surfaced more than 100,000 CVEs so far this year, with Microsoft’s Patch Tuesday disclosing more than 1,000 vulnerabilities in each of the past two months. AI has also shrunk the elapsed time between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits . “We are in an era where AI is accelerating the discovery of legacy software flaws, forcing organizations to race to patch vulnerabilities before adversaries can exploit them, which inevitably creates friction and disruptions,” Kaiser said. “Even when an outage isn’t caused by a cyberattack, these moments of operational distraction leave dangerous gaps open for threat actors and opportunists to take advantage of, making it crucial for both institutions and everyday individuals to remain on high alert against social engineering and unsolicited outreach.” Even when attackers aren’t using AI to facilitate intrusions, the technology itself has become a source of risk to organizations. “Autonomous agents can execute actions, change configurations, access sensitive information, and interact with critical systems at machine speed,” Kollender said. “When those systems lack proper governance and safeguards, a mistake can develop just as quickly as an attack. Former US Department of Defense network exploitation and vulnerability analyst Mike Wiacek, when asked if these regular system outages are the new normal, told us: “The brutal truth is yes. Especially in the AI world that we live in.” After the DoD, Wiacek founded Google’s Threat Analysis Group. He's since founded Stairwell, a threat-intel firm he serves as chief technology officer. “The idea that we are going to patch ourselves to security is, dare I say, an antiquated concept,” he told The Register . One of Stairwell’s engineers was doing regular, daily software development tasks on an open source library with Anthropic’s Claude Mythos, and the model told the engineer about a buffer-overflow vulnerability in the code. “We weren't even looking for it,” Wiacek said. “It found a vulnerability in open source software by accident. You used to need specialized bug hunters and really, really technical security folks to discover and develop vulnerabilities and exploits. Now, it’s almost too easy to do it.” This new reality, he said, necessitates a total rethink of how we build and maintain digital infrastructure. “How do we get to a world where we assume compromised by default, and continuously recompromised, and then develop the architectures and the systems necessary to make what was the expense of incident-response investigation really fast and cheap? Because we will not be able to patch our way out of it.” It requires vulnerability managers and system administrators to patch as soon as software updates become available. But from an engineering perspective, it also means building in “as many fail-safes as possible,” Wiacek said. “An elevator doesn't have just one cable hoisting it,” he continued. “There's a lot of redundancy in those systems. Enterprises and organizations and governments haven't really had to operate like that. But that's going to be the new norm, whether we want it to be or not. Pandora's box is opened, and it's not going to go back inside.” ®

item.title: Nations League roundup: Devenny’s divine strike lifts Northern Ireland to top tier
item.description: Haaland’s late penalty grabs Norway last-eight spot Parrott penalties help Republic of Ireland secure playoff A wonder strike from Justin Devenny earned Northern Ireland top spot in Nations League Group B2 and promotion to the top tier of the competition. The Stoke player fired home on the volley from the edge of the area to earn a 1-1 draw away to Hungary , who would have leapfrogged Michael O’Neill’s side in the group with victory. Northern Ireland had fallen 1-0 behind after a 35th-minute goal from the striker Barnabas Varga, who slotted home when one-on-one with the goalkeeper Pierce Charles after a defensive mix-up. The goal ended Northern Ireland’s proud record of not having conceded in this campaign and also sent Hungary to the top of the group in the live standings. Continue reading...

item.title: Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang
item.description: Company issues first earnings report after ouster of CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spy Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday. Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster. Nvidia announced the same day that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago. The third-quarter earnings report comes just days after the world’s most valuable chip company saw the ouster of Huang over allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with his own employees. item.title: Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense
item.description: Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe's first true vertically integrated end-to-end space company. The announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio's shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo. Avio said its board of directors "has taken note of the notice" from ICEYE and is considering the purchase offer. Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. The Vega C has flown successfully seven times in eight attempts since 2022. It is a follow-on to an earlier version of the Vega rocket that amassed a 20-for-22 record since debuting in 2012. Read full article Comments

item.title: Jeff Bezos says he was ‘heavily involved’ in picking the new James Bond
item.description: Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond made enough sense given his recent work with director Denis Villeneuve, who's making the franchise's next film over at Amazon. But it turns out that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos played a significant role in making the final decision, too. During Semafor 's Silicon Valley and the World conference today, Bezos said that he was "heavily involved" in the process of casting the newest 007: We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday. There was a big group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists. Then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists, and it … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: GPU giants throw HPC users some tasty crumbs
item.description: At Supercomputing 2026 this week, Nvidia unveiled a new variant of its Rubin GPUs aimed at – you’ll never believe it – high performance computing (HPC). The creatively named Rubin HPC promises more than 50,000 CUDA cores, nearly twice that of the AI-focused version of the chip that Nvidia unveiled earlier this year. It will arrive sometime in 2028. According to Dan Ernst, Nvidia’s senior director of supercomputing, the new chip offers a rebalanced architecture optimized for the kinds of simulation, engineering, and high-performance analytics workloads common in the HPC and scientific computing communities. This is not the first time Nvidia has introduced specialized hardware. Last year, the company optimized its B300 accelerator for AI inferencing workloads. “Rubin HPC is the same idea,” Ernst told El Reg . “Within the Rubin platform, but we’re building variants to really focus on a specific sub domain of applications.” Details remain remarkably thin. Nvidia hasn’t disclosed peak performance memory capacity or bandwidth. That said, the chip will likely include features which show Nvidia can think beyond AI and still cares about the HPC community. Fearing that Nvidia could ignore HPC is reasonable becuase beginning with the launch of Blackwell Ultra (B300/GB300), the company traded double-precision matrix acceleration for higher throughput at lower-precisions. The result was a chip that at FP4 churned out 15 petaFLOPS of AI compute, but just 1.3 teraFLOPS at FP64. That's good for AI, but less useful for scientists. When Nvidia unveiled Rubin, it seemed the GPU-slinger would continue this trend. At 33 teraFLOPS, the chip was not only slower at FP64 than the Blackwell GPUs it replaced, but slower than Nvidia’s now four-year-old Hopper accelerators as well. Nvidia contended that for sparse vector-heavy workloads measured by the High Performance Conjugate Gradients (HPCG) benchmark, the higher ratio of memory bandwidth to compute should deliver meaningful performance gains. Meanwhile, for dense matrix-heavy workloads, for which benchmarks like High-Performance Linpack (HPL) are representative, Nvidia adopted a new strategy: FP64 emulation. We discussed the pros and cons of this technique in greater detail earlier this year, but in a nutshell it uses an algorithm derived from the so-called Ozaki Scheme. The algorithm works by decomposing FP64 matrix operations into a string of INT8 operations that, when run on Nvidia’s tensor cores, achieve higher-than-native performance. Nvidia, we’re told, isn’t using INT8, but it is unlocking substantial performance gains, at least for certain workloads. According to Nvidia, Rubin can churn out up to 200 emulated FP64 matrix teraFLOPS. While Ernst didn’t offer any specifics, he assured us that Nvidia’s HPC hardware should offer native FP64 matrix performance and customers won't have to rely entirely on emulation. item.dc:creator: Tobias Mann
item.content:encoded: At Supercomputing 2026 this week, Nvidia unveiled a new variant of its Rubin GPUs aimed at – you’ll never believe it – high performance computing (HPC). The creatively named Rubin HPC promises more than 50,000 CUDA cores, nearly twice that of the AI-focused version of the chip that Nvidia unveiled earlier this year. It will arrive sometime in 2028. According to Dan Ernst, Nvidia’s senior director of supercomputing, the new chip offers a rebalanced architecture optimized for the kinds of simulation, engineering, and high-performance analytics workloads common in the HPC and scientific computing communities. This is not the first time Nvidia has introduced specialized hardware. Last year, the company optimized its B300 accelerator for AI inferencing workloads. “Rubin HPC is the same idea,” Ernst told El Reg . “Within the Rubin platform, but we’re building variants to really focus on a specific sub domain of applications.” Details remain remarkably thin. Nvidia hasn’t disclosed peak performance memory capacity or bandwidth. That said, the chip will likely include features which show Nvidia can think beyond AI and still cares about the HPC community. Fearing that Nvidia could ignore HPC is reasonable becuase beginning with the launch of Blackwell Ultra (B300/GB300), the company traded double-precision matrix acceleration for higher throughput at lower-precisions. The result was a chip that at FP4 churned out 15 petaFLOPS of AI compute, but just 1.3 teraFLOPS at FP64. That's good for AI, but less useful for scientists. When Nvidia unveiled Rubin, it seemed the GPU-slinger would continue this trend. At 33 teraFLOPS, the chip was not only slower at FP64 than the Blackwell GPUs it replaced, but slower than Nvidia’s now four-year-old Hopper accelerators as well. Nvidia contended that for sparse vector-heavy workloads measured by the High Performance Conjugate Gradients (HPCG) benchmark, the higher ratio of memory bandwidth to compute should deliver meaningful performance gains. Meanwhile, for dense matrix-heavy workloads, for which benchmarks like High-Performance Linpack (HPL) are representative, Nvidia adopted a new strategy: FP64 emulation. We discussed the pros and cons of this technique in greater detail earlier this year, but in a nutshell it uses an algorithm derived from the so-called Ozaki Scheme. The algorithm works by decomposing FP64 matrix operations into a string of INT8 operations that, when run on Nvidia’s tensor cores, achieve higher-than-native performance. Nvidia, we’re told, isn’t using INT8, but it is unlocking substantial performance gains, at least for certain workloads. According to Nvidia, Rubin can churn out up to 200 emulated FP64 matrix teraFLOPS. While Ernst didn’t offer any specifics, he assured us that Nvidia’s HPC hardware should offer native FP64 matrix performance and customers won't have to rely entirely on emulation. Assessing the new chip's vector performance is much easier. With more than 50 thousand CUDA cores (by our calculation, it should be closer to 53,248), the chip should deliver at least 86 percent higher vector performance at double precision. AMD’s HPC beast AMD is also cooking up new HPC chips. In a blog post published late last week, AMD revealed the HPC-tuned version of its MI400-series GPUs. The Instinct MI430X boasts 432 GB of HBM4, 23 TB/s of memory bandwidth and a whopping 288 teraFLOPS of peak double precision grunt. AMD isn’t relying on FP64 emulation. Instead, AMD took advantage of its modular chiplet architecture to build two distinct versions of its MI400-series accelerators: one optimized for AI and another designed to excel in HPC and scientific computing workloads. AMD has shared predictions as to how the chips will perform in several of the Top500’s headline benchmarks. In a total non-surprise, the House of Zen says systems like EuroHPC’s Alice Recoque and Oak Ridge National Laboratories’ upcoming Discovery supers would enjoy significant performance gains if they upgrade from its earlier Instinct MI300A and MI250X-based offerings. ®

item.title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
item.description: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword. Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript. Read full article Comments

item.title: Apple outage: iPhone apps suffer disruption days after major Microsoft issues
item.description: Google’s Gmail also affected after problems reported in technological infrastructure in the US and worldwide Thousands reported disruptions to Google’s Gmail and Apple’s iPhone apps, such as Apple Pay and iCloud, on Tuesday, according to Downdetector . Apple confirmed the outages in a statement but said it had resolved them, while Google said it had not seen internal signs of outages. Apple’s own system status page as of 2.30pmET showed problems with services such as the App Store, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps and AppleCare. Continue reading...

item.title: Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied
item.description: One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese Football Federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards. For Wales, a Nations League relegation playoff double-header awaits in March, with Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia and Herzegovina – who knocked them out of World Cup qualifying this year – all potential opponents in Friday’s draw in Switzerland. Afterwards Craig Bellamy stressed the importance of keeping elite company to accelerate improvement but reiterated that he will not be in the job beyond Euro 2028, after which his contract expires. Continue reading...

item.title: NASA Launches Nuclear Power Systems Student Contest
item.description: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write a short essay about a “superpower” of their own. Submissions are due March 1, 2027. Every mission requires a power source. Some of the most interesting locations to study on our Moon face some of the harshest conditions. Nuclear power could sustain human life and allow researchers to study the resource-rich environment despite freezing temperatures, long nights, and deep craters that never see sunlight. “As NASA returns to the Moon and establishes a lunar base where astronauts will live, work, and explore, we need to build an infrastructure to make it all possible. Nuclear power could enable exploration in the permanently shadowed regions near the Moon’s South Pole, carry robust science payloads over long distances, and keep instruments warm through the lunar night,” said Carl Sandifer, a program manager for NASA’s Space Reactors Division at the agency’s headquarters in Washington. “NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge prepares the next generation of explorers to use the unique power within themselves to dream up a nuclear-powered Moon base of their own design. We cannot wait to see what they come up with!” Entries include a 200-word essay and an original illustration. Essays should describe one of the students’ unique powers that will help the mission. Illustrations should convey the students’ vision of a nuclear-powered lunar base that supports human and robotic exploration of the Moon’s surface using both radioisotope and fission-based power solutions and demonstrate the students’ understanding of the kinds of exploration nuclear energy can enable. Judges will review entries in three grade-level categories: K-4, 5-8, and 9-12. One grand prize winner from each grade category will receive a trip for two to NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland to learn about the people and technologies that enable NASA missions. Every student who submits an entry will receive a digital certificate and an invitation to a virtual event with NASA experts where they’ll learn about what energizes the NASA workforce to advance NASA’s missions and sustain America’s leadership in space. Judges Needed NASA and Future Engineers are seeking volunteers to help judge the thousands of contest entries anticipated from around the country. U.S. residents older than 18 who are interested in volunteering approximately three hours should register to judge at the Future Engineers website . item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
item.description: null Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer? It comes down to choices made for speed and science during the twin missions' nearly 50-year journey, specifically during the first bit when they were flying by planets. The result is Voyager 1 is zooming out at a speed of 3.5 Earth-sun distances (astronomical units a year), while Voyager 2 has a more stately speed of 3.1 Earth-sun distances, according to NASA . Need for speed The original aim of both the spacecraft, which launched about two weeks apart in 1977 with Voyager 2 going first, was to look at Jupiter and Saturn. If funding persisted, which it did, the hope was to bring Voyager 2 past Uranus and Neptune, taking advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Voyager 1, by contrast, made a turn at Saturn to look at the planet's rings and the prebiotic (pre-life-chemistry) moon of Titan , before flying outside the plane of the solar system. NASA had a range of trajectory options to consider when launching the spacecraft, and elected to bring Voyager 1 at a faster trajectory — as illustrated in this video by Britannica, where you can quickly see the spacecraft overtaking Voyager 2 on its way to Jupiter even though Voyager 1. Voyager 1 arrived at Jupiter on March 5, 1979 while Voyager 2 got there four months later on July 9. The trajectories of Voyager 1 and 2 through the outer solar system. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Each of the spacecraft then performed a "gravity assist"—a sort of slingshot around the planet in which they took a tiny bit of momentum from Jupiter to gain speed as the spacecraft flew to Saturn. This technique is used constantly, such as recently when the ESCAPADE Mars mission flew two spacecraft by Earth on the way to the Red Planet, as it allows spacecraft to gain speed while saving on fuel. The planets themselves don't slow down that much. "Because the planet is so much more massive than the spacecraft, the transfer doesn't affect the planet to any measurable extent, but to the spacecraft it's a big deal," the Planetary Society wrote . "For example, we can calculate that during the Voyager encounters with Jupiter in 1979, Jupiter slowed down by roughly 10 to the -24th power kilometers per second — a change much too small to measure."
